questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds undergo Aldol condensation followed by dehydration to give 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al?
questions.solution:
The target product is 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al, which is cinnamaldehyde. Its structure is $C_{6}H_{5}-CH=CH-CHO$.

The structure contains a phenyl group attached to a three-carbon chain with an aldehyde functional group at the end. This indicates that the condensation occurs between an aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde) and an aliphatic aldehyde (ethanal).

The reaction is a Claisen-Schmidt condensation, a type of crossed aldol condensation. Benzaldehyde ($C_{6}H_{5}CHO$) acts as the electrophile because it lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens, and ethanal ($CH_{3}CHO$) acts as the nucleophile because it possesses $\alpha$-hydrogens.

The reaction proceeds as follows: $C_{6}H_{5}CHO + CH_{3}CHO \xrightarrow{OH^{-}} C_{6}H_{5}CH(OH)CH_{2}CHO \xrightarrow{-H_{2}O} C_{6}H_{5}CH=CHCHO$.

Therefore, the reactants are benzaldehyde and ethanal.

Answer: Benzaldehyde and Ethanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the final product formed when Toluene undergoes a series of reactions with reagents given in the order:
(i) $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ / Sunlight
(ii) $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} / 373 \mathrm{~K}$
(iii) Acetophenone / $\mathrm{OH^-}$ at $293 \mathrm{~K}$
questions.solution:
Toluene reacts with $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ in the presence of sunlight to undergo free radical chlorination at the side chain, yielding benzal chloride, $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHCl}_2$.

Hydrolysis of benzal chloride with $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ at $373 \mathrm{~K}$ replaces the two chlorine atoms with an oxygen atom to form benzaldehyde, $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHO}$.

The reaction of benzaldehyde with acetophenone ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCH}_3$) in the presence of a base ($\mathrm{OH}^{-}$) is a Claisen-Schmidt condensation reaction. This reaction involves the nucleophilic attack of the enolate ion of acetophenone on the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde, followed by dehydration to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone.

The product formed is $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CHCOC}_6\mathrm{H}_5$, which is 1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one, commonly known as benzalacetophenone or chalcone.

Answer: 1, 3-Diphenylprop-2-en-1-one

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is/are the product/s formed when Benzaldehyde and Ethanal react in presence of dil. $\mathrm{NaOH}$ followed by heating the intermediate product formed?
questions.solution:
The reaction between Benzaldehyde ($C_{6}H_{5}CHO$) and Ethanal ($CH_{3}CHO$) in the presence of dilute $NaOH$ is a crossed aldol condensation. Since Benzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, it acts as the electrophile, while Ethanal acts as the nucleophile.

The initial aldol addition product is $C_{6}H_{5}CH(OH)CH_{2}CHO$ (3-hydroxy-3-phenylpropanal). Upon heating, this undergoes dehydration to form 3-phenylprop-2-enal (cinnamaldehyde).

Additionally, Ethanal can undergo self-aldol condensation in the presence of dilute $NaOH$ to form $CH_{3}CH(OH)CH_{2}CHO$ (3-hydroxybutanal). Upon heating, this dehydrates to form but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde).

Therefore, the products formed are 3-phenylprop-2-enal and but-2-enal.

Answer: 3-Phenylprop-2-enal & But-2-enal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given are the names of 4 compounds. Two of these compounds will not undergo Cannizzaro's reaction. Identify the two.
A. 2-Chlorobutanal
B. 2,2-Dimethylpropanal
C. Benzaldehyde
D. 2-Phenyl ethanol
questions.solution:
Cannizzaro reaction is a disproportionation reaction given by aldehydes that do not possess any $\alpha$-hydrogen atom. In the presence of a strong base, these aldehydes undergo self-oxidation and reduction to form a carboxylic acid salt and an alcohol.

Analyzing the given compounds:
A. 2-Chlorobutanal: The structure is $CH_3-CH_2-CHCl-CHO$. The carbon atom adjacent to the carbonyl group (the $\alpha$-carbon) has one hydrogen atom attached. Since it has an $\alpha$-hydrogen, it will undergo aldol condensation, not Cannizzaro reaction.

B. 2,2-Dimethylpropanal: The structure is $(CH_3)_3C-CHO$. The $\alpha$-carbon is bonded to three methyl groups and has no hydrogen atom attached. Therefore, it does not have an $\alpha$-hydrogen and will undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

C. Benzaldehyde: The structure is $C_6H_5-CHO$. The carbonyl carbon is attached directly to the benzene ring. There is no $\alpha$-hydrogen atom present. Therefore, it will undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

D. 2-Phenyl ethanol: The structure is $C_6H_5-CH_2-CH_2-OH$. This is a primary alcohol, not an aldehyde. Cannizzaro reaction is specific to aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens. Thus, it will not undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

The compounds that will not undergo Cannizzaro reaction are 2-Chlorobutanal (A) and 2-Phenyl ethanol (D).

Answer: A & D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect regarding acetal and ketal formation when Propanal and Propanone are separately reacted with Ethanol in presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ gas.
options: Rate of formation of acetal is greater than that of ketal formation.
Both Propanal and Propanone undergo Nucleophilic addition reaction during this process.
Propanal and Ethanol should be taken in the approximate ratio of $1: 2$ for acetal formation.
Anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ gas decreases the electrophilicity of the Carbonyl Carbon.
questions.solution:
Propanal is an aldehyde and Propanone is a ketone. Aldehydes are more reactive towards nucleophilic addition than ketones due to both steric and electronic factors. Thus, the rate of acetal formation from propanal is greater than the rate of ketal formation from propanone.

Both reactions involve the nucleophilic attack of ethanol on the carbonyl carbon, which is a nucleophilic addition reaction.

Acetal formation is a reversible reaction. To shift the equilibrium towards the product (acetal), an excess of alcohol is typically used, or water is removed. The stoichiometric ratio for the reaction $RCHO + 2R'OH \rightarrow RCH(OR')_2 + H_2O$ is $1:2$.

Anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ acts as an acid catalyst. It protonates the carbonyl oxygen, which increases the positive charge density on the carbonyl carbon, thereby increasing its electrophilicity and making it more susceptible to nucleophilic attack by ethanol. Therefore, the statement that $\mathrm{HCl}$ decreases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon is incorrect.

Answer: Anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ gas decreases the electrophilicity of the Carbonyl Carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A Carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ when reacted with Methyl magnesium bromide followed by hydrolysis gave product $\mathrm{Y}$. When $\mathrm{Y}$ is heated with $\mathrm{Cu}$ at $573 \mathrm{~K}$, it gave $\mathrm{Z}$ (2- Methylbut-2-ene) as one of the products. Identify $\mathrm{X}$.
questions.solution:
The reaction of a carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ with $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields an alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$.

Heating alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ with $\mathrm{Cu}$ at $573 \mathrm{~K}$ is a dehydrogenation reaction for primary and secondary alcohols, or a dehydration reaction for tertiary alcohols. Since the product $\mathrm{Z}$ is 2-methylbut-2-ene, which is an alkene, the reaction is a dehydration of a tertiary alcohol.

The structure of 2-methylbut-2-ene is $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

The tertiary alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ that dehydrates to form 2-methylbut-2-ene is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, which has the structure $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

The alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ (2-methylbutan-2-ol) is formed by the reaction of a ketone with methylmagnesium bromide. Specifically, the reaction of butan-2-one ($\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$) with $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields 2-methylbutan-2-ol.

Therefore, the carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ is butan-2-one.

Answer: Butanone

questions.q: Which one of the following compounds would not undergo Aldol condensation?
questions.solution:
Aldol condensation requires the presence of at least one $\alpha$-hydrogen atom in the carbonyl compound. An $\alpha$-hydrogen is a hydrogen atom attached to the carbon atom adjacent to the carbonyl group.

Analyzing the structures:

1. 2,2-Dimethylbutanal: The structure is $CH_3-CH_2-C(CH_3)_2-CHO$. The $\alpha$-carbon is the carbon atom attached to the aldehyde group. In this molecule, the $\alpha$-carbon is bonded to two methyl groups and the aldehyde group, meaning it has no hydrogen atoms attached to it. Thus, it lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens.

2. 2-Methylpentanal: The structure is $CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CHO$. The $\alpha$-carbon has one hydrogen atom attached.

3. 1-Phenylpropanone: The structure is $C_6H_5-CO-CH_2-CH_3$. The $\alpha$-carbon (the carbon of the ethyl group attached to the carbonyl) has two hydrogen atoms.

4. Phenyl ethanal: The structure is $C_6H_5-CH_2-CHO$. The $\alpha$-carbon has two hydrogen atoms.

Since 2,2-Dimethylbutanal has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, it cannot undergo Aldol condensation.

Answer: 2,2-Dimethyl butanal

questions.solution:
The reaction of pentan-2-one with NaCN/HCl is a cyanohydrin formation reaction. Pentan-2-one is $CH_3-C(=O)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$.

The nucleophilic addition of cyanide ion ($CN^{-}$) to the carbonyl carbon of pentan-2-one followed by protonation yields 2-hydroxy-2-methylpentanenitrile, which is the intermediate [X]. The structure of [X] is $CH_3-C(OH)(CN)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$.

The subsequent reaction of [X] with 95% $H_3PO_4$ at elevated temperature is a dehydration reaction. The hydroxyl group (-OH) is protonated to form a good leaving group ($-OH_2^{+}$), which then leaves to form a carbocation at the C2 position. This is followed by the elimination of a proton from an adjacent carbon to form a double bond, resulting in an unsaturated nitrile.

The most stable alkene formed is the one where the double bond is conjugated with the nitrile group, or the more substituted alkene. Dehydration of 2-hydroxy-2-methylpentanenitrile leads to the formation of 2-methylpent-2-enenitrile, which is $CH_3-C(CN)=CH-CH_2-CH_3$.

Comparing this structure with the given options, the structure $CH_3-C(CN)=CH-CH_2-CH_3$ corresponds to the first option.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What would be the products obtained when a mixture of p-Methoxy benzaldehyde and Methanal are heated with $50 \%$ concentrated Caustic soda solution?
options: p- Methoxy benzyl alcohol and methanol.
p- Methoxy sodium benzoate and sodium formate
p-Methoxy benzyl alcohol and sodium formate.
p- Methoxy sodium benzoate and sodium acetate.
questions.solution:
The reaction between p-Methoxybenzaldehyde and Methanal in the presence of concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide (50% NaOH) is a crossed Cannizzaro reaction.

In a crossed Cannizzaro reaction involving an aromatic aldehyde and formaldehyde, formaldehyde acts as the reducing agent because it is more reactive towards nucleophilic attack by the hydroxide ion ($OH^{-}$).

The mechanism involves the nucleophilic attack of $OH^{-}$ on the carbonyl carbon of formaldehyde to form a hydride donor species, which then transfers a hydride ion to the carbonyl carbon of p-Methoxybenzaldehyde.

Consequently, the formaldehyde is oxidized to sodium formate ($HCOONa$), and the p-Methoxybenzaldehyde is reduced to p-Methoxybenzyl alcohol ($CH_{3}OC_{6}H_{4}CH_{2}OH$).

The overall reaction is: $CH_{3}OC_{6}H_{4}CHO + HCHO + NaOH \rightarrow CH_{3}OC_{6}H_{4}CH_{2}OH + HCOONa$.

Answer: p-Methoxy benzyl alcohol and sodium formate.

Since a stable compound is specified, the $\beta$-hydroxy ketone undergoes dehydration to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone. The resulting $C=C$ extends conjugation with both the carbonyl group and the adjacent phenyl ring, providing significant resonance stabilisation.

The enolate ion of acetophenone attacks the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde to form a $\beta$-hydroxy ketone intermediate, which subsequently undergoes dehydration in the presence of the base and heat to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the final product formed when benzenamine reacts with the given reagents in the sequential order as:
i. (CH_3-$CO )_2$O / Pyridine. \\ ii. Conc. HNO_3$ + H_2$SO_4$ & then reacted with H_3$O$^+$ \\ iii. NaNO_2$ HCl (273K) & then reacted with H_3$PO_2$(aq).$
questions.solution:
Benzenamine (aniline) reacts with acetic anhydride in the presence of pyridine to form acetanilide. This step protects the amino group and prevents polysubstitution and oxidation.

Acetanilide undergoes nitration with a mixture of concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form $p$-nitroacetanilide as the major product due to steric hindrance at the ortho position.

Hydrolysis of $p$-nitroacetanilide with $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ removes the acetyl group, yielding $p$-nitroaniline.

$p$-Nitroaniline reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $273\text{ K}$ to form $p$-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride.

Reaction of the diazonium salt with aqueous $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ (hypophosphorous acid) reduces the diazonium group, replacing it with a hydrogen atom (deamination).

The final product formed is nitrobenzene.

Answer: Nitrobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: Aniline cannot be prepared by Phthalimide reaction
Propan–2–amine can be obtained by reacting acetoxime with Na / C_2$H_5$OH
The decreasing order of basic strength of amines in aqueous solution is Ethanamine > N,N–Dimethylaniline > Benzenamine
Fluorobenzene cannot be prepared from Benzenediazonium chloride by Sandmeyer's reaction because Fluorination of the Diazonium salt is highly endothermic in nature
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines. Aniline cannot be prepared by this method because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide. Statement A is correct.

Acetoxime is $(CH_3)_2C=NOH$. Reduction of acetoxime with $Na / C_2H_5OH$ yields propan-2-amine, $(CH_3)_2CHNH_2$. Statement B is correct.

Aliphatic amines are more basic than aromatic amines. Among aromatic amines, the $+I$ effect of two methyl groups in N,N-dimethylaniline increases the electron density on nitrogen, making it more basic than benzenamine. Thus, the basic strength order is Ethanamine > N,N-Dimethylaniline > Benzenamine. Statement C is correct.

Fluorobenzene cannot be prepared by Sandmeyer's reaction, but it is prepared by the Balz-Schiemann reaction. The reason it cannot be prepared by Sandmeyer's reaction is not because the fluorination of the diazonium salt is highly endothermic. In fact, direct fluorination is highly exothermic and violent, and $CuF$ is not effective for the Sandmeyer reaction. Therefore, the reason provided in statement D is incorrect.

Answer: Fluorobenzene cannot be prepared from Benzenediazonium chloride by Sandmeyer's reaction because Fluorination of the Diazonium salt is highly endothermic in nature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A Nitrogen containing organic compound with molecular formula C_3$H_5$N undergoes the following reactions.
C_3$H_5$N + Na / Hg in C_2$H_5$OH \rightarrow [A]
[A] + CH_3$COCl / NaOH (aq) \rightarrow [B] \\ [A] + CHCl_3$ / KOH on heating \rightarrow [C] (foul smelling compound)
Identify compounds [B] and [C]
questions.solution:
The molecular formula of the given organic compound is $C_3H_5N$. Its degree of unsaturation is $3 + 1 - \dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 2$.

The compound undergoes reduction to form [A], which reacts with $CHC$l_3$ and KOH to give a foul-smelling compound [C]. This is the carbylamine reaction, which is characteristic of primary amines. Thus, [A] is a primary amine.

Since [A] is a primary amine obtained by the reduction of a compound with degree of unsaturation 2, the original compound $C_3H_5N$ must be an alkyl cyanide (nitrile). Therefore, $C_3H_5N$ is propanenitrile, $CH_3-CH_2-CN$.

Reduction of propanenitrile with Na/Hg in $C_2H_5OH$ yields propan-1-amine:
$CH_3-CH_2-CN \xrightarrow{Na/Hg, C_2H_5OH} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH_2$ ([A])

Reaction of propan-1-amine [A] with acetyl chloride ($CH_3COCl$) in the presence of NaOH (aq) results in acetylation to form N-propylacetamide:
$CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH_2 + CH_3COCl \xrightarrow{NaOH} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH-COCH_3 + HCl$
Thus, [B] is $CH_3-(CH_2)_2-NH-COCH_3$.

Reaction of propan-1-amine [A] with $CHCl_3$ and KOH on heating yields propyl isocyanide, which is the foul-smelling compound:
$CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH \xrightarrow{\Delta} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O$
Thus, [C] is $CH_3-(CH_2)_2-NC$.

Answer: [B]: CH_3-$(CH_2$)_2-$NH$-$COCH_3$ [C]: CH_3-$(CH_2$)_2-$NC

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reagent used in carbylamine reaction is ----------------------- and the product of the reaction will be ---------------
questions.solution:
The carbylamine reaction is a characteristic test for primary amines (both aliphatic and aromatic).

When a primary amine is heated with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) and alcoholic potassium hydroxide ($\text{KOH}$), it forms an isocyanide (also known as carbylamine), which has a characteristic foul smell.

The general reaction is:
$R-\text{NH}_2 + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{KOH (alc.)} \xrightarrow{\Delta} R-\text{NC} + 3\text{KCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Thus, the reagent used is alcoholic $\text{KOH} + \text{CHCl}_3$ and the product is an isocyanide.

Answer: Alcoholic $\text{KOH} + \text{CHCl}_3$ ; isocyanide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct reaction of Hinsberg's reagent with primary, secondary and tertiary amines?
options: Tertiary amine forms N, N-dialkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is insoluble in alkali
Primary amine forms N-alkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali
Secondary amine forms N, N-dialkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali
Primary amine forms N, N-dialkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali
questions.solution:
Hinsberg's reagent is benzenesulphonyl chloride ($C_6H_5SO_2Cl$).

Primary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent to form N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide. The hydrogen attached to the nitrogen in the sulphonamide is strongly acidic due to the presence of the strong electron-withdrawing sulphonyl group. Hence, it is soluble in alkali.

Secondary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent to form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide. Since N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide does not contain any hydrogen atom attached to the nitrogen atom, it is not acidic and hence insoluble in alkali.

Tertiary amines do not react with Hinsberg's reagent to form sulphonamides.

Therefore, primary amine forms N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide which is soluble in alkali.

Answer: Primary amine forms N-alkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct order of the type of reactions taking place in this sequence:
questions.solution:
Nitrobenzene is converted to Aniline using $Sn/HCl$. This involves the removal of oxygen and addition of hydrogen, which is a Reduction reaction.

Aniline reacts with $NaNO_2/HCl$ (which forms $HNO_2$ in situ) to form Benzene Diazonium Chloride. The process of conversion of a primary aromatic amine into its diazonium salt is called Diazotization.

Benzene Diazonium Chloride reacts with another molecule of aniline in a mildly acidic medium to form $p$-amino Azobenzene. This is an electrophilic aromatic substitution where the diazonium ion acts as an electrophile. This specific type of reaction forming an azo dye is known as a Coupling reaction.

Therefore, the correct sequence of reactions is Reduction, Diazotization, Coupling.

Answer: Reduction, Diazotization, Coupling

Degree of unsaturation for $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ is $3 - \dfrac{9}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 = 0$.

The compound is a saturated aliphatic amine. It can exist as primary, secondary, or tertiary amines.

Primary amines ($1^{\circ}$):
1. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (Propan-1-amine)
2. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)\text{CH}_3$ (Propan-2-amine)

Secondary amines ($2^{\circ}$):

Tertiary amines ($3^{\circ}$):
4. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ (N,N-Dimethylmethanamine)

Total number of structural isomers is $4$.

Answer: $4$

Identify the name of the reaction involved in conversion of A→B and name the compound B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following compounds
ethanamine (i); diethylamine (ii); aniline (iii) and $N$ - methylbenzenamine (iv) The correct decreasing order of pKb values of the compounds is:
questions.solution:
The basicity of amines is inversely proportional to their $pK_b$ values. Higher basicity corresponds to a lower $pK_b$ value.

Comparing the basicity of the given compounds:
1. Diethylamine (ii) is a secondary aliphatic amine. It is the most basic due to the electron-donating inductive effect of two ethyl groups and favorable solvation.
2. Ethanamine (i) is a primary aliphatic amine. It is less basic than diethylamine due to fewer electron-donating groups.
3. $N$-methylbenzenamine (iv) is an aromatic amine where the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalized into the benzene ring, reducing its availability for protonation. However, the methyl group provides a slight electron-donating effect compared to aniline.
4. Aniline (iii) is a primary aromatic amine where the lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring. It is the least basic among the given compounds.

The order of basicity is: (ii) > (i) > (iv) > (iii).

Since $pK_b$ is inversely proportional to basicity, the decreasing order of $pK_b$ values is: (iii) > (iv) > (i) > (ii).

Answer: iii > iv > i > ii

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel's phthalimide synthesis?
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves the reaction of potassium phthalimide with an alkyl halide to form an N-alkyl phthalimide, which is subsequently hydrolyzed to yield a primary amine.

The reaction proceeds via an $S_N2$ mechanism. Therefore, the alkyl halide used must be a primary or secondary alkyl halide. Tertiary alkyl halides undergo elimination reactions instead of substitution, and aryl halides do not undergo $S_N2$ reactions with the phthalimide anion.

Analyzing the options:
1. 2-phenylethylamine is a primary amine and can be prepared from 2-phenylethyl chloride.
2. n-propylamine is a primary amine and can be prepared from n-propyl chloride.
3. N-methylbenzylamine is a secondary amine. Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is specifically used for the preparation of primary amines only. It cannot be used to prepare secondary or tertiary amines because the phthalimide anion is a bulky nucleophile and the resulting N-alkyl phthalimide does not allow for further alkylation to form secondary amines.
4. Isobutyl amine is a primary amine and can be prepared from isobutyl chloride.

Thus, N-methylbenzylamine cannot be prepared by this method.

Answer: N-methylbenzylamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The major product ' $D$ ' of the following reaction is:
questions.solution:
The starting material is nitrobenzene. Nitrobenzene undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with $Cl_{2}/AlCl_{3}$. Since the $-NO_{2}$ group is meta-directing, the chlorine atom enters the meta position, forming A, which is 1-chloro-3-nitrobenzene.

In the next step, A (1-chloro-3-nitrobenzene) is treated with $Zn/HCl$, which is a reducing agent. This reduces the nitro group ($-NO_{2}$) to an amino group ($-NH_{2}$), resulting in B, which is 3-chloroaniline.

Next, B (3-chloroaniline) is treated with $HNO_{2}$ at $0-5^{\circ}C$. This is a diazotization reaction, which converts the amino group into a diazonium salt, forming C, which is 3-chlorobenzenediazonium chloride.

Finally, C (3-chlorobenzenediazonium chloride) is treated with $Cu_{2}Br_{2}$ (or $CuBr/HBr$), which is a Sandmeyer reaction. This replaces the diazonium group ($-N_{2}^{+}Cl^{-}$) with a bromine atom, resulting in D, which is 1-bromo-3-chlorobenzene.

Answer: 1-bromo-3-chlorobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the correct statement:
options: Anilinium ion is less resonance stabilised than Aniline.
Aliphatic amines are weaker bases than $\mathrm{NH}_3$ while aromatic amines are stronger bases than $\mathrm{NH}_3$.
Sec-butylamine is optically inactive because Nitrogen atom of the $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group is achiral.
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for preparing both Ethyl amine and Aniline.
questions.solution:
(1) Correct: In aniline ($C_6H_5NH_2$), the lone pair on N is delocalized into the benzene ring, forming multiple resonance structures. In the anilinium ion ($C_6H_5NH_3^+$), the lone pair is donated to a proton and can no longer participate in resonance. Hence anilinium ion is less resonance stabilised than aniline.

(2) Incorrect: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than $NH_3$ due to the $+I$ effect of alkyl groups. Aromatic amines are weaker bases than $NH_3$ because their lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring.

(3) Incorrect: sec-Butylamine ($CH_3CH_2CH(NH_2)CH_3$) has a chiral carbon bonded to four different groups ($-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH_2CH_3$, $-NH_2$), making it optically active.

(4) Incorrect: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves $S_N2$ reaction with alkyl halides. Aryl halides do not undergo $S_N2$, so aniline cannot be prepared by this method.

The correct statement is (1).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound $\mathrm{A}\left(\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_9 \mathrm{~N}\right)$ upon reaction with $\mathrm{Na} / \mathrm{Hg} / \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{OH}$ gives compound B . B reacts with $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}$ at 274 K to form C with quantitative liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2$ gas. B also reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to form a compound which is soluble in alkali. Identify compound B.
questions.solution:
Two key reactions of B:

1. Reacts with $NaNO_2/HCl$ at 274 K to liberate $N_2$ quantitatively \Rightarrow characteristic of a primary aliphatic amine ($R-NH_2 + HNO_2 \rightarrow R-OH + N_2\uparrow + H_2O$)

2. Reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to form a product soluble in alkali \Rightarrow confirms primary amine (secondary amines give alkali-insoluble product; tertiary amines do not react).

Among the options, only option (3) $CH_3-(CH_2)_4-NH_2$ is a primary amine. Options (1) and (2) are tertiary and secondary amines respectively, and option (4) is a quaternary ammonium ion.

B is $CH_3-(CH_2)_4-NH_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Complete the following 2 reactions A & B by choosing appropriate reactants \([\mathrm{X}]\) & \([\mathrm{Y}]\).
questions.solution:
The reactions shown are electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions, specifically diazo coupling reactions between a diazonium salt and an activated aromatic ring.

In reaction A, benzenediazonium chloride reacts with [X] to form p-hydroxyazobenzene. This is a coupling reaction with phenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) in an alkaline medium (indicated by $\text{OH}^{-}$). The phenol acts as the nucleophile, attacking the diazonium cation at the para position.

In reaction B, benzenediazonium chloride reacts with [Y] to form p-dimethylaminoazobenzene. This is a coupling reaction with N,N-dimethylaniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2$) in an acidic medium (indicated by $\text{H}^{+}$). The dimethylamino group activates the benzene ring towards electrophilic substitution at the para position.

Comparing these with the given options, [X] corresponds to $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ and [Y] corresponds to $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.

Answer: $[\mathrm{X}] = \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH} \quad [\mathrm{Y}] = \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An optically active compound $[\mathrm{X}]$ (Molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_8 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{~N}$ ) reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ / Ethanolic KOH on heating to form an isocyanide. On reaction with $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}$, it yields an alcohol with liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2$. Identify the compound $[\mathrm{X}]$.
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_8 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{N}$ corresponds to a degree of unsaturation of $8 - \dfrac{11}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 = 4$. This indicates the presence of a benzene ring.

The reaction with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3 / \mathrm{KOH}$ (carbylamine test) indicates that $[\mathrm{X}]$ is a primary amine. The reaction with $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}$ yielding an alcohol with the liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2$ is characteristic of aliphatic primary amines, as aromatic primary amines form diazonium salts which are stable at low temperatures.

Among the options, 1-phenylethanamine ($\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2) \mathrm{CH}_3$) is a primary amine where the amino group is attached to an aliphatic carbon. It contains a chiral center at the carbon atom attached to the amino group, making it optically active. The other options are aromatic amines (anilines), which do not form alcohols under these conditions but rather form stable diazonium salts at $0-5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.

Therefore, 1-phenylethanamine satisfies all the given conditions.

Answer: 1-Phenylethanamine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, one Assertion and the other Reason are given. Identify the correct option

Assertion: Primary and secondary amides on treatment with $\mathrm{Br}_2$ and alcoholic NaOH yield primary and secondary amines respectively and the reaction involves stepping down the series.

Reason: The reaction occurs due to the migration of alkyl group from Carbonyl carbon atom to the Nitrogen atom with elimination of carbonyl group as the carbonate salt.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
The reaction described is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction. In this reaction, a primary amide ($RCONH_2$) reacts with $Br_2$ and a strong base (like $NaOH$ or $KOH$) to form a primary amine ($RNH_2$) with one carbon atom less than the original amide. This is a well-known method for stepping down the carbon chain.

Secondary amides ($RCONHR'$) do not undergo the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction to yield secondary amines. The reaction is specific to primary amides because it requires two hydrogen atoms on the nitrogen atom to form the intermediate isocyanate ($RNCO$) via the migration of the alkyl group. Therefore, the assertion that secondary amides undergo this reaction is incorrect.

The mechanism of the Hofmann bromamide degradation involves the formation of an N-bromamide intermediate, followed by the abstraction of a proton to form an anion, which then undergoes rearrangement. During this rearrangement, the alkyl group migrates from the carbonyl carbon to the nitrogen atom, leading to the formation of an isocyanate ($RNCO$), which is subsequently hydrolyzed to the primary amine and carbonate. Thus, the reason correctly describes the mechanism of the reaction for primary amides.

Answer: Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the correct statement from the options given
options: Benzene diazonium chloride when reacted with Aniline in presence of dil. HCl at 273 K yields \(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H} 5-\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5\)
On heating an aliphatic primary amine with \(\mathrm{CHCl}_3\) in presence of Ethanolic KOH, a Nitrile is formed
The intermolecular bonding in primary amines is stronger than in secondary amines.
The decreasing order of basic nature of the following amines is: Methylamine \( \gt \) Dimethylamine \( \gt \) Trimethylamine \( \gt \) Aniline.
questions.solution:
(1) Incorrect: Coupling of benzene diazonium chloride with aniline yields p-aminoazobenzene ($H_2N-C_6H_4-N=N-C_6H_5$), not the diazoaminobenzene structure shown.

(2) Incorrect: Heating a primary amine with $CHCl_3$ and ethanolic KOH (carbylamine test) yields an isocyanide (carbylamine), not a nitrile.

(3) Correct: Primary amines (R-$NH_2$) have two N-H bonds, enabling a more extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding network. Secondary amines ($R_2NH$) have only one N-H bond, resulting in weaker intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

(4) Incorrect: The correct decreasing order of basic strength in aqueous solution is: Dimethylamine ($2°$) > Methylamine ($1°$) > Trimethylamine ($3°$) > Aniline.

The correct statement is (3).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An organic compound $[\mathrm{X}]$ (molecular formula- $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{NO}$ when reacted with $\mathrm{Br}_2 /$ aq. NaOH yielded [Y] which reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ and Ethanolic KOH to produce a foul smelling compound.
Compound $[\mathrm{Y}]$ also reacts with HONO to produce Butan-1-ol with liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{~g})$. Identify [X].
questions.solution:
The reaction of compound [X] with $\mathrm{Br}_2 / \mathrm{aq. NaOH}$ is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction, which converts an amide ($\mathrm{R-CONH}_2$) into a primary amine ($\mathrm{R-NH}_2$).

The product [Y] reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ and ethanolic $\mathrm{KOH}$ to produce a foul-smelling compound (isocyanide test), confirming that [Y] is a primary aliphatic amine.

The reaction of [Y] with $\mathrm{HONO}$ (nitrous acid) produces Butan-1-ol with the liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2$ gas. This indicates that the amine [Y] is Butan-1-amine, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$.

Since the Hofmann bromamide degradation results in the loss of the carbonyl carbon atom, the original amide [X] must have one more carbon atom than the amine [Y]. Thus, [X] is a pentanamide with the formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{11}\mathrm{NO}$.

The structure of the amide corresponding to Butan-1-amine is $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CONH}_2$.

Answer: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\left(\mathrm{CH}_2\right)_3-\mathrm{CONH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{N}$ on hydrolysis gives compound '$\mathrm{X}$' which on treatment with $\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \mathrm{P}$ gives compound '$\mathrm{Y}$'. Compound '$\mathrm{Y}$' on reaction with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ gives '$\mathrm{Z}$'. The compound '$\mathrm{Z}$' is :
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{N}$ corresponds to propionitrile ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CN}$).

Hydrolysis of propionitrile ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CN} + 2\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{NH}_3$) yields propanoic acid as compound '$\mathrm{X}$'.

Treatment of propanoic acid with $\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \mathrm{P}$ is the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction, which results in $\alpha$-chlorination: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{P}} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHClCOOH}$ (2-chloropropanoic acid) as compound '$\mathrm{Y}$'.

Reaction of 2-chloropropanoic acid with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ involves nucleophilic substitution of the chlorine atom by the amino group: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHClCOOH} + 2\mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)\mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$.

The product '$\mathrm{Z}$' is 2-aminopropanoic acid (alanine).

Answer: 2-aminopropanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following amines in the decreasing order of their solubilities in water.
questions.solution:
The solubility of amines in water depends on their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules. Amines with lower molecular weight and fewer hydrophobic alkyl groups are generally more soluble.

Compound [I] is aniline ($C_6H_5NH_2$), which contains a large hydrophobic phenyl group. This large hydrocarbon part significantly reduces its solubility in water.

Compound [II] is ethylamine ($CH_3CH_2NH_2$), a primary amine with a small alkyl group. It can form effective hydrogen bonds with water and has a smaller hydrophobic part compared to [I] and [III].

Compound [III] is diethylamine ($(CH_3CH_2)_2NH$), a secondary amine. Although it can form hydrogen bonds, it has two ethyl groups, making it more hydrophobic than ethylamine [II].

Comparing the hydrophobic character: The phenyl group in [I] is the most hydrophobic, followed by the two ethyl groups in [III], and then the single ethyl group in [II].

Therefore, the decreasing order of solubility is ethylamine [II] > diethylamine [III] > aniline [I].

Answer: II > III > I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 4-methyl benzamide (A) on reaction with ethanolic solution of $\mathrm{KOH}$ and bromine gives another compound (B). The compound (B) on treatment with benzoyl chloride gives compound (C). Identify the correct structure of compound (C) from the following.
questions.solution:
The reaction of 4-methylbenzamide with $Br_{2}$ and ethanolic $KOH$ is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction. This reaction converts an amide ($R-CONH_{2}$) into a primary amine ($R-NH_{2}$) with one less carbon atom.

Starting with 4-methylbenzamide ($CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-CONH_{2}$), the Hofmann bromamide degradation yields 4-methylaniline ($p$-toluidine), which is $CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-NH_{2}$. This is compound (B).

Compound (B), 4-methylaniline, then reacts with benzoyl chloride ($C_{6}H_{5}-COCl$) in the presence of a base (like pyridine or aqueous $NaOH$) to form an amide through a nucleophilic acyl substitution reaction. This is the Schotten-Baumann reaction.

The reaction is: $CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-NH_{2} + C_{6}H_{5}-COCl \rightarrow CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-NH-CO-C_{6}H_{5} + HCl$.

The resulting product (C) is $N$-(4-methylphenyl)benzamide, which corresponds to the structure where the nitrogen atom is attached to the 4-methylphenyl group and the carbonyl group of the benzoyl moiety. This matches the first structure provided in the options.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: One of the reactions A, B, C, D given below yields a product which will not answer Hinsberg's test when reacted with Benzene sulphonyl chloride. Identify the reaction.
questions.solution:
Hinsberg test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary amines. Benzene sulphonyl chloride ($C_{6}H_{5}SO_{2}Cl$) reacts with primary and secondary amines to form sulfonamides. Primary amines form N-alkylbenzenesulfonamides which are soluble in alkali, while secondary amines form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulfonamides which are insoluble in alkali. Tertiary amines do not react with benzene sulphonyl chloride because they lack an acidic hydrogen atom on the nitrogen.

Reaction [A]: Benzamide ($C_{6}H_{5}CONH_{2}$) reacts with $LiAlH_{4}$ to form benzylamine ($C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), which is a primary amine and gives a positive Hinsberg test.

Reaction [B]: $p$-Nitrobenzonitrile ($NO_{2}-C_{6}H_{4}-CN$) reacts with $Na/Hg$ in $C_{2}H_{5}OH$ (Bouveault-Blanc reduction conditions) to reduce the nitrile group to a primary amine ($CH_{2}NH_{2}$), which gives a positive Hinsberg test.

Reaction [C]: $m$-Tolunitrile ($CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-CN$) reacts with $H_{2}/Ni$ to form $m$-methylbenzylamine ($CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-CH_{2}NH_{2}$), which is a primary amine and gives a positive Hinsberg test.

Reaction [D]: Benzonitrile ($C_{6}H_{5}CN$) reacts with $SnCl_{2}/HCl$ followed by hydrolysis (Stephen reduction) to form benzaldehyde ($C_{6}H_{5}CHO$). Benzaldehyde is an aldehyde and does not contain an amino group, so it does not react with benzene sulphonyl chloride and thus will not answer the Hinsberg test.

Answer: D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound having molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{N}$, reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ in alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$, on heating, to form a compound with a foul smell. Identify the optically active isomer of the compound which also shows the above reaction.
questions.solution:
The reaction of a compound with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ and alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ to produce a foul-smelling substance (isocyanide) is the carbylamine test. This test is specific to primary amines ($R-NH_2$).

The molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{N}$ corresponds to a saturated primary amine. The possible primary amine isomers are:
1. Butan-1-amine: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$
2. Butan-2-amine: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)-\mathrm{CH}_3$
3. 2-Methylpropan-1-amine: $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$
4. 2-Methylpropan-2-amine: $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{NH}_2$

Among these, we check for optical activity. A molecule is optically active if it contains a chiral center (a carbon atom bonded to four different groups).

In Butan-2-amine, the carbon at position 2 is bonded to a methyl group, an ethyl group, a hydrogen atom, and an amino group. Since all four groups are distinct, this carbon is chiral. Therefore, Butan-2-amine is optically active.

Answer: Butan-2-amine

questions.q: Identify the final product formed when Benzamide undergoes the following reactions:

The reaction of benzamide with $Br_{2} / KOH$ is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction. This reaction converts a primary amide into a primary amine with one less carbon atom. Thus, benzamide ($C_{6}H_{5}CONH_{2}$) reacts to form aniline ($C_{6}H_{5}NH_{2}$), which is the product [X].

The subsequent reaction of aniline with acetic anhydride ($(CH_{3}CO)_{2}O$) in the presence of pyridine is an acetylation reaction. The amino group of aniline undergoes nucleophilic substitution with the acetic anhydride to form N-phenylacetamide, commonly known as acetanilide ($C_{6}H_{5}NHCOCH_{3}$), which is the final product [Y].

Answer: Acetanilide

questions.q: What is the final product formed when Toluene undergoes the following series of reactions?
questions.solution:
Toluene reacts with conc. $HNO_{3}$ and $H_{2}SO_{4}$ (nitrating mixture) to undergo electrophilic aromatic substitution. Since the methyl group is ortho/para directing, the major product [B] is p-nitrotoluene.

Reduction of p-nitrotoluene with $Fe/HCl$ converts the nitro group ($-NO_{2}$) into an amino group ($-NH_{2}$), yielding [C], which is p-toluidine (4-methylaniline).

Reaction of p-toluidine with acetic anhydride $(CH_{3}CO)_{2}O$ results in the acetylation of the amino group to form [D], which is 4-methylacetanilide.

Answer: 4-methylacetanilide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which one of the following shows the correct increasing order of basic nature of the given compounds?
A: Phenylmethanamine
B: N-Ethylethanamine
C:N, N-Dimethylaniline
D : N, N-Dimethylmethanamine
questions.solution:
The basicity of amines depends on the availability of the lone pair on the nitrogen atom. Electron-donating groups increase basicity, while electron-withdrawing groups or resonance delocalization decrease it.

Compound A is Phenylmethanamine ($C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), a primary amine where the lone pair is not delocalized into the ring, but the phenyl group exerts a weak inductive effect. It is more basic than aromatic amines but less basic than aliphatic amines.

Compound B is N-Ethylethanamine ($(C_{2}H_{5})_{2}NH$), a secondary aliphatic amine. Secondary aliphatic amines are generally the most basic due to the strong inductive effect of two alkyl groups and favorable solvation.

Compound C is N,N-Dimethylaniline ($C_{6}H_{5}N(CH_{3})_{2}$), a tertiary aromatic amine. The lone pair on the nitrogen is delocalized into the benzene ring, making it the least basic among the given compounds.

Compound D is N,N-Dimethylmethanamine ($(CH_{3})_{3}N$), a tertiary aliphatic amine. While it has three electron-donating methyl groups, its basicity is often lower than secondary amines due to steric hindrance and solvation effects in aqueous media.

Comparing the basicity: C (aromatic) < A (primary aliphatic/aromatic-like) < D (tertiary aliphatic) < B (secondary aliphatic).

Thus, the increasing order is C < A < D < B.

Answer: C < A < D < B

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Aniline undergoes reactions with reagents given in the order shown
(i) Aqueous $\mathrm{Br}_2$
(ii) $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl} / 0^0 \mathrm{C}$
(iii) Hypophosphorous acid
What is the product formed at the end of these reactions?
questions.solution:
Aniline reacts with aqueous $\text{Br}_2$ to form $2,4,6$-tribromoaniline as the major product due to the strong activating effect of the $-\text{NH}_2$ group.

The $2,4,6$-tribromoaniline then reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}$ at $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ to undergo diazotization, forming the corresponding diazonium salt, $2,4,6$-tribromobenzenediazonium chloride.

Finally, the reaction of the diazonium salt with hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) and water results in the reduction of the diazonium group to a hydrogen atom, yielding $1,3,5$-tribromobenzene as the final product.

Answer: $1,3,5$ - Tribromobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following will give a positive result when it is warmed with Chloroform and alcoholic solution of $\mathrm{KOH}$ ?
questions.solution:
The carbylamine reaction is a characteristic test for primary amines. When a primary amine is heated with chloroform ($CHCl_3$) and an alcoholic solution of potassium hydroxide ($KOH$), an isocyanide (carbylamine) is formed, which is characterized by an extremely foul smell.

The reaction is represented as: $R-NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH \rightarrow R-NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O$.

Analyzing the given options:
(1) p-Methylbenzylamine is a primary amine ($CH_3-C_6H_4-CH_2-NH_2$), so it will undergo the carbylamine reaction.
(2) N-Methyl-o-Methylaniline is a secondary amine ($CH_3-C_6H_4-NH-CH_3$), which does not give the carbylamine test.
(3) N-Methyl-p-Methylaniline is a secondary amine ($CH_3-C_6H_4-NH-CH_3$), which does not give the carbylamine test.
(4) N,N-Dimethylaniline is a tertiary amine ($C_6H_5-N(CH_3)_2$), which does not give the carbylamine test.

Therefore, only p-Methylbenzylamine gives a positive result.

Answer: p-Methylbenzylamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Select the strongest base from the given compounds:
[A] p- $\mathrm{NO}_2-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{NH}_2$
[B] $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$
[C] $\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{NO}_2-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{NH}_2$
[D] $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{NH}_2$
questions.solution:
The basicity of amines is determined by the availability of the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom for protonation.

In p-nitroaniline [A] and m-nitroaniline [C], the $-\mathrm{NO}_2$ group is a strong electron-withdrawing group (EWG) that decreases the electron density on the nitrogen atom through both inductive (-I) and resonance (-M) effects, significantly reducing basicity compared to aniline [D].

In aniline [D], the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom is in conjugation with the benzene ring, which decreases its availability for protonation.

In benzylamine [B], the $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group is attached to a $-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ group, which is attached to the benzene ring. The $-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ group acts as an insulator, preventing the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen from being delocalized into the benzene ring via resonance. Consequently, benzylamine behaves like an aliphatic amine and is significantly more basic than aniline and its derivatives.

Answer: [B]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rank the following compounds in order of increasing basicity.
questions.solution:
Compound 1: Aniline ($C_6H_5NH_2$) - lone pair on N delocalised into ring via resonance \to moderate basicity.

Compound 2: Benzylamine ($C_6H_5CH_2NH_2$) - $NH_2$ not directly attached to ring, no resonance with ring \to most basic among these.

Compound 3: 2-Nitroaniline - $-NO_2$ at ortho position withdraws electrons by both inductive and resonance effects, plus steric hindrance prevents coplanarity reducing basicity further \to less basic than aniline.

Compound 4: Benzamide ($C_6H_5CONH_2$) - lone pair on N delocalised into $C=O$ (amide resonance), making N least basic.

Increasing basicity: $4 \lt 3 \lt 1 \lt 2$. Answer: (2)

questions.solution:
The reaction of a nitrile ($R-CN$) with a Grignard reagent ($R'-MgX$) followed by acidic hydrolysis ($H_3O^{+}$) is a standard method for the synthesis of ketones.

The mechanism proceeds as follows:
1. The nucleophilic alkyl group ($CH_3^{-}$) from the Grignard reagent attacks the electrophilic carbon of the nitrile group ($-CN$).
2. This forms an imine salt intermediate: $Ar-C(CH_3)=N-MgBr$.
3. Subsequent acidic hydrolysis ($H_3O^{+}$) converts the imine intermediate into a ketone ($Ar-C(=O)CH_3$) and releases ammonia/ammonium salts.

In the given substrate, 3-methoxybenzonitrile, the nitrile group is attached to the benzene ring at the meta position relative to the methoxy group. The reaction with $CH_3MgBr$ followed by $H_3O^{+}$ replaces the $-CN$ group with a $-COCH_3$ group.

Therefore, the product is 3-methoxyacetophenone, which corresponds to the structure with a benzene ring having a $-COCH_3$ group and a $-OCH_3$ group at the meta position.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Gabriel's synthesis is used frequency for the preparation of which of the following?
questions.solution: Gabriel's phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare pure primary ($1°$) amines. Phthalimide is treated with KOH to form potassium phthalimide, which reacts with a primary alkyl halide via $S_N2$, followed by hydrolysis (or hydrazinolysis) to release the primary amine. This method avoids over-alkylation (formation of $2°$ and $3°$ amines) that occurs when $NH_3$ reacts directly with alkyl halides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is highly basic?
questions.solution:
The basicity of amines is determined by the availability of the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom for protonation.

In aniline, the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is involved in resonance with the benzene ring, which decreases its availability for protonation, making it weakly basic.

In diphenylamine, the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is involved in resonance with two benzene rings, which further decreases its availability compared to aniline, making it even less basic.

In triphenylamine, the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is involved in resonance with three benzene rings, making it extremely weakly basic or essentially non-basic.

In benzylamine ($C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is not involved in resonance with the benzene ring because the nitrogen is separated from the ring by a $CH_{2}$ group. The electron-donating inductive effect of the benzyl group increases the electron density on the nitrogen atom, making it significantly more basic than the aromatic amines listed.

Answer: Benzylamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is most stable?
questions.solution:
Stability of diazonium salts ($R-N_2^+X^-$) depends on the stability of the carbocation formed after loss of $N_2$.

$CH_2N_2^+X^-$ and $CH_3CH_2N_2^+X^-$: aliphatic \Rightarrow resulting carbocations are highly unstable. These decompose rapidly.

$C_6H_5CH_2N_2^+X^-$: benzyl carbocation is resonance stabilized, but still relatively reactive.

$C_6H_5N_2^+X^-$: the diazonium group is directly attached to the aromatic ring. The lone pair on the nitrogen delocalizes into the ring \Rightarrow the diazonium cation itself is resonance stabilized. This makes benzene diazonium salt the most stable, existing in solution at $0-5^\circ C$.

Correct option: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement.
options: Except Glycine and Tryptophan all the other naturally occurring Amino acids are optically active
Glucose gets oxidised to Gluconic acid with B$r_2$(aq) which indicates that the carbonyl group in it is an Aldehydic group
The "D" in D(+) –glucose represents the dextrorotatory nature of Glucose and (+) stands for its configuration
During denaturation of Proteins its 3- dimensional structure is destroyed because the primary, secondary and tertiary structures get destroyed due to rise in temperature
questions.solution:
Glycine is the only naturally occurring amino acid that is optically inactive because its $\alpha$-carbon is attached to two hydrogen atoms. Tryptophan is optically active. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

Bromine water is a mild oxidising agent that specifically oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids. The oxidation of glucose to gluconic acid by bromine water confirms the presence of an aldehydic group. Thus, the second statement is correct.

In D(+)-glucose, 'D' represents the relative configuration with respect to glyceraldehyde, while '(+)' represents the dextrorotatory nature of the molecule. Thus, the third statement is incorrect.

During the denaturation of proteins, the secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed due to the unfolding of the protein chain, but the primary structure (the sequence of amino acids) remains intact. Thus, the fourth statement is incorrect.

Answer: Glucose gets oxidised to Gluconic acid with B$r_2$(aq) which indicates that the carbonyl group in it is an Aldehydic group

questions.q: A small segment of a polypeptide gave on complete hydrolysis 3 molecules of alanine, 2 molecules of glycine and 3 molecules of cysteine. What is the number of peptide linkages in the segment of the polypeptide?
questions.solution:
Total number of amino acid molecules obtained on complete hydrolysis = $3 + 2 + 3 = 8$.

In a linear polypeptide chain, the number of peptide linkages is equal to the total number of amino acid residues minus one.

Number of peptide linkages = $8 - 1 = 7$.

Answer: $7$

questions.solution:
Vitamin $B_{12}$ is a water-soluble vitamin but it is stored in the liver and is not excreted easily from the body. Thus, A matches Y. \\ \\ Deficiency of Vitamin B_2$ (Riboflavin) causes cheilosis, which is the fissuring at the corners of the mouth and lips. Thus, B matches W.

Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble vitamins. Therefore, Vitamin E is fat-soluble. Thus, C matches Z.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The secondary structure of protein consists of:
options: A folding of the polypeptide chains which exists as fibrous and globular
Two or more polypeptide chains which exist as sub-units
A long polypeptide chain which exists $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet structure
A long chain of amino acids linked with each other in a specific sequence
questions.solution:
The primary structure of a protein refers to the specific sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide chain.

The secondary structure refers to the local folded structures that form within a polypeptide due to hydrogen bonding between the backbone amide and carbonyl groups. The most common types of secondary structures are the $\alpha$-helix and the $\beta$-pleated sheet.

The tertiary structure refers to the overall three-dimensional folding of the entire polypeptide chain, which gives rise to fibrous and globular shapes.

The quaternary structure refers to the arrangement of multiple polypeptide chains (sub-units) into a single functional protein complex.

Therefore, the secondary structure consists of a long polypeptide chain which exists as an $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet structure.

Answer: A long polypeptide chain which exists $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is an INCORRECT statement?
options: Polysaccharides are known as non-sugars as they are not sweet in taste
In monosaccharides, aldoses are reducing sugars while ketoses are non-reducing sugars
In D (+) Glucose, D represents the configuration similar to D-Glyceraldehyde
D (-) fructose forms a five membered ring known as furanose which is in analogy with the compound furan
questions.solution:
All monosaccharides, whether aldoses or ketoses, are reducing sugars. Ketoses such as fructose can reduce Tollens' and Fehling's reagents because they undergo isomerization to aldoses in the alkaline medium via an enediol intermediate. Thus, the statement that ketoses are non-reducing sugars is incorrect.

Polysaccharides are indeed called non-sugars because they are not sweet in taste.

The 'D' in D-(+)-Glucose indicates that the configuration at the highest numbered chiral carbon is the same as that of D-Glyceraldehyde.

D-(-)-Fructose exists as a five-membered cyclic structure called furanose, which is named by analogy to the heterocyclic compound furan.

Answer: In monosaccharides, aldoses are reducing sugars while ketoses are non-reducing sugars

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct match?
questions.solution:
DNA contains $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose sugar, whereas RNA contains $\beta$-D-ribose sugar.

RNA molecules (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) are directly responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.

Glucocorticoids are steroid hormones secreted by the adrenal cortex that regulate carbohydrate metabolism and stress responses, not hyperthyroidism.

Deficiency of Vitamin A causes night blindness and xerophthalmia, whereas deficiency of Vitamin B6 causes convulsions.

Therefore, the only correct match is RNA - Protein Synthesis.

Answer: RNA - Protein Synthesis

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A polysaccharide $[\mathrm{X}]$ represented as $\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{10} \mathrm{O}_5\right)$ n serves as a reserve carbohydrate in human beings. An enzyme Phosphorylase breaks it down to glucose when required. It is also found in yeast and fungi. What is $[\mathrm{X}]$ ?
questions.solution:
The polysaccharide represented by the formula $(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{10} \mathrm{O}_5)_n$ is a polymer of glucose. Among the given options, glycogen is the primary reserve carbohydrate in humans and animals, stored mainly in the liver and muscles. It is also known as animal starch and is found in yeast and fungi. Glycogen is broken down into glucose-1-phosphate by the enzyme glycogen phosphorylase during glycogenolysis to meet the body's energy requirements. Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide in plants, while starch and amylose are reserve carbohydrates in plants.

Answer: Glycogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statement/s about nucleic acids is/are correct?
i. The chirality of both DNA and RNA molecules is due to the L-sugar component.
ii. The complementary bases in DNA are adenine \& thymine and guanine \& cytosine.
iii. $\quad \beta$-D-glucopyranose is the sugar moiety present in the RNA molecule.
iv. RNA controls the synthesis of proteins.
questions.solution:
Statement (i) is incorrect because the chirality of DNA and RNA is due to the D-sugar component, specifically D-2-deoxyribose in DNA and D-ribose in RNA.

Statement (ii) is correct. In DNA, adenine (A) pairs with thymine (T) via two hydrogen bonds, and guanine (G) pairs with cytosine (C) via three hydrogen bonds.

Statement (iii) is incorrect. The sugar moiety in RNA is $\beta$-D-ribofuranose, not $\beta$-D-glucopyranose.

Statement (iv) is correct. RNA plays a central role in protein synthesis through the processes of transcription and translation.

Since statements (ii) and (iv) are correct, the correct option is (Vj2Fl).

Answer: (ii) and (iv)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which statement is incorrect about aminoacids?
options: $\alpha$-aminoacids are soluble in polar solvents like petroleum ether and benzene.
All aminoacids except glycine are optically active.
At isoelectric point, an aminoacid has the least solubility in water.
questions.solution:
Amino acids are polar compounds due to the presence of both amino and carboxyl groups, which exist as zwitterions in aqueous solutions. Because of their ionic nature, they are highly soluble in water but are insoluble in non-polar organic solvents like petroleum ether and benzene.

Methionine is indeed an essential amino acid, meaning it cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through diet.

Glycine is the simplest amino acid with the structure $NH_2-CH_2-COOH$. Since the $\alpha$-carbon is attached to two identical hydrogen atoms, it is achiral and thus optically inactive. All other naturally occurring $\alpha$-amino acids possess a chiral $\alpha$-carbon and are optically active.

At the isoelectric point, the net charge on the amino acid is zero. In this state, the electrostatic attractions between the zwitterions are maximized, and the interaction with water molecules is minimized, leading to the lowest solubility in water.

Therefore, the statement that $\alpha$-amino acids are soluble in non-polar solvents like petroleum ether and benzene is incorrect.

Answer: $\alpha$-aminoacids are soluble in polar solvents like petroleum ether and benzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct statement?
options: Fructose exists as a five membered ring named furanose.
Amylose is a water insoluble branched chain polymer of $\propto$-D-( - )-glucose.
Glucose gives Saccharic acid on reaction with $\mathrm{Br}_2$ water.
Cellulose is a branched chain polysaccharide having only $\propto$-D-glucose units.
questions.solution:
Fructose exists in a five-membered ring structure known as a furanose ring, which is formed by the intramolecular reaction between the carbonyl group at C-2 and the hydroxyl group at C-5. This statement is correct.

Amylose is a linear, water-soluble polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose units, not a branched chain polymer. Amylopectin is the branched component of starch.

Glucose reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ water to form gluconic acid, which is a monocarboxylic acid. Saccharic acid (glucaric acid) is formed by the oxidation of glucose with stronger oxidizing agents like concentrated nitric acid, which oxidizes both the aldehyde group and the primary alcohol group.

Cellulose is a linear, unbranched polysaccharide consisting of $\beta$-D-glucose units linked by $\beta$-1,4-glycosidic bonds, not $\alpha$-D-glucose units.

Answer: Fructose exists as a five membered ring named furanose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ and D with the appropriate functions given.
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline & \text { Column I } & & \text { Functions } \\ \hline \text { A } & \text { Oxidoreductase } & \text { P } & \text { Malfunctioning leads to Addison's disease. } \\ \hline \text { B } & \text { Phosphodiester bonds } & \text { Q } & \text { Regulates responses to external stimuli. } \\ \hline \text { C } & \text { Adrenal cortex } & \text { R } & \text { Catalyses glycolysis. } \\ \hline \text { D } & \text { Epinephrine. } & \text { S } & \text { Links nucleotides together. } \\ \hline \end{array}\)
questions.solution:
Oxidoreductases are enzymes that catalyze oxidation-reduction reactions. In the context of metabolic pathways like glycolysis, enzymes such as glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase act as oxidoreductases. Thus, A matches with R.

Phosphodiester bonds are the covalent linkages that connect the 3' carbon atom of one sugar molecule and the 5' carbon atom of another in the sugar-phosphate backbone of DNA and RNA. Thus, B matches with S.

The adrenal cortex is an endocrine gland that produces essential hormones like cortisol and aldosterone. Malfunctioning or deficiency of the adrenal cortex leads to Addison's disease. Thus, C matches with P.

Epinephrine, also known as adrenaline, is a hormone and neurotransmitter that prepares the body for fight-or-flight responses, effectively regulating responses to external stimuli. Thus, D matches with Q.

Combining these, we get A=R, B=S, C=P, D=Q.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Q}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Imagine a pentapeptide molecule having a total of one $-\text{SH}$, $-\text{CONH}_2$, $-\text{NH}_2$ group each and two $-\text{COOH}$ groups. If the pH is maintained at 13.2, what would be the total number of negative charges on the pentapeptide?
questions.solution:
At pH 13.2, groups with $pK_a \lt 13.2$ will be deprotonated.

Two $-COOH$ groups ($pK_a \approx 2-4$): both deprotonated $\to2 \times (-1) = -2$ charges

One $-SH$ group ($pK_a \approx 8.3$): deprotonated to $-S^-\to-1$ charge

One $-NH_2$ group ($pK_a$ of conjugate acid $\approx 9-10$): at pH 13.2, exists as neutral $-NH_2\to$ 0 charge

One $-CONH_2$ group: amide, non-ionizable \to 0 charge

Total negative charges $= 2 + 1 = 3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a water soluble vitamin?
questions.solution:
Vitamins are classified into two categories based on their solubility: fat-soluble and water-soluble.

Fat-soluble vitamins include Vitamin A, Vitamin D, Vitamin E, and Vitamin K. These are stored in the liver and adipose tissues.

Water-soluble vitamins include the B-complex group and Vitamin C. These vitamins are not stored in the body in significant amounts and must be replenished regularly through the diet.

Comparing the given options, Vitamin C is the only water-soluble vitamin listed.

Answer: Vitamin C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement.
options: Amylose is a branched chain polymer of $\alpha-\mathrm{D}-(+)$ - glucose units
Leucine and Tryptophan are classified as Essential amino acids
Curdling of milk is not a denaturation process
Fructose is an example of Invert sugar
questions.solution:
Amylose is a linear polymer of $\alpha$-D-(+)-glucose units linked by $\alpha$-1,4-glycosidic bonds, not a branched chain polymer. Therefore, the first statement is incorrect.

Leucine and Tryptophan are indeed classified as essential amino acids, as they cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through the diet. Therefore, the second statement is correct.

Curdling of milk involves the denaturation of casein protein due to the change in pH caused by lactic acid production, which alters the protein structure. Thus, it is a denaturation process, making the third statement incorrect.

Invert sugar is an equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose obtained by the hydrolysis of sucrose. Fructose itself is a monosaccharide and not an invert sugar. Therefore, the fourth statement is incorrect.

Answer: Leucine and Tryptophan are classified as Essential amino acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, one Assertion and the other Reason are given. Choose the right option.
Assertion: Insulin is called a protein whereas Glycyl alanine is not called a protein
Reason: A polypeptide with amino acid residue less than 100 can also be called as a protein if it has a well-defined conformation of a protein.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect
Both Assertion and Reason are correct
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
questions.solution:
Insulin is a hormone composed of 51 amino acids arranged in two polypeptide chains linked by disulfide bonds. It is classified as a protein because it possesses a specific, well-defined three-dimensional conformation essential for its biological activity. Therefore, the assertion that insulin is called a protein is correct.

Glycyl alanine is a dipeptide consisting of only two amino acid residues. It lacks the complex, well-defined three-dimensional structure required to be classified as a protein. Thus, it is not called a protein. The assertion is correct.

The reason states that a polypeptide with fewer than 100 amino acid residues can be called a protein if it has a well-defined conformation. This is a scientifically accepted definition in biochemistry, as the functional classification of a protein depends more on its specific folded structure and biological activity than strictly on the number of amino acid residues. Thus, the reason is correct and provides a valid explanation for why insulin is considered a protein despite its relatively small size.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct

questions.q:
Match the reactions of Glucose given in Column I with the major product formed in the reaction as in Column II.
Column I - ReactionsColumn II - Major Product
A$C_6H_{12}O_6 + HI$ (Heat)P$HOOC-(CHOH)_4-COOH$
B$C_6H_{12}O_6 + Br_2$ (aq)Q$CH_3-(CH_2)_4-CH_3$
C$C_6H_{12}O_6 + $ Conc. $HNO_3$R$NH_4OOC-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH$
D$C_6H_{12}O_6 + 2[Ag(NH_3)_2]OH$S$HOOC-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH$
questions.solution:
A + HI (Heat): Strong reduction, removes all OH groups \rightarrow n-hexane $CH_3-(CH_2)_4-CH_3\Rightarrow$ A = Q

B + $Br_2$ (aq): Mild oxidation, only oxidises aldehyde ($-CHO$) at $C_1\rightarrow$ Gluconic acid $HOOC-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH\Rightarrow$ B = S

$A = Q,\ B = S,\ C = P,\ D = R$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, one Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R) are given. Choose the correct option.
Assertion: 2-aminoethanoic acid and p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid can exist as Zwitter ions while p-aminobenzoic acid cannot.
Reason: When the acid group is a relatively strong proton donor and the $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group is sufficiently basic it can accept a $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ion from the acid group to form the dipolar ion.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A .
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A .
A is wrong but R is correct.
questions.solution:
A Zwitter ion is formed when an acidic group (proton donor) and a basic group (proton acceptor) are present in the same molecule, allowing for internal proton transfer. 2-aminoethanoic acid (glycine) contains a carboxylic acid group ($-COOH$) and an amino group ($-NH_2$), which allows it to exist as $H_3N^{+}-CH_2-COO^{-}$.

p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid (sulphanilic acid) contains a strongly acidic sulphonic acid group ($-SO_3H$) and a basic amino group ($-NH_2$), which allows it to exist as a Zwitter ion $H_3N^{+}-C_6H_4-SO_3^{-}$.

p-aminobenzoic acid contains a carboxylic acid group ($-COOH$) and an amino group ($-NH_2$). However, the basicity of the amino group attached to the benzene ring is significantly reduced due to resonance with the aromatic ring. Consequently, it is not basic enough to accept a proton from the carboxylic acid group to form a stable Zwitter ion in aqueous solution.

The Reason (R) correctly explains the requirement for Zwitter ion formation: the acid group must be a strong enough proton donor and the amino group must be sufficiently basic to accept the proton. Since the Assertion (A) correctly identifies the compounds that can form Zwitter ions and the Reason (R) provides the correct chemical principle, both are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

Answer: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, one Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R) are given. Choose the correct option.
Assertion: Maltose, a disaccharide, is a reducing sugar and is obtained by the partial hydrolysis of starch in presence of the enzyme diastase.
Reason: Hydrolysis of one mole of Maltose gives one mole each of $\alpha-\mathrm{D}-$ Glucose and $\beta-$ D-Fructose.
options: A is correct but R is wrong.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A .
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is not the correct explanation of $A$.
questions.solution:
Maltose is a disaccharide composed of two $\alpha$-D-glucose units linked by an $\alpha(1 \to 4)$ glycosidic bond. Since the anomeric carbon of one glucose unit is involved in the glycosidic linkage while the other remains free, it exhibits mutarotation and acts as a reducing sugar. It is indeed produced by the partial hydrolysis of starch using the enzyme diastase. Thus, the Assertion (A) is correct.

Hydrolysis of one mole of maltose yields two moles of $\alpha$-D-glucose, not one mole of glucose and one mole of fructose. The combination of glucose and fructose is characteristic of sucrose. Therefore, the Reason (R) is incorrect.

Answer: A is correct but R is wrong.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: Denaturation of protein is due to loss of both the secondary and tertiary structures of the protein.
The hormone Glucocorticoid controls the level of excretion of water and salts by the kidney.
Vitamins A and K are fat soluble and are stored in the liver of human beings.
Complete hydrolysis of RNA gives Nitrogen containing bases, a pentose sugar and phosphoric acid.
questions.solution:
Denaturation of proteins involves the loss of secondary and tertiary structures due to physical or chemical changes, while the primary structure remains intact. Thus, the statement regarding denaturation is correct.

Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble vitamins and are stored in the liver and adipose tissues. Thus, the statement regarding vitamins is correct.

Complete hydrolysis of RNA yields a pentose sugar (ribose), phosphoric acid, and nitrogenous bases (adenine, guanine, cytosine, and uracil). Thus, the statement regarding RNA hydrolysis is correct.

Glucocorticoids are hormones involved in carbohydrate metabolism, immune response, and inflammation. The hormone that primarily controls the excretion of water and salts by the kidney is mineralocorticoid (specifically aldosterone), not glucocorticoid. Thus, the statement regarding glucocorticoid is incorrect.

Answer: The hormone Glucocorticoid controls the level of excretion of water and salts by the kidney.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
With reference to vitamins and its deficiency diseases, the correct statements are:
(i) Cheilosis is due to the deficiency of Riboflavin
(ii) The deficiency of Vitamin B6 causes pernicious anaemia
(iii) Osteomalacia is due to the deficiency of Vitamin E
(iv) The deficiency of ascorbic acid causes scurvy
(v) The deficiency of Vitamin A causes xerophthalmia
questions.solution:
Statement (i) is correct: Riboflavin (Vitamin $B_2$) deficiency leads to cheilosis, which is the fissuring at the corners of the mouth and lips.

Statement (ii) is incorrect: Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin $B_{12}$ (cyanocobalamin), not Vitamin $B_6$.

Statement (iii) is incorrect: Osteomalacia is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin D, not Vitamin E.

Statement (iv) is correct: Ascorbic acid is Vitamin C, and its deficiency leads to scurvy, characterized by bleeding gums and loose teeth.

Statement (v) is correct: Vitamin A deficiency leads to xerophthalmia, a condition characterized by the hardening of the cornea of the eye.

Therefore, the correct statements are (i), (iv), and (v).

Answer: $\text { (i), (iv) and (v) }$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statement is not true about glucose?
options: Glucose on reaction with $\mathrm{HI}$ and red $\mathrm{P}$ at $373 \mathrm{~K}$ gives a mixture of cyclohexane and 1-iodohexane
Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime
Glucose does not give Schiff's reagent test
Both $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose undergo mutarotation in aqueous solutions
questions.solution:
Glucose is an aldohexose with the structure $CHO(CHOH)_{4}CH_{2}OH$.

Reaction with $HI$ and red phosphorus at $373 \text{ K}$ reduces glucose to $n$-hexane, not a mixture of cyclohexane and 1-iodohexane. This reaction confirms the presence of a straight chain of six carbon atoms in glucose.

Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine ($NH_{2}OH$) to form an oxime, confirming the presence of a carbonyl group.

Although glucose contains an aldehyde group, it does not give the Schiff's reagent test because the aldehyde group exists in a hemiacetal form in the cyclic structure, which is in equilibrium with a very small amount of the free aldehyde form in aqueous solution.

Both $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose undergo mutarotation in aqueous solution, where they interconvert through the open-chain form until an equilibrium mixture is reached.

Answer: Glucose on reaction with $\mathrm{HI}$ and red $\mathrm{P}$ at $373 \mathrm{~K}$ gives a mixture of cyclohexane and 1-iodohexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following peptides, identify the pair where the name and its structure are correctly matched.
questions.solution:
The structure of a peptide is named by listing the amino acid residues from the N-terminal end to the C-terminal end. The N-terminal amino acid has a free $-NH_2$ group, and the C-terminal amino acid has a free $-COOH$ group.

3. The third structure shows $H_2N-CH_2-CO-NH-CH(CH_3)-CO-NH-CH(CH_3)-COOH$. The residues are Glycine (Gly), Alanine (Ala), and Alanine (Ala). The name provided is Gly-Ala-Gly, which is incorrect.

4. The fourth structure shows $H_2N-CH_2-CO-NH-CH(CH_3)-COOH$. The N-terminal is Glycine (Gly) and the C-terminal is Alanine (Ala). The name provided is Ala-Gly, which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, Assertion and Reason are given. Choose the correct option from the following.
Assertion: In the secondary structure of RNA, double helix structure is formed.
Reason: In the double structure of RNA, two nucleic acid chains are wound about each other and held together by hydrogen bonds between pairs of bases
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
questions.solution:
Assertion is correct: RNA is single-stranded, but its secondary structure involves the strand folding back on itself to form localised double-helical regions (e.g., stem-loops in tRNA, hairpin loops).

Reason is incorrect: The double-helical regions in RNA are formed by intramolecular hydrogen bonding within a single chain, not by two separate nucleic acid chains wound around each other. That description applies to DNA, not RNA.

Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the Vitamins given in Column I with the diseases caused by their deficiency as given in Column II.
No.VitaminNo.Deficiency
AKPCheilosis
B$B_{12}$QOsteomalacia
C$B_2$RPermicious Anaemia
DDSHaemophilia
questions.solution:
Vitamin K deficiency leads to increased blood clotting time, which is associated with haemorrhagic conditions like haemophilia (A-S).

Vitamin B_{12}$ deficiency causes pernicious anaemia, a condition where the body cannot make enough healthy red blood cells (B-R). \\ \\ Vitamin B_{2}$ (riboflavin) deficiency leads to cheilosis, which involves cracking and inflammation at the corners of the mouth (C-P).

Vitamin D deficiency leads to softening of bones, known as osteomalacia in adults (D-Q).

Matching these, we get A-S, B-R, C-P, D-Q.
