questions.q:
A dilute solution of sulphuric acid is electrolysed using a current of 0.20 A for 4 hours to produce hydrogen and oxygen gas. The total volume of gas produced at STP is ........ $\mathrm{cm}^3$ [Nearest integer]
[Given, Faraday constant $F=96500 \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{mol}$ at STP molar volume of an ideal gas is $22.7 \mathrm{~L} / \mathrm{mol}]$ [in mL]
questions.solution:
At anode
$2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{O}_2(g)+4 \mathrm{H}^{+}+4 e^{-}$
At cathode
$2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-}$
Now number of gram equivalent $=\frac{\text { Current } \times \text { Time }}{\text { Faraday constant }}$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\frac{0.2 \times 4 \times 60 \times 60}{96500}=0.0298 \\ \\ V_{\mathrm{O}_2} & =\frac{0.0298}{4} \times 22.7=0.1693 \\ \\ V_{\mathrm{H}_2} & =\frac{0.0298}{2} \times 22.7=0.3387 \\ \\ V_{\text {Total }} & =V_{\mathrm{O}_2}+V_{\mathrm{H}_2}=0.5077=508 \mathrm{~mL} \text { or } \mathrm{CC} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 3 Faraday of electricity is passed through three electrolytic cells connected in series containing $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}, \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Al}^{+3}$ ions respectively. The molar ratio in which the 3 metal ions are liberated at the electrodes is
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{r}\mathrm{Ag}^{+}+e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ag} \\ \mathrm{Ca}^{+2}+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ca} \\ \mathrm{Al}^{+3}+3 e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}\end{array} \\ For 1 mol of $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}, \mathrm{Ca}^{+2}$ and $\mathrm{Al}^{+3}, 1 \mathrm{~mol}$ of $e^{-}, 2 \mathrm{~mol}$ of $e^{-}$and 3 mol of $e^{-}$are required respectively. \\ $$ \\ For 1 mole $e^{-}=1$ Faraday $\longrightarrow 1$ mole of $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}$ \\ For 1 mole $e^{-}=1$ Faraday $\longrightarrow \frac{1}{2}$ mole of $\mathrm{Ca}^{+2}$ \\ For 1 mole $e^{-}=1$ Faraday $\longrightarrow \frac{1}{3}$ mole of $\mathrm{Al}^{+3}$ \\ So, for 3 Faraday $\longrightarrow 1 \times 3, \frac{1}{2} \times 3, \frac{1}{3} \times 3$ \\ $=3: \frac{3}{2}: 1 \text { or } 6: 3: 2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$\mathrm{Cu}(s)+\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}(0.01 \mathrm{M}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(0.1 \mathrm{M})+\mathrm{Sn}(s)$
The gibbs free energy change for above mention reaction at NTP is $x \times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$. The value of $x$ is $\qquad$ [Nearest integer]
$\left[\right.$ Given $E_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}}^{\circ}=0.34 \mathrm{~V}, E_{\mathrm{Sn}^{2+} / / \mathrm{sn}}^{\circ}=-0.14 \mathrm{~V}F=96500 \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{mol}]$
questions.solution:
Given,
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{Cu}(s)+\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}(0.01 \mathrm{M}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(0.1 \mathrm{M})+\mathrm{Sn}(s) \\ \\ & E_{\text {cell }}^{\circ}=E_{\text {cathode }}^{\circ}-E_{\text {anoode }}^{\circ} \\ \\ & =-0.14-(0.34)=-0.48 \mathrm{~V} \\ \\ & E_{\text {cell }}=E_{\text {cell }}^*-\frac{0.059}{n} \log \frac{\left[\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\right]}[n=2] \\ \\ & =-0.48-\frac{0.059}{2} \log \frac{[0.1]}{0.01} \\ \\ & =-0.48-0.0290 \log [10]=-0.5095 \mathrm{~V} \\ \end{aligned}$
Gibb's free energy,
$\begin{aligned} \\ \Delta G & =-n F E_{\text {cell }} \\ \\ & =+2(96500) \times 0.5095 \\ \\ & =98.33 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol} \\ \end{aligned}$
or $983 \times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$
Hence, the value of $x$ is 983 .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ undergoes disproportionation, according to the equation,
$
2 \mathrm{Cu}^{+} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+\mathrm{Cu}
$
The $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value for the reaction is:
$[\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}}^{\mathrm{o}}=0.34 \mathrm{~V} \text { and } \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}^{+}}^{\mathrm{O}}=0.15 \mathrm{~V}]$
questions.solution:
The given disproportionation reaction is $2 \mathrm{Cu}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + \mathrm{Cu}$.

This reaction can be split into two half-reactions:
1) Oxidation: $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + e^{-}$ (where $E^{\circ}_{ox} = -E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}^{+}} = -0.15 \text{ V}$)
2) Reduction: $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$ (where $E^{\circ}_{red} = E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+}/\mathrm{Cu}}$)

To find $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+}/\mathrm{Cu}}$, we use the Gibbs free energy relation $\Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}$.
For $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, $\Delta G^{\circ}_{1} = -2 \times F \times 0.34 = -0.68F$.
For $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{+}$, $\Delta G^{\circ}_{2} = -1 \times F \times 0.15 = -0.15F$.
Subtracting the second from the first gives $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, with $\Delta G^{\circ}_{3} = \Delta G^{\circ}_{1} - \Delta G^{\circ}_{2} = -0.68F - (-0.15F) = -0.53F$.
Thus, $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+}/\mathrm{Cu}} = -\Delta G^{\circ}_{3} / (1 \times F) = 0.53 \text{ V}$.

The standard cell potential for the disproportionation reaction is $E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{ox} + E^{\circ}_{red} = -0.15 \text{ V} + 0.53 \text{ V} = +0.38 \text{ V}$.

Answer: $+0.38$ V

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The limiting molar conductivity of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ is $238 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$. At $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, molar conductance of $0.1 \mathrm{M}$ aqueous solution of ammonium hydroxide is $9.54 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$. The degree of ionisation of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ at the same concentration and temperature is:
questions.solution:
The degree of ionisation $\alpha$ of a weak electrolyte is given by the ratio of the molar conductivity at a given concentration $\Lambda_m^c$ to the limiting molar conductivity $\Lambda_m^{\circ}$.

$\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m^c}{\Lambda_m^{\circ}}$

Given values are $\Lambda_m^c = 9.54 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Lambda_m^{\circ} = 238 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Substituting these values into the formula:

$\alpha = \dfrac{9.54}{238} \approx 0.040084$

To express this as a percentage, multiply by 100:

$\alpha \% = 0.040084 \times 100 = 4.0084 \%$

Answer: 4.008%

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ values of $\mathrm{A} . \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ are given. Which element/(s) is/(are) good for coating the surface of iron to prevent corrosion?
Given: $[\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} / \mathrm{Fe}}^0=-0.44 \mathrm{~V} ; \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{A}^{2+} / \mathrm{A}}^0=-2.37 \mathrm{~V} ; \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{B}^{2+} / \mathrm{B}}^0=-0.15 \mathrm{~V} ; \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{C}^{2+} / \mathrm{C}}^0=+0.34 \mathrm{~V}]$
questions.solution:
To prevent the corrosion of iron, the metal used for coating must act as a sacrificial anode. This means the coating metal must have a more negative standard reduction potential than that of iron ($E^{\circ}_{Fe^{2+}/Fe} = -0.44 \text{ V}$).

Comparing the given standard reduction potentials:
$E^{\circ}_{A^{2+}/A} = -2.37 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{B^{2+}/B} = -0.15 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{C^{2+}/C} = +0.34 \text{ V}$

Since $-2.37 \text{ V} \lt -0.44 \text{ V}$, element A has a lower reduction potential than iron. Therefore, element A can act as a sacrificial anode and protect iron from corrosion.

Elements B and C have reduction potentials greater than $-0.44 \text{ V}$, meaning they are more noble than iron and would not provide sacrificial protection.

Answer: Element A only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement among the following.
options: Electrolytic conductance increases with increase in temperature
Conductivity does not depend on the viscosity of the solution
Conductivity depends on the size of the ions
Conductivity depends on the solvation of the ions
questions.solution:
(1) Correct: With increase in temperature, kinetic energy of ions increases and viscosity of solvent decreases \to ions move faster \to conductance increases.

(3) Correct: Larger ions move more slowly \to lower mobility \to lower conductivity.

(4) Correct: Greater solvation \to larger effective ionic radius \to lower mobility \to lower conductivity.

(2) Incorrect: Ion mobility is inversely proportional to viscosity of the solution. Higher viscosity \to greater resistance to ion movement \to lower conductivity. So conductivity does depend on viscosity.

Incorrect statement: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 0.1 mole of $\mathrm{MnO}_4{ }^{2-}$ is oxidised, the quantity of electricity required to completely oxidise $\mathrm{MnO}_4{ }^{2-}$ to $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$ is
questions.solution:
The oxidation reaction of manganate ion to permanganate ion is given by:

$\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-} \rightarrow \mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} + e^{-}$

In this reaction, the oxidation state of manganese changes from $+6$ to $+7$. Thus, $1$ mole of $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-}$ requires $1$ mole of electrons for complete oxidation to $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}$.

Given that $0.1$ mole of $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-}$ is to be oxidized, the number of moles of electrons required is $0.1$ mole.

The quantity of electricity $Q$ is given by $Q = n \times F$, where $n$ is the number of moles of electrons and $F$ is the Faraday constant ($96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$).

$Q = 0.1 \text{ mol} \times 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1} = 9650 \text{ C}$.

Answer: 9650 C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A dry cell consists of a moist paste of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ and $\mathrm{ZnCl}_2$ contained in a $\mathrm{Zn}$ casing which encloses a Carbon rod surrounded by black $\mathrm{MnO}_2$ paste. What is the role of $\mathrm{ZnCl}_2$ in it?
options: It acts as the anode while Carbon rod acts as the cathode.
It prevents pressure being developed in the cell due to $\mathrm{NH}_3$ gas formation.
It serves as cathode thus permitting Carbon rod to act as anode.
It keeps the contents dry and prevents leakage of electrolyte.
questions.solution:
In a Leclanche dry cell, the zinc casing acts as the anode and the carbon rod acts as the cathode. The electrolyte is a moist paste of $\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{Cl}$ and $\mathrm{ZnCl}_2$.

The chemical reaction at the cathode involves the reduction of $\mathrm{MnO}_2$ and the production of ammonia gas, $\mathrm{NH}_3$. Specifically, $\mathrm{NH}_4^{+}$ ions react to form $\mathrm{NH}_3$.

The $\mathrm{NH}_3$ gas produced would otherwise build up pressure inside the cell. $\mathrm{ZnCl}_2$ reacts with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ to form a complex salt, $[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]$, which prevents the accumulation of ammonia gas and the resulting pressure buildup.

Answer: It prevents pressure being developed in the cell due to $\mathrm{NH}_3$ gas formation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following redox couples in the increasing order of their reducing strength:
$\begin{array}{ll}
{[\mathrm{A}]=\mathrm{Cu} / \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}} & \mathrm{E}^0=-0.34 \mathrm{~V} \\
{[\mathrm{~B}]=\mathrm{Ag} / \mathrm{Ag}^{+}} & \mathrm{E}^0=-0.8 \mathrm{~V} \\
{[\mathrm{C}]=\mathrm{Ca} / \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}} & \mathrm{E}^0=+2.87 \mathrm{~V} \\
{[\mathrm{D}]=\mathrm{Cr} / \mathrm{Cr}^{3+}} & \mathrm{E}^0=+0.74 \mathrm{~V}
\end{array}$
questions.solution:
The reducing strength of a species is determined by its standard oxidation potential. A higher standard oxidation potential ($E^{0}_{ox}$) indicates a stronger reducing agent. The given values are standard oxidation potentials ($E^{0}_{ox}$) for the couples $M/M^{n+}$.

The values are:
A: $Cu/Cu^{2+}$, $E^{0}_{ox} = -0.34$ V
B: $Ag/Ag^{+}$, $E^{0}_{ox} = -0.8$ V
C: $Ca/Ca^{2+}$, $E^{0}_{ox} = +2.87$ V
D: $Cr/Cr^{3+}$, $E^{0}_{ox} = +0.74$ V

Comparing the values:
$-0.8 \lt -0.34 \lt +0.74 \lt +2.87$

This corresponds to the order:
B < A < D < C

Thus, the increasing order of reducing strength is B < A < D < C.

Answer: B < A < D < C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the quantity of charge, in Faraday units, required for the reduction of 3.5 moles of $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O} 7^{2-}$ in acid medium?
questions.solution:
The reduction half-reaction for the dichromate ion in an acidic medium is given by:

$\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-} + 14\mathrm{H}^{+} + 6\mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+} + 7\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

From the balanced equation, it is observed that 1 mole of $\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$ requires 6 moles of electrons for its reduction.

Since 1 mole of electrons corresponds to 1 Faraday of charge, 1 mole of $\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$ requires 6 Faraday of charge.

For 3.5 moles of $\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$, the total charge required is:

Charge = $3.5 \text{ moles} \times 6 \text{ Faraday/mole} = 21.0 \text{ Faraday}$

Answer: 21.0

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are 2 statements: Assertion and Reason. Choose the correct option.
Assertion: When Molar conductivity for a strong electrolyte is plotted versus $\sqrt{C}(\mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L})^{1 / 2}$, a straight line is obtained with intercept equal to Molar conductivity at infinite dilution for the electrolyte and Slope equal to $-\mathrm{A}$. All electrolytes of a given type have the same $\mathrm{A}$ value.
Reason: At infinite dilution, strong electrolytes of the same type will have different number of ions due to incomplete dissociation.
options: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect statement.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct statement.
Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect statements.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
questions.solution:
The molar conductivity of a strong electrolyte varies with concentration according to the Kohlrausch equation: $\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^{\circ} - A\sqrt{C}$. This equation represents a straight line when $\Lambda_m$ is plotted against $\sqrt{C}$, where the intercept is $\Lambda_m^{\circ}$ (molar conductivity at infinite dilution) and the slope is $-A$. The constant $A$ depends on the type of electrolyte (e.g., 1:1, 1:2, 2:1) and the solvent properties, meaning all electrolytes of a given type in a given solvent have the same $A$ value. Thus, the Assertion is correct.

The Reason states that at infinite dilution, strong electrolytes of the same type have a different number of ions due to incomplete dissociation. This is incorrect because strong electrolytes are considered to be completely dissociated at all concentrations, including at infinite dilution. Furthermore, the number of ions produced per formula unit is determined by the stoichiometry of the electrolyte, which is constant for a given type of electrolyte. Therefore, the Reason is an incorrect statement.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect statement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A current of 3.0A is passed through 750 ml of 0.45 M solution of CuSO_4$ for 2 hours with a current efficiency of 90%. If the volume of the solution is assumed to remain constant, what would be the final molarity of CuSO_4$ solution?
questions.solution:
The reaction for the electrolysis of CuS$O_{4}$ is Cu$^{2+}$ + 2e$^{-} \rightarrow$ Cu(s). \\ \\ The total charge passed through the solution is $Q = I \times t \times \text{efficiency}$. \\ \\ $Q = 3.0 \text{ A} \times (2 \times 3600 \text{ s}) \times 0.90 = 19440 \text{ C}$. \\ \\ The number of moles of electrons passed is $n_{e} = \dfrac{Q}{F} = \dfrac{19440}{96500} \approx 0.20145 \text{ mol}$. \\ \\ Since 2 moles of electrons are required to reduce 1 mole of Cu$^{2+}$, the moles of Cu$^{2+}$ reduced is $n_{\text{reduced}} = \dfrac{n_{e}}{2} = \dfrac{0.20145}{2} = 0.100725 \text{ mol}$. \\ \\ The initial moles of CuSO_{4}$ is $n_{\text{initial}} = M \times V = 0.45 \text{ M} \times 0.750 \text{ L} = 0.3375 \text{ mol}$.

The final moles of CuSO_{4}$ is $n_{\text{final}} = n_{\text{initial}} - n_{\text{reduced}} = 0.3375 - 0.100725 = 0.236775 \text{ mol}$. \\ \\ The final molarity is $M_{\text{final}} = \dfrac{n_{\text{final}}}{V} = \dfrac{0.236775}{0.750} = 0.3157 \text{ M} \approx 0.316 \text{ M}$.

Answer: 0.316

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement regarding corrosion of iron rod left exposed to atmosphere.
options:
The reaction occurring at the cathodic area is:
$
\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g})+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})+4 \mathrm{e} \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{OH}^{-}$

The overall reaction occurring during the corrosion process is:
$
2 \mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{S})}+3 / 2 \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g})+6 \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} ; \mathrm{E}^0=-1.23 \mathrm{~V}$

The reaction occurring at the cathodic area is:
$
\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g})+4 \mathrm{H}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+4 \mathrm{e} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) ; \mathrm{E}^0=+1.23 \mathrm{~V}$

Reaction occurring at anodic area is:
$
2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) \rightarrow \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g})+4 \mathrm{H}^{+}+4 \mathrm{e}$
questions.solution:
At the anodic area: $2Fe(s) \rightarrow 2Fe^{2+}(aq) + 4e^-$ (oxidation)

At the cathodic area: $O_2(g) + 4H^+(aq) + 4e^- \rightarrow 2H_2O(l)$; $E° = +1.23$ V

$H^+$ ions come from dissolution of atmospheric $CO_2$ in moisture forming weak carbonic acid.

Option (3) correctly states the cathodic reaction with $E° = +1.23$ V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The cell reaction is $\mathrm{Cd}(s) + 2\mathrm{H}^{+}(aq) \rightarrow \mathrm{Cd}^{2+}(aq) + \mathrm{H}_{2}(g)$.

The standard cell potential $E^{0}_{cell}$ is calculated as $E^{0}_{cathode} - E^{0}_{anode}$.

Given $E^{0}(\mathrm{H}^{+}/\mathrm{H}_{2}) = 0.00 \text{ V}$ and $E^{0}(\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cd}) = -0.40 \text{ V}$.

$E^{0}_{cell} = 0.00 - (-0.40) = 0.40 \text{ V}$.

Using the Nernst equation at $298 \text{ K}$:

$E_{cell} = E^{0}_{cell} - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log \dfrac{[\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}] P_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]^{2}}$

Here $n = 2$, $[\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}] = 0.01 \text{ M}$, $[\mathrm{H}^{+}] = 0.02 \text{ M}$, and $P_{\mathrm{H}_{2}} = 0.8 \text{ atm}$.

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log \dfrac{0.01 \times 0.8}{(0.02)^{2}}$

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - 0.02955 \log \dfrac{0.008}{0.0004}$

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - 0.02955 \log(20)$

Since $\log(20) = \log(2 \times 10) = 0.3010 + 1 = 1.3010$.

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - 0.02955 \times 1.3010$

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - 0.03844 = 0.36156 \text{ V} \approx 0.3616 \text{ V}$.

Answer: 0.3616 V

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $0.1 \mathrm{M}$ solution of $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ is taken in a Conductivity cell and a potential difference of $40 \mathrm{~V}$ is applied across the ends of a column of this solution whose diameter is $4.0 \mathrm{~cm}$ and length of the column is $12 \mathrm{~cm}$. The current used is $0.4 \mathrm{~A}$. The Molar conductivity of the solution is _________.
questions.solution:
The resistance $R$ of the solution is given by Ohm's law: $R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{40 \text{ V}}{0.4 \text{ A}} = 100 \Omega$.

The area of cross-section $A$ of the column is $\pi r^2$. Given diameter $d = 4.0 \text{ cm}$, the radius $r = 2.0 \text{ cm}$. Thus, $A = \pi \times (2.0 \text{ cm})^2 = 4\pi \text{ cm}^2 \approx 12.566 \text{ cm}^2$.

The cell constant $G^{*}$ is given by $\dfrac{l}{A}$, where $l = 12 \text{ cm}$. So, $G^{*} = \dfrac{12}{4\pi} = \dfrac{3}{\pi} \text{ cm}^{-1} \approx 0.9549 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

The conductivity $\kappa$ is given by $\kappa = \dfrac{G^{*}}{R} = \dfrac{3/\pi}{100} = \dfrac{3}{100\pi} \text{ S cm}^{-1} \approx 0.009549 \text{ S cm}^{-1}$.

The molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is calculated using the formula $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{1000 \times \kappa}{C}$, where $C = 0.1 \text{ M}$.

Substituting the values: $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{1000 \times (3 / (100\pi))}{0.1} = \dfrac{30}{\pi \times 0.1} = \dfrac{300}{\pi} \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Calculating the value: $\Lambda_m \approx \dfrac{300}{3.14159} \approx 95.493 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Rounding to the nearest option, we get $95.5 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $95.5 \mathrm{~Scm}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are 4 equations showing Molar conductivities at infinite dilution of various electrolytes. Which one of them represents the correct equation?
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N a B r}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N a C l}=\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KCl}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KBr}} \\
& \left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{HCl}}+\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KOH}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KCl}}=\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}} \\
& \left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KBr}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{NaBr}}=\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{NaBr}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{Nal}} \\
& \left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N H_4 \mathrm{Cl}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{NO}_3}=\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N H_4 \mathrm{Cl}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N H 4 B r}
\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
Using Kohlrausch's law, expanding Equation 2 LHS: $(A^0_m)_{HCl} + (A^0_m)_{KOH} - (A^0_m)_{KCl}$

$= [\lambda^0(H^+) + \lambda^0(Cl^-)] + [\lambda^0(K^+) + \lambda^0(OH^-)] - [\lambda^0(K^+) + \lambda^0(Cl^-)]$

$= \lambda^0(H^+) + \lambda^0(OH^-)$

$= (A^0_m)_{H_2O}$ = RHS

Equation 2 is correct. The cancellation of $\lambda^0(Cl^-)$ and $\lambda^0(K^+)$ on both sides confirms LHS = RHS.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Propane in presence of $\mathrm{O}_2$ gas undergoes complete combustion to produce $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$. The required $\mathrm{O}_2$ for this combustion reaction was produced by the electrolysis of water. For what duration of time had water been electrolysed by passing $200 \mathrm{~A}$ current so that Oxygen gas produced could completely burn $44 \mathrm{~g}$ of Propane?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of propane is:
$\text{C}_{3}\text{H}_{8} + 5\text{O}_{2} \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_{2} + 4\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$

The molar mass of propane ($\text{C}_{3}\text{H}_{8}$) is $3 \times 12 + 8 \times 1 = 44 \text{ g/mol}$.

Moles of propane = $\dfrac{44 \text{ g}}{44 \text{ g/mol}} = 1 \text{ mol}$.

From the stoichiometry, $1 \text{ mol}$ of propane requires $5 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_{2}$.

The electrolysis of water is given by:
$2\text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_{2} + \text{O}_{2}$

For $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_{2}$ produced, $4 \text{ moles}$ of electrons are required (since each oxygen atom changes oxidation state from $-2$ to $0$, and there are $2$ oxygen atoms per $\text{O}_{2}$ molecule).

Total moles of electrons required for $5 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_{2}$ = $5 \times 4 = 20 \text{ mol}$.

Using Faraday's law of electrolysis, $Q = n \times F = I \times t$, where $F \approx 96500 \text{ C/mol}$.

$20 \times 96500 = 200 \times t$

$t = \dfrac{20 \times 96500}{200} = 9650 \text{ seconds}$.

Converting to hours: $t = \dfrac{9650}{3600} \approx 2.68 \text{ hours}$.

Answer: 2.68 hours

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the chemical reactions taking place at the Anode of the cell with the correct cell in which the reaction occurs.
No.Anodic ReactionNo.Cell
A$Zn(Hg) + 2OH^- \to ZnO_{(s)} + H_2O + 2e^-$PFuel cell
B$2H_2(g) + 4OH^- \to 4H_2O(l) + 4e^-$QLeclanche cell
C$Zn_{(s)} \to Zn^{2+} + 2e^-$RNickel Cadmium storage cell
D$Cd_{(s)} + 2OH^- \to CdO_{(s)} + H_2O(l) + 2e^-$SMercury cell
questions.solution:
The anodic reaction $\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{Hg})+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{ZnO}_{(\mathrm{S})}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+2 e$ occurs in the Mercury cell (S).

The anodic reaction $2 \mathrm{H}_2(g)+4 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l)+4 e$ occurs in the Fuel cell (P).

The anodic reaction $Z n_{(S)} \rightarrow Z n^{2+}+2 e$ occurs in the Leclanche cell (Q).

The anodic reaction $\mathrm{Cd}_{(S)}+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{CdO}_{(S)}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l)+2 e$ occurs in the Nickel Cadmium storage cell (R).

Matching these gives A=S, B=P, C=Q, D=R.

questions.q:
For a cell reaction,
$A(s)+B^{2+}(a q) \longrightarrow A^{2+}(a q)+B(s)$; the
standard emf of the cell is $0.295 \mathrm{~V}$ at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The equilibrium constant at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ will be

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If electrolysis of water is carried out for a time duration of 2 hours, how much electric current in amperes would be required to liberate $100 \mathrm{~ml}$ of $\mathrm{O}_2$ gas measured under standard conditions of temperature and pressure?
questions.solution:
The electrolysis of water produces oxygen gas at the anode according to the reaction: $2H_2O(l) \rightarrow O_2(g) + 4H^{+}(aq) + 4e^{-}$.

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $4$ moles of electrons are required to produce $1$ mole of $O_2$ gas. At standard temperature and pressure (STP), $1$ mole of any gas occupies $22.4$ liters or $22400$ ml.

The volume of $O_2$ given is $100$ ml. The number of moles of $O_2$ produced is $n_{O_2} = \dfrac{100}{22400} = \dfrac{1}{224}$ moles.

The total charge $Q$ required is $n_{e^{-}} \times F$, where $n_{e^{-}} = 4 \times n_{O_2} = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{224} = \dfrac{1}{56}$ moles of electrons and $F = 96500$ C/mol.

$Q = \dfrac{96500}{56} \approx 1723.21$ Coulombs.

The time duration is $2$ hours, which is $2 \times 3600 = 7200$ seconds.

The current $I$ is given by $I = \dfrac{Q}{t} = \dfrac{1723.21}{7200} \approx 0.2393$ A.

Answer: 0.2393 A

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The reaction taking place in a galvanic cell is as given
$\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{B}^{2+}\left(\mathrm{1} \mathrm{1} \mathrm{1 0} \mathrm{0}^{-\mathrm{M}} \mathrm{M}\right) \rightarrow \mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\mathrm{A}^{2+}(0.1 \mathrm{M}).$
The emf of the cell is $+2.651 \mathrm{~V}$. If the standard emf of the cell is $+2.71 \mathrm{~V}$, what is the value of $\mathrm{X}$ ?
questions.solution:
The cell reaction is $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{B}^{2+}(10^{-X} \mathrm{M}) \rightarrow \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{A}^{2+}(0.1 \mathrm{M})$.

The Nernst equation for the cell at $298 \mathrm{K}$ is given by $E_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log Q$, where $n$ is the number of electrons transferred.

Here, $n = 2$, $E_{\text{cell}} = 2.651 \mathrm{~V}$, and $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = 2.71 \mathrm{~V}$.

The reaction quotient $Q$ is $\dfrac{[\mathrm{A}^{2+}]}{[\mathrm{B}^{2+}]} = \dfrac{0.1}{10^{-X}} = 10^{X-1}$.

Substituting the values into the Nernst equation:

$2.651 = 2.71 - \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log(10^{X-1})$

$2.651 - 2.71 = -0.02955 \times (X-1)$

$-0.059 = -0.02955 \times (X-1)$

$X-1 = \dfrac{0.059}{0.02955} \approx 2$

$X = 2 + 1 = 3$.

Answer: X = 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When Lead Storage battery is in the process of getting charged which one of the following reactions takes place?
options: $\mathrm{SO}_3$ gas gets liberated and $\mathrm{PbO}_{2(\mathrm{~s})}$ is formed.
questions.solution:
In a lead storage battery, the discharge reaction is: $\mathrm{Pb}_{(s)} + \mathrm{PbO}_{2(s)} + 2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4(aq)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{PbSO}_{4(s)} + 2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{(l)}$.

During the charging process, the reaction is reversed by applying an external potential. The reaction becomes: $2\mathrm{PbSO}_{4(s)} + 2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{(l)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Pb}_{(s)} + \mathrm{PbO}_{2(s)} + 2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4(aq)}$.

In this process, $\mathrm{PbSO}_{4(s)}$ at the cathode is reduced to $\mathrm{Pb}_{(s)}$, and $\mathrm{PbSO}_{4(s)}$ at the anode is oxidized to $\mathrm{PbO}_{2(s)}$.

Thus, $\mathrm{PbSO}_{4(s)}$ is converted into $\mathrm{Pb}_{(s)}$ and $\mathrm{PbO}_{2(s)}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{PbSO}_{4(\mathrm{~s})}$ gets converted to $\mathrm{Pb}_{(\mathrm{S})}$ and $\mathrm{PbO}_{2(\mathrm{~s})}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The Molar conductivity of $0.05 \mathrm{M}$ solution of $\mathrm{MgCl}_2$ is $194.5 \mathrm{~ohm}^{-1} \mathrm{~cm}^2$ per mole at room temperature. A Conductivity cell with electrodes having $3.0 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ surface area and $1.0 \mathrm{~cm}$ apart is filled with the solution of $\mathrm{MgCl}_2$. What would be the resistance offered by the conductivity cell?
questions.solution:
The molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is related to the conductivity $\kappa$ and molarity $C$ by the formula $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{1000 \times \kappa}{C}$.

Given $\Lambda_m = 194.5 \text{ ohm}^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $C = 0.05 \text{ M}$, we calculate the conductivity $\kappa$ as follows:

$\kappa = \dfrac{\Lambda_m \times C}{1000} = \dfrac{194.5 \times 0.05}{1000} = \dfrac{9.725}{1000} = 0.009725 \text{ S cm}^{-1}$.

The cell constant $G^{*}$ is defined as $\dfrac{l}{A}$, where $l$ is the distance between electrodes and $A$ is the surface area of the electrodes.

$G^{*} = \dfrac{1.0 \text{ cm}}{3.0 \text{ cm}^2} = 0.3333 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

The relationship between conductivity $\kappa$, resistance $R$, and cell constant $G^{*}$ is $\kappa = \dfrac{G^{*}}{R}$.

Rearranging for resistance $R$:

$R = \dfrac{G^{*}}{\kappa} = \dfrac{0.3333}{0.009725} \approx 34.27 \text{ ohms}$.

Answer: 34.27 ohms

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the items in Column I with their description in Column II
S.No.Column IS.No.Column II
AKappa KPIntensive property.
B$E_{cell}^0$QExtensive property.
CMolar conductivityRDecreases with decrease in concentration of both strong and weak electrolytes.
D$\Delta G_{cell}$SIncreases with dilution.
questions.solution:
Kappa (K) is the specific conductivity, which is defined as the conductance of a unit volume of solution. It decreases with a decrease in concentration (dilution) because the number of ions per unit volume decreases.

Standard cell potential ($\mathrm{E_{cell}^0}$) is an intensive property because it does not depend on the amount of substance in the system.

Molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) is defined as the conductivity of a solution containing one mole of electrolyte. It increases with dilution because the volume of the solution containing one mole of electrolyte increases, leading to greater dissociation (for weak electrolytes) and reduced inter-ionic attractions (for strong electrolytes).

Gibbs free energy change ($\mathrm{\Delta G_{cell}}$) is an extensive property because it depends on the amount of substance undergoing the reaction in the cell.

Matching the items:
A (Kappa) matches R (Decreases with decrease in concentration).
B ($\mathrm{E_{cell}^0}$) matches P (Intensive property).
C (Molar conductivity) matches S (Increases with dilution).
D ($\mathrm{\Delta G_{cell}}$) matches Q (Extensive property).

Thus, the correct mapping is A=R, B=P, C=S, D=Q.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Q}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a cell reaction, $A(s)+B^{2+}(a q) \longrightarrow A^{2+}(a q)+B(s)$; the standard emf of the cell is $0.295 \mathrm{~V}$ at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The equilibrium constant at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ will be
questions.solution:
The cell reaction is $A(s) + B^{2+}(aq) \rightarrow A^{2+}(aq) + B(s)$. The number of electrons transferred in the reaction is $n = 2$.

The relationship between the standard cell potential $E^{\circ}_{cell}$ and the equilibrium constant $K_{eq}$ is given by the Nernst equation at $25^{\circ}C$ (298 K):

$E^{\circ}_{cell} = \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log K_{eq}$

Substituting the given values $E^{\circ}_{cell} = 0.295 \text{ V}$ and $n = 2$:

$0.295 = \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log K_{eq}$

$\log K_{eq} = \dfrac{0.295 \times 2}{0.0591}$

$\log K_{eq} = \dfrac{0.59}{0.0591} \approx 10$

$K_{eq} = 10^{10}$

Answer: $1 \times 10^{10}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Assuming a theoretical setup where only the anodic removal of $\text{OH}^-$ affects the solution, and no change in volume, the time required to obtain a solution of $\text{pH} = 4$ by electrolysis of $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}\text{NaOH}$ (using current $0.5\text{ A}$) will be:
questions.solution:
Initial moles of $OH^- = M \times V = 0.1 \times 0.1 = 0.01$ mol

Target pH $= 4\Rightarrow[H^+] = 10^{-4}$ M, meaning solution is acidic \Rightarrow practically all $OH^-$ must be removed.

Moles of $OH^-$ to be removed $\approx 0.01$ mol

Anodic reaction: $4OH^- \to O_2 + 2H_2O + 4e^-$

1 mole of $OH^-$ releases 1 mole of electrons $\Rightarrown_e = 0.01$ mol

$Q = n_e \times F = 0.01 \times 96500 = 965$ C

$t = \dfrac{Q}{I} = \dfrac{965}{0.5} = 1930\ s = 1.93 \times 10^3\ s$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What will be the emf of the following cell at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ?
$\mathrm{Fe} / \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}(0.001 \mathrm{M})|| \mathrm{H}^{+}(0.01 \mathrm{M}) \mid \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})$
(1 Bar) $\mid \mathrm{Pt}(s)E_{\left(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} / \mathrm{Fe}\right)}^{\circ}=-0.44 \mathrm{~V} ; E_{\left(\mathrm{H}^{+} / \mathrm{H}_2\right)}^{\circ}=0.00 \mathrm{~V}$
questions.solution:
The cell reaction is given by:
Anode: $\text{Fe}(s) \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^{-}$
Cathode: $2\text{H}^{+}(aq) + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{H}_{2}(g)$
Overall reaction: $\text{Fe}(s) + 2\text{H}^{+}(aq) \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) + \text{H}_{2}(g)$

The standard cell potential $E^{\circ}_{cell}$ is calculated as:
$E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cathode} - E^{\circ}_{anode}$
$E^{\circ}_{cell} = 0.00 \text{ V} - (-0.44 \text{ V}) = 0.44 \text{ V}$

Using the Nernst equation at $25^{\circ} \text{C}$:
$E_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cell} - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log \dfrac{[\text{Fe}^{2+}] \cdot P_{\text{H}_{2}}}{[\text{H}^{+}]^{2}}$
Here $n = 2$, $[\text{Fe}^{2+}] = 0.001 \text{ M}$, $[\text{H}^{+}] = 0.01 \text{ M}$, and $P_{\text{H}_{2}} = 1 \text{ bar}$.

$E_{cell} = 0.44 - \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log \dfrac{0.001 \times 1}{(0.01)^{2}}$
$E_{cell} = 0.44 - 0.02955 \log \dfrac{10^{-3}}{10^{-4}}$
$E_{cell} = 0.44 - 0.02955 \log(10)$
$E_{cell} = 0.44 - 0.02955 \approx 0.41 \text{ V}$

Answer: $0.41 \mathrm{~V}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the molar conductance of $0.025 \mathrm{M}$ aqueous solution of calcium chloride at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The specific conductance of calcium chloride is $12.04 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{Sm}^{-1}$
questions.solution:
The molar conductance $\Lambda_m$ is given by the formula $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa}{C}$, where $\kappa$ is the specific conductance and $C$ is the molar concentration.

Given:
$\kappa = 12.04 \times 10^{-2} \text{ S m}^{-1}$
$C = 0.025 \text{ M} = 0.025 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Convert concentration to $\text{mol m}^{-3}$:
$1 \text{ L} = 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$
$C = 0.025 \text{ mol} / 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3 = 25 \text{ mol m}^{-3}$

Substitute the values into the formula:
$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{12.04 \times 10^{-2} \text{ S m}^{-1}}{25 \text{ mol m}^{-3}}$
$\Lambda_m = 0.4816 \times 10^{-2} \text{ S m}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Express in scientific notation as required by the options:
$\Lambda_m = 481.6 \times 10^{-5} \text{ S m}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $481.6 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{Sm}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given that molar conductances for $\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$, $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}$ are $523.28,280.0$ and $129.8\Omega^{-1} \mathrm{~cm}^{2} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively. What is the molar conductivity $\left(\Omega^{-1} \mathrm{~cm}^{2} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)$ of $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{OH}$ ?
questions.solution:
According to Kohlrausch law of independent migration of ions, the molar conductivity of an electrolyte at infinite dilution is the sum of the molar conductivities of its constituent ions.

The given molar conductivities are:
$\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}) = \lambda^{\circ}(\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}) + 2\lambda^{\circ}(\mathrm{OH}^{-}) = 523.28$
$\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}) = \lambda^{\circ}(\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}) + 2\lambda^{\circ}(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}) = 280.0$
$\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}) = \lambda^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}) + \lambda^{\circ}(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}) = 129.8$

We need to find $\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = \lambda^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}) + \lambda^{\circ}(\mathrm{OH}^{-})$.

Using the given values, we can express $\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH})$ as:
$\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = \Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}) - \dfrac{1}{2}\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{BaCl}_{2})$

Substituting the values:
$\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = 129.8 + \dfrac{523.28}{2} - \dfrac{280.0}{2}$
$\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = 129.8 + 261.64 - 140.0$
$\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}) = 391.44 - 140.0 = 251.44$

Answer: $251.44$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The specific conductivity of a solution containing $1.0 \mathrm{~g}$ of anhydrous $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ in $200 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$ of the solution has been found to be $0.0058 \mathrm{Scm}^{-1}$. The molar and equivalent conductivity of the solution respectively are
questions.solution:
The molar mass of $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ is $137.3 + 2 \times 35.5 = 208.3 \mathrm{~g/mol}$.

The number of moles of $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ is $n = \dfrac{1.0 \mathrm{~g}}{208.3 \mathrm{~g/mol}} \approx 0.0048008 \mathrm{~mol}$.

The molarity $M$ of the solution is $M = \dfrac{n}{V(\text{in L})} = \dfrac{0.0048008 \mathrm{~mol}}{0.200 \mathrm{~L}} = 0.024004 \mathrm{~M}$.

The molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is calculated as $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa \times 1000}{M} = \dfrac{0.0058 \mathrm{~S cm}^{-1} \times 1000 \mathrm{~cm}^3 \mathrm{L}^{-1}}{0.024004 \mathrm{~mol L}^{-1}} \approx 241.626 \mathrm{~S cm}^2 \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.

For $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$, the n-factor is 2 (since $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ba}^{2+} + 2\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$).

The equivalent conductivity $\Lambda_{eq}$ is calculated as $\Lambda_{eq} = \dfrac{\Lambda_m}{n\text{-factor}} = \dfrac{241.626}{2} \approx 120.813 \mathrm{~S cm}^2 \mathrm{eq}^{-1}$.

Rounding to the nearest values provided in the options, we get $241.6 \mathrm{~S cm}^2 \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and $120.83 \mathrm{~S cm}^2 \mathrm{eq}^{-1}$.

Answer: $241.6 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^{2} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and $120.83 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^{2} \mathrm{eq}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ozone in stratosphere is depleted by
questions.solution:
The depletion of the ozone layer in the stratosphere is primarily caused by chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).

CFCs are compounds containing chlorine, fluorine, and carbon. When these compounds reach the stratosphere, they are decomposed by ultraviolet radiation to release chlorine free radicals ($\mathrm{Cl}^{\bullet}$).

The chlorine radical acts as a catalyst in the destruction of ozone ($\mathrm{O}_3$) through the following reactions:

$\mathrm{Cl}^{\bullet} + \mathrm{O}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}^{\bullet} + \mathrm{O}_2\mathrm{ClO}^{\bullet} + \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cl}^{\bullet} + \mathrm{O}_2$

Among the given options, $\mathrm{CF}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$ (dichlorodifluoromethane, commonly known as Freon-12) is a well-known CFC responsible for this ozone depletion process.

Answer: $\mathrm{CF}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$

Acid rain is primarily caused by the emission of sulphur dioxide ($SO_2$) and nitrogen oxides ($NO_x$).

These gases react with water vapor and other chemicals in the atmosphere to form sulphuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) and nitric acid ($HNO_3$), which then fall to the ground as acid rain.

Among the given options, sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxide are the primary pollutants responsible for this phenomenon.

Answer: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxide

questions.q: Carbon monoxide is poisonous to human beings because
options: it binds 300 times more strongly to haemoglobin than oxygen.
it leads to coagulation of blood.
questions.solution:
Carbon monoxide ($CO$) has a very high affinity for haemoglobin, which is approximately 300 times greater than that of oxygen ($O_{2}$).

When $CO$ is inhaled, it binds to the iron atom in the haemoglobin molecule to form carboxyhaemoglobin, which is much more stable than oxyhaemoglobin.

This binding prevents haemoglobin from transporting oxygen to the tissues, leading to oxygen deprivation and toxicity.

Answer: it binds 300 times more strongly to haemoglobin than oxygen.

Carbon monoxide (CO) is a gaseous pollutant, not particulate matter. Tin (Sn) and Selenium (Se) are not primary particulate emissions associated with standard vehicle exhaust systems.

Answer: Pb

questions.q: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement?
options: $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ are separated by fractional distillation
In sodium nitroprusside test for Sulphur, the violet colour is due to formation of complex $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]$
questions.solution:
Electrophiles are electron-deficient species that can accept an electron pair. While $\text{AlCl}_3$, $\text{SO}_3$, and $\text{NO}_2^+$ are electrophiles, $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ possess lone pairs of electrons on their central atoms (nitrogen and oxygen, respectively). This makes them electron-rich species, so they act as nucleophiles, not electrophiles.

Option (A) is a correct statement because fractional distillation is used to separate miscible liquids with a boiling point difference of less than $25\text{ K}$.

Option (B) is a correct statement. In the sodium nitroprusside test for sulphur, the sulphide ion reacts to form a violet-coloured complex: $\text{S}^{2-} + [\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]^{2-} \rightarrow [\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$, which corresponds to $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]$.

Option (D) is a correct statement as all the given species have either a negative charge or lone pairs of electrons, making them nucleophiles.

Therefore, the incorrect statement is (C).

Answer: $\text{AlCl}_3, \text{NH}_3, \text{SO}_3, \text{NO}_2^+, \text{H}_2\text{O}$ are electrophiles

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the aromatic compounds among the given set based on Huckel's rule:
questions.solution:
According to Huckel's rule, a compound is aromatic if it is cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and has $(4n + 2)\pi$ electrons, where $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$

Compound (I): Cyclopropenyl cation is cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated. It has $2\pi$ electrons. $4n + 2 = 2 \Rightarrow n = 0$. Thus, it is aromatic.

Compound (II): Naphthalene is cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated. It has $10\pi$ electrons ($5$ double bonds). $4n + 2 = 10 \Rightarrow n = 2$. Thus, it is aromatic.

Compound (III): Cyclopentadiene contains an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom, which breaks the continuous conjugation. Thus, it is non-aromatic.

Compound (IV): Azulene is cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated. It has $10\pi$ electrons ($5$ double bonds). $4n + 2 = 10 \Rightarrow n = 2$. Thus, it is aromatic.

Therefore, compounds I, II, and IV are aromatic.

Answer: I, II, IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the given resonating structures of molecules negative mesomeric effect is represented by:
questions.solution:
The negative mesomeric effect ($-M$ effect) is observed when a substituent withdraws electron density from a conjugated system (such as a benzene ring) through resonance. This results in a decreased electron density in the ring, typically placing positive charges at the ortho and para positions.

In option (A), the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group donates a lone pair of electrons to the ring, showing a $+M$ effect and creating negative charges at the ortho and para positions.

In option (B), the $-\text{OH}$ group donates a lone pair of electrons to the ring, showing a $+M$ effect.

In option (C), the $-\text{NO}_2$ group withdraws $\pi$ electrons from the ring towards itself, creating positive charges at the ortho and para positions. This represents the $-M$ effect.

In option (D), the $-\text{NH}_2$ group donates a lone pair of electrons to the ring, showing a $+M$ effect.

Answer:

Anisole is the common name for methoxybenzene, which consists of a benzene ring attached to a methoxy group ($-OCH_3$).

The prefix 'o-' (ortho) indicates that an ethyl group ($-C_2H_5$) is attached to the adjacent carbon atom (position 2) on the benzene ring relative to the methoxy group.

Therefore, o-ethyl anisole has an $-OCH_3$ group and a $-C_2H_5$ group at the 1 and 2 positions of the benzene ring. This structure corresponds to option (D).

Answer:

Aniline (boiling point $457 \text{ K}$) and chloroform (boiling point $334 \text{ K}$) have a large difference in their boiling points and can be separated by simple distillation.

2-Nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol are separated by steam distillation. 2-Nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas 4-nitrophenol is not steam volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

Thus, the correct matching is A \rightarrow R, B \rightarrow S, C \rightarrow Q, D \rightarrow P.

Answer: A — R B—S C—Q D—P

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is not the correct IUPAC name of the compound?
questions.solution:
Let us evaluate the IUPAC name for each given structure:

Option (A): The structure is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. The alkyl group attached to the oxygen atom is a 3-methylbutyl group. Thus, the ether is named 3-methylbutoxybenzene. This name is correct.

Option (B): The structure is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. The principal functional group is $-\text{OH}$, so the longest chain containing the $-\text{OH}$ group and the double bond is selected and numbered from the right to give the $-\text{OH}$ group the lowest locant (1). The substituents are a bromo group at C-2 and a methyl group at C-3. The name is 2-bromo-3-methylbut-2-en-1-ol. This name is correct.

Option (C): The structure is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3$. The principal chain must contain both $-\text{OH}$ groups. The longest such chain has 6 carbon atoms. Numbering from right to left gives the $-\text{OH}$ groups the lower locants (1,3) compared to left to right (4,6). The methyl substituents are at C-2 and C-5. The name is 2,5-dimethylhexane-1,3-diol. This name is correct.

Option (D): The structure is a cyclohexane ring with a propoxy group ($-\text{OC}_3\text{H}_7$) and two methyl groups on adjacent carbons. We must number the ring to give the lowest possible locant set for the substituents. Numbering from the carbon with the two methyl groups gives the locant set $1, 1, 2$. Numbering from the carbon with the propoxy group gives the locant set $1, 2, 2$. Comparing the two sets, $1, 1, 2$ is lower than $1, 2, 2$. Therefore, the methyl groups are at position 1 and the propoxy group is at position 2. Alphabetically, 'methyl' comes before 'propoxy'. The correct IUPAC name is 1,1-dimethyl-2-propoxycyclohexane. The given name 2,2-dimethyl-1-propoxycyclohexane is incorrect.

Answer: 2,2–Dimethyl–1–propoxycyclohexane:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen fails in
questions.solution:
Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen involves the fusion of the organic compound with sodium metal to form sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$).

For the formation of cyanide ion ($\text{CN}^{-}$), both carbon and nitrogen must be present in the organic compound.

Hydrazine hydrochloride ($\text{NH}_2\text{-NH}_2\cdot\text{HCl}$) does not contain carbon. Therefore, it cannot form sodium cyanide upon fusion with sodium metal, and Lassaigne's test for nitrogen fails.

The other compounds ($\text{NH}_2\text{CONH}_2$, $\text{NH}_2\text{CONHNH}_2\cdot\text{HCl}$, and $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NHNH}_2\cdot\text{HCl}$) contain both carbon and nitrogen, so they will give a positive test.

Answer: $\text{NH}_2\text{- NH}_2\text{HCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not aromatic?
questions.solution:
Aromatic compounds must satisfy Huckel's rule, which states that a planar, cyclic, conjugated system must have $(4n + 2)\pi$ electrons to be aromatic, where $n$ is an integer.

Cyclopentadienyl anion has $6\pi$ electrons ($4$ from two double bonds and $2$ from the lone pair on the carbon atom), which satisfies $4n + 2 = 6$ for $n = 1$. Thus, it is aromatic.

Pyridine is a heterocyclic aromatic compound with $6\pi$ electrons ($6$ from the ring atoms), satisfying Huckel's rule. Thus, it is aromatic.

Cyclopropenyl cation has $2\pi$ electrons from the one double bond, which satisfies $4n + 2 = 2$ for $n = 0$. Thus, it is aromatic.

Cyclooctatetraene has $8\pi$ electrons. According to Huckel's rule, systems with $4n$ electrons are anti-aromatic if planar. However, cyclooctatetraene adopts a non-planar tub-shaped conformation to avoid anti-aromaticity, making it non-aromatic.

Answer: Cyclooctatetraene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following exhibits geometrical isomerism?
questions.solution:
Geometrical isomerism occurs in alkenes when each carbon atom of the double bond is attached to two different groups. Let us examine the structures of the given compounds.

For 1, 2-dibromopropene, the structure is $CH_3-C(Br)=CHBr$. The carbon at position 2 is attached to a methyl group and a bromine atom. The carbon at position 1 is attached to a hydrogen atom and a bromine atom. Since both carbons have two different groups attached, this compound exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms).

For 2-methylbut-2-ene, the structure is $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$. The carbon at position 2 is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not exhibit geometrical isomerism.

For hex-1-ene, the structure is $CH_2=CHCH_2CH_2CH_2CH_3$. The terminal carbon is attached to two identical hydrogen atoms, so it does not exhibit geometrical isomerism.

For 1, 1-diphenylethene, the structure is $(C_6H_5)_2C=CH_2$. The carbon at position 1 is attached to two identical phenyl groups, so it does not exhibit geometrical isomerism.

Answer: 1, 2-Dibromopropene

questions.q:
Two statements, one Assertion and the other Reason are given. Choose the correct option.
Assertion: Heterocyclic compounds like Pyridine and Thiophene are non-aromatic compounds.
Reason: According to Huckel rule for a given compound to exhibit aromaticity, the molecule must be planar, cyclic system having delocalised $(4 n+2) \pi$ electrons.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct.
Reason is correct but Assertion is incorrect.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect.
questions.solution:
Assertion is incorrect: Pyridine and Thiophene are well-known aromatic compounds. Pyridine has 6 delocalized $\pi$ electrons (3 double bonds), and Thiophene has 6 delocalized $\pi$ electrons (2 double bonds + lone pair of S). Both satisfy Huckel's rule and are aromatic.

Reason is correct: Huckel's rule states that a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated system with $(4n+2)\pi$ electrons is aromatic.

Reason is correct but Assertion is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, One Assertion and the other Reason, are given.
Which one of the following is the correct option?
Assertion: The acid strength of 4 compounds in the descending order is p-Nitrophenol > p-Methoxyphenol > Phenol > p- chlorophenol.
Reason: Electron withdrawing groups increase the acid strength while Electron donating groups decrease the acid strength of Phenol and its derivatives.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct.
Assertion is correct but Reason is wrong.
Assertion is wrong but Reason is correct.
Both Assertion and Reason are wrong.
questions.solution:
The acid strength of substituted phenols depends on the electronic effects of the substituents. Electron withdrawing groups (EWG) stabilize the phenoxide ion through inductive (-I) and resonance (-M) effects, thereby increasing acidity. Electron donating groups (EDG) destabilize the phenoxide ion through inductive (+I) and resonance (+M) effects, thereby decreasing acidity.

Comparing the substituents:
1. p-Nitrophenol: $-NO_{2}$ is a strong EWG ($-I$ and $-M$ effects), making it the most acidic.
2. p-Chlorophenol: $-Cl$ is an EWG ($-I$ effect dominates over $+M$ effect), making it more acidic than phenol.
3. Phenol: Reference compound.
4. p-Methoxyphenol: $-OCH_{3}$ is an EDG ($+M$ effect dominates over $-I$ effect), making it the least acidic.

The correct descending order of acid strength is p-Nitrophenol > p-Chlorophenol > Phenol > p-Methoxyphenol. The assertion states the order as p-Nitrophenol > p-Methoxyphenol > Phenol > p-chlorophenol, which is incorrect. The reason correctly states that EWGs increase acid strength and EDGs decrease it.

Answer: Assertion is wrong but Reason is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The best method for the separation of $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol from their mixture is:
questions.solution:
$o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol can be separated by steam distillation based on the difference in their volatility.

$o$-nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding, which reduces its intermolecular forces of attraction, making it more volatile and capable of being steam distilled.

$p$-nitrophenol exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding, leading to the formation of associated molecules, which significantly increases its boiling point and makes it less volatile.

Therefore, $o$-nitrophenol distills over with steam while $p$-nitrophenol remains in the distillation flask.

Answer: Steam distillation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the most stable free radical?
questions.solution:
The stability of free radicals is determined by factors such as resonance, hyperconjugation, and inductive effects.

Option (1) is a vinyl radical, which is highly unstable due to the $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atom having the unpaired electron in an $sp^2$ orbital.

Option (2) is a methyl radical, which has no alkyl groups to provide stability through hyperconjugation.

Option (3) is a tertiary butyl radical, which is stabilized by hyperconjugation from nine $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms.

Option (4) is a diphenylmethyl radical, which is highly stabilized by extensive resonance with two phenyl rings. The unpaired electron is delocalized over the entire conjugated system of both benzene rings, making it significantly more stable than the tertiary butyl radical.

Answer: $\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5\right)_2 \dot{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.
options: Staggered conformation of ethane is more stable than the eclipsed conformation.
The energy difference between the staggered and eclipsed conformation of ethane is $12.55 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$
A $90^{\circ}$ rotation converts staggered conformation of ethane into eclipsed conformation.
The distance between non-bonded H-atoms of ethane in eclipsed conformation is $2.29 Å$
questions.solution:
In the ethane molecule, the staggered conformation is more stable than the eclipsed conformation due to lower torsional strain. This is a correct statement.

The energy difference between the staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane is approximately $12.55 \text{ kJ/mol}$ ($3.0 \text{ kcal/mol}$), which is a correct statement.

The dihedral angle between the C-H bonds of adjacent carbon atoms in the staggered conformation is $60^{\circ}$. A rotation of $60^{\circ}$ about the C-C bond converts the staggered conformation into the eclipsed conformation. Therefore, a $90^{\circ}$ rotation does not convert the staggered conformation into the eclipsed conformation. This is an incorrect statement.

In the eclipsed conformation of ethane, the distance between the non-bonded hydrogen atoms on adjacent carbon atoms is approximately $2.29 \text{ \AA}$, which is a correct statement.

Answer: A $90^{\circ}$ rotation converts staggered conformation of ethane into eclipsed conformation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following free radicals in the increasing order of their stability:
questions.solution:
The stability of free radicals is primarily determined by resonance, hyperconjugation, and the inductive effect.

Structure A is an isopropyl radical, which is a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) alkyl radical. It is stabilized by hyperconjugation from 6 $\alpha$-hydrogens.

Structure B is a tert-butyl radical, which is a tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) alkyl radical. It is stabilized by hyperconjugation from 9 $\alpha$-hydrogens. Thus, B is more stable than A.

Structure C is an allyl radical ($CH_2=CH-CH_2^{\bullet}$), which is stabilized by resonance. The unpaired electron is delocalized over the $\pi$ system. Resonance stabilization is generally more significant than hyperconjugation.

Structure D is a benzyl radical ($C_6H_5-CH_2^{\bullet}$), which is stabilized by resonance with the benzene ring. The unpaired electron is delocalized over the entire aromatic ring, providing greater resonance stabilization than the allyl radical.

Comparing the stability:
1. Alkyl radicals (A and B) are less stable than resonance-stabilized radicals (C and D).
2. Among alkyl radicals, $3^{\circ} \gt 2^{\circ}$, so $B \gt A$.
3. Among resonance-stabilized radicals, the benzyl radical (D) is more stable than the allyl radical (C) due to more extensive delocalization.

Therefore, the increasing order of stability is $A \lt B \lt C \lt D$.

Answer: $\mathrm{A} \lt \mathrm{B} \lt \mathrm{C} \lt \mathrm{D}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the compound which is non-aromatic in nature.
questions.solution:
To determine the aromaticity of the given compounds, we apply Huckel's rule, which states that a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated system with $(4n+2)\pi$ electrons is aromatic, while one with $4n\pi$ electrons is anti-aromatic. If the molecule is not planar or lacks continuous conjugation, it is non-aromatic.

Compound [A] is cyclooctatetraene. It has $8\pi$ electrons ($4n$ system). However, it adopts a non-planar 'tub' shape to minimize angle strain and avoid anti-aromaticity, making it non-aromatic.

Compound [B] is the cyclopentadienyl anion. It has $6\pi$ electrons ($4n+2$ with $n=1$), is planar, and fully conjugated, making it aromatic.

Compound [C] is tropolone. It is a planar, cyclic, conjugated system with $6\pi$ electrons in the ring (considering the resonance structure with the oxygen atom), making it aromatic.

Compound [D] is thiophene. It has $6\pi$ electrons ($4$ from the double bonds and $2$ from the lone pair on sulfur), is planar, and fully conjugated, making it aromatic.

Therefore, cyclooctatetraene [A] is the non-aromatic compound.

Answer: A

What is the percentage of element $\mathrm{X}$ and what is the formula of the violet-coloured compound formed when Lassaigne's extract of the organic compound is treated with sodium nitroprusside?
questions.solution:
The element X is sulphur because the treatment with fuming $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ followed by $\mathrm{BaCl}_2$ results in the precipitation of $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$.

The molar mass of $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ is $137 + 32 + 4 \times 16 = 233 \text{ g/mol}$.

The mass of sulphur in $1.2 \text{ g}$ of $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ is calculated as:
$\text{Mass of S} = \dfrac{32}{233} \times 1.2 \approx 0.1648 \text{ g}$.

The percentage of sulphur in the organic compound is:
$\% \text{S} = \dfrac{\text{Mass of S}}{\text{Mass of compound}} \times 100 = \dfrac{0.1648}{0.8} \times 100 = 20.6 \%$.

When Lassaigne's extract containing $\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}$ is treated with sodium nitroprusside, $\mathrm{Na}_2[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_5\mathrm{NO}]$, a violet-coloured complex is formed. The reaction is:
$\mathrm{Na}_2[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_5\mathrm{NO}] + \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_5\mathrm{NOS}]$.

Thus, the percentage is $20.6$ and the formula is $\mathrm{Na}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_5\mathrm{NOS}]$.

Answer: $20.6 \quad \& \quad \mathrm{Na}_4\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_5 \mathrm{NOS}\right]$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the following compounds, identify the one which is most acidic.
questions.solution:
The acidity of a compound is determined by the stability of its conjugate base. The more stable the conjugate base, the more acidic the compound.

Compound [A] is phenol, which forms a phenoxide ion. The negative charge on the oxygen is delocalized into the benzene ring.

Compound [B] is dicyclohexylmethanol, an aliphatic alcohol. It lacks resonance stabilization for its conjugate base and is the least acidic.

Compound [C] is p-nitrophenol. The nitro group ($-NO_2$) is a strong electron-withdrawing group (EWG) due to both its inductive effect ($-I$) and resonance effect ($-M$). This group significantly stabilizes the phenoxide ion by dispersing the negative charge, making p-nitrophenol more acidic than phenol.

Compound [D] is cyclohexanol, an aliphatic alcohol, which is less acidic than phenol.

Comparing the compounds, the presence of the strong electron-withdrawing $-NO_2$ group in [C] makes it the most acidic among the given options.

Answer: C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A statement of Assertion followed by a statement of Reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the following options.
Assertion: The Eclipsed and the Staggered conformations of Ethane continuously flip from one form to the other. 
Reason: The torsional barrier between the Conformers of Ethane has a high value of about $50 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$ and this restricts free rotation around $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}$ bond.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct statement.
Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect statements.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect statement.
questions.solution:
The eclipsed and staggered conformations of ethane are conformers that interconvert rapidly at room temperature due to the low energy barrier for rotation around the carbon-carbon single bond. Thus, the assertion that they continuously flip is correct.

The torsional barrier for rotation in ethane is approximately $12.5 \text{ kJ/mol}$ (or $3 \text{ kcal/mol}$), not $50 \text{ kJ/mol}$. This energy barrier is low enough to allow for rapid rotation at room temperature, meaning rotation is not restricted. Therefore, the reason provided is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect statement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The stability of free radicals is primarily determined by resonance stabilization and hyperconjugation. The species are:

A: $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\dot{\mathrm{C}}$ (tert-butyl radical) - stabilized by 9 hyperconjugative hydrogens.

B: $(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)_3\dot{\mathrm{C}}$ (triphenylmethyl radical) - stabilized by extensive resonance with three phenyl rings.

C: $(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)_2\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}$ (diphenylmethyl radical) - stabilized by resonance with two phenyl rings.

D: $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}$ (isopropyl radical) - stabilized by 6 hyperconjugative hydrogens.

Comparing the stabilization effects, resonance provides significantly greater stability than hyperconjugation. Therefore, the radicals with phenyl rings (B and C) are more stable than the alkyl radicals (A and D).

Among the resonance-stabilized radicals, B has three phenyl rings while C has two, making B more stable than C. Among the alkyl radicals, A has 9 hyperconjugative hydrogens while D has 6, making A more stable than D.

The decreasing order of stability is B > C > A > D.

Answer: B > C > A > D

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: In $\mathrm{CH}_3^{-}$, Carbon carrying negative charge is $\mathrm{sp}^2$ hybridised.

The order of stability of Carbanions is $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2^{-}\lt \left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5\right)_2 \mathrm{CH}^{-}\lt \left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5\right)_3 \mathrm{C}^{-}$
The order of stability of Carbocations is $(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5)_3 \mathrm{C}^{+}\lt (\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5)_2 \mathrm{CH}^{+}\lt \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2^{+}$
In $\mathrm{CH}_3{ }^{+}$, Carbon carrying positive charge is $\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridised.
questions.solution:
In $\mathrm{CH}_3^{-}$, the carbon atom is bonded to three hydrogen atoms and has one lone pair. The steric number is $3 + 1 = 4$, which corresponds to $\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridisation. Thus, option (1) is incorrect.

In $\mathrm{CH}_3^{+}$, the carbon atom is bonded to three hydrogen atoms and has no lone pair. The steric number is $3 + 0 = 3$, which corresponds to $\mathrm{sp}^2$ hybridisation. Thus, option (4) is incorrect.

For carbocations, the stability increases with the number of phenyl groups due to resonance stabilization. The order is $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2^{+} \lt (\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5)_2 \mathrm{CH}^{+} \lt (\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5)_3 \mathrm{C}^{+}$. Thus, option (3) is incorrect.

For carbanions, the stability increases with the number of phenyl groups due to resonance stabilization. The order is $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2^{-} \lt (\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5)_2 \mathrm{CH}^{-} \lt (\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5)_3 \mathrm{C}^{-}$. This matches option (2), which is correct.

Answer: The order of stability of Carbanions is $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2^{-}\lt \left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5\right)_2 \mathrm{CH}^{-}\lt \left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5\right)_3 \mathrm{C}^{-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following in the decreasing order of their Dipole moments.
a. Chlorobenzene
b. 1,2-Dichlorobenzene
c. 1,3-Dichlorobenzene
d. 1,4-Dichlorobenzene.
questions.solution:
Let $\mu$ be the dipole moment of a single C-Cl bond. The net dipole moment is $\mu_{net} = \sqrt{\mu_1^2 + \mu_2^2 + 2\mu_1\mu_2\cos\theta}$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the two C-Cl bonds.

(b) 1,2-Dichlorobenzene (ortho): $\theta = 60°$
$\mu_{net} = \sqrt{\mu^2 + \mu^2 + 2\mu^2\cos60°} = \sqrt{3}\mu$ (Highest)

(d) 1,4-Dichlorobenzene (para): $\theta = 180°$
$\mu_{net} = \sqrt{\mu^2 + \mu^2 + 2\mu^2\cos180°} = 0$ (Lowest)

(c) 1,3-Dichlorobenzene (meta): $\theta = 120°$
$\mu_{net} = \sqrt{\mu^2 + \mu^2 + 2\mu^2\cos120°} = \mu$

(a) Chlorobenzene: theoretically $\mu_{net} = \mu$, but due to the $-I$ effect of the second Cl in 1,3-dichlorobenzene slightly reducing individual bond dipoles, chlorobenzene has a slightly higher dipole moment than 1,3-dichlorobenzene.

Decreasing order: $b \gt a \gt c \gt d$

questions.q: The blue colouration obtained from the Lassaigne's test of nitrogen is due to the formation of
questions.solution:
In Lassaigne's test for nitrogen, the organic compound is fused with metallic sodium to convert nitrogen into sodium cyanide, $\mathrm{NaCN}$.

The extract is then treated with ferrous sulphate, $\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}$, which reacts with $\mathrm{NaCN}$ to form sodium ferrocyanide: $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} + 6\mathrm{CN}^{-} \rightarrow [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{4-}$.

On adding ferric chloride, $\mathrm{FeCl}_{3}$, some $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ions are oxidized to $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions. These $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions react with the ferrocyanide ions to form ferric ferrocyanide, which is Prussian blue in colour.

The chemical reaction is: $3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{4-} + 4\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]_{3}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Fe}_4\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Give the correct order of acidity of
questions.solution:
The acidity of oxoacids of chlorine depends on the stability of the conjugate base formed after the loss of a proton. The conjugate bases are $\mathrm{ClO}_{4}^{-}$, $\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}$, $\mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-}$, and $\mathrm{ClO}^{-}$.

The stability of these conjugate bases is determined by the number of oxygen atoms attached to the central chlorine atom. More oxygen atoms lead to greater delocalization of the negative charge through resonance, thereby increasing the stability of the conjugate base.

The number of oxygen atoms in the acids are: $\mathrm{HClO}_4$ (4), $\mathrm{HClO}_3$ (3), $\mathrm{HClO}_2$ (2), and $\mathrm{HClO}$ (1).

The stability order of the conjugate bases is $\mathrm{ClO}_{4}^{-} \gt \mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-} \gt \mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-} \gt \mathrm{ClO}^{-}$.

Since a more stable conjugate base corresponds to a stronger acid, the order of acidity is $\mathrm{HClO}_4 \gt \mathrm{HClO}_3 \gt \mathrm{HClO}_2 \gt \mathrm{HClO}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{HClO} \lt \mathrm{HClO}_2 \lt \mathrm{HClO}_3 \lt \mathrm{HClO}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange stability of the given carbon cation in decreasing order
questions.solution:
The stability of carbocations is determined by the electron-donating or electron-withdrawing nature of the substituents attached to the benzene ring. The carbocations are stabilized by resonance from the lone pairs on the substituents at the para position.

The substituents are: (i) $-OCH_{3}$, (ii) $-OH$, (iii) $-NH_{2}$, and (iv) $-Cl$.

The resonance donating ability of these groups depends on the electronegativity of the atom directly attached to the ring. A less electronegative atom donates its lone pair more effectively into the ring via resonance ($+M$ effect). The order of $+M$ effect is $-NH_{2} \gt -OH \gt -OCH_{3}$.

The $-Cl$ group is an electron-withdrawing group due to its strong $-I$ effect, which outweighs its weak $+M$ effect, making it the least stabilizing among the given options.

Comparing the resonance donors: Nitrogen is less electronegative than Oxygen, so $-NH_{2}$ is a stronger donor than $-OH$ and $-OCH_{3}$. Between $-OH$ and $-OCH_{3}$, the $-OH$ group is a slightly better donor than $-OCH_{3}$ because the methyl group in $-OCH_{3}$ is electron-donating, which slightly reduces the electron density on the oxygen atom compared to the hydrogen in $-OH$.

Thus, the order of stability is (iii) $ \gt (ii) \gt (i) \gt (iv)$.

Answer: (iii) $ \gt ($ ii $) \gt ($ i $) \gt ($ iv $)$

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of following compound?
questions.solution:
The given structure is a central carbon atom bonded to two vinyl groups ($-CH=CH_2$) and two ethynyl groups ($-C\equiv CH$).

The structure can be represented as $C(CH=CH_2)_2(C\equiv CH)_2$.

To determine the IUPAC name, we identify the longest carbon chain containing the maximum number of multiple bonds. The longest chain containing both the double and triple bonds is a five-carbon chain (pentadiene derivative).

The parent chain is a pentadiene with double bonds at positions 1 and 4. The substituents at position 3 are two ethynyl groups ($-C\equiv CH$).

Thus, the IUPAC name is 3,3-diethynylpenta-1,4-diene.

Answer: 3, 3-diethynylpenta-1, 4-diene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: The reducing agent which is used to reduce iron oxide in blast furnace is
questions.solution:
In the blast furnace, iron oxides such as $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$ are reduced to metallic iron. The process involves two main reducing agents: coke ($\mathrm{C}$) and carbon monoxide ($\mathrm{CO}$).

Coke acts as the primary fuel and also reacts with oxygen to form $\mathrm{CO_2}$, which is then reduced by more coke to form $\mathrm{CO}$ according to the reaction $\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}$.

The carbon monoxide ($\mathrm{CO}$) is the actual chemical reducing agent that reduces the iron oxides in the upper, cooler parts of the furnace, for example: $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3} + 3\mathrm{CO} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO_2}$.

While coke is the source of the reducing agent, $\mathrm{CO}$ is the primary reducing agent that performs the reduction of iron oxides in the blast furnace.

Answer: $\mathrm{CO}$
