questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An Alkene " X " on reaction with hot acidified $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ gave a mixture of Ethanoic acid and Propanone. Identify " X ".
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alkene with hot acidified $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ results in oxidative cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond. The products formed depend on the substitution pattern at the double bond carbons.

Ethanoic acid is $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH}$, which corresponds to a terminal $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=$ group after oxidation. Propanone is $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COCH}_3$, which corresponds to a $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{C}=$ group after oxidation.

Combining these two fragments, the alkene must be $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2$.

The structure $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2$ is 2-methylbut-2-ene.

Answer: 2- Methylbut-2-ene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkene on reductive ozonolysis gives ketones only as the product?
questions.solution:
Reductive ozonolysis of an alkene involves the cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond ($C=C$) to form carbonyl compounds. If the carbons involved in the double bond are substituted with two alkyl groups (i.e., tetrasubstituted or trisubstituted with alkyl groups), the products are ketones. If one or both carbons are bonded to a hydrogen atom, the products are aldehydes.

Analyzing the options:

But-2-ene ($CH_3-CH=CH-CH_3$): Each carbon of the double bond is bonded to one hydrogen atom. Ozonolysis yields two molecules of acetaldehyde ($CH_3CHO$), which are aldehydes.

1,2-butadiene ($CH_2=C=CH-CH_3$): This is an allene. Ozonolysis yields formaldehyde ($HCHO$), carbon dioxide ($CO_2$), and acetaldehyde ($CH_3CHO$).

1,4-cyclohexadiene: The double bonds are within the ring. Ozonolysis leads to the formation of dialdehydes (specifically, succinaldehyde).

2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene ($(CH_3)_2C=C(CH_3)_2$): Each carbon of the double bond is bonded to two methyl groups. Ozonolysis cleaves the double bond to produce two molecules of acetone ($(CH_3)_2C=O$), which is a ketone.

Answer: 2, 3-dimethylbut-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the type of reaction:
questions.solution:
The reaction shown is the addition of hydrogen bromide (HBr) to propene ($CH_3-CH=CH_2$).

The reaction proceeds via the electrophilic addition mechanism. In the first step, the electrophile $H^{+}$ from HBr attacks the double bond to form the more stable secondary carbocation ($CH_3-CH^{+}-CH_3$).

In the second step, the nucleophile $Br^{-}$ attacks the carbocation to form 2-bromopropane ($CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_3$).

This follows Markovnikov's rule, which is characteristic of electrophilic addition reactions to alkenes.

Answer: Electrophilic addition

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the Alkane (molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_8 \mathrm{H}_{18}$ ) which yields only a single monochloride on Chlorination in the presence of sunlight.
questions.solution:
The formation of only a single monochloride upon chlorination implies that all hydrogen atoms in the alkane molecule are equivalent. This means the molecule must possess a high degree of symmetry such that replacing any hydrogen atom with a chlorine atom results in the same product.

Analyzing the options:

2,4-Dimethylhexane has multiple types of hydrogen atoms (primary, secondary, and tertiary), leading to multiple monochlorinated isomers.

3,4-Dimethylhexane also has multiple types of hydrogen atoms, leading to multiple monochlorinated isomers.

2,2,3,3-Tetramethylbutane has a structure where all 18 hydrogen atoms are equivalent. Specifically, it consists of two tert-butyl groups connected by a central C-C bond. Each of the four methyl groups attached to the quaternary carbons is equivalent, and there are no other types of hydrogens. Thus, chlorination yields only one monochloride, 1-chloro-2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane.

2,2,4-Trimethylpentane (isooctane) has several distinct types of hydrogen atoms (primary, secondary, and tertiary), leading to multiple monochlorinated products.

Therefore, 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane is the correct alkane.

Answer: 2, 2, 3, 3-Tetramethylbutane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the final product $[\mathrm{Y}]$ in the following reaction.
$[\mathrm{X}]+\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{COCH}_3 \xrightarrow[293 \mathrm{~K}]{\mathrm{OH}^{-}}[\mathrm{Y}]$
questions.solution:
The reaction of $p$-nitrotoluene with $CrO_2Cl_2$ in $CS_2$ followed by hydrolysis is the Etard reaction, which oxidizes the methyl group to an aldehyde. Thus, $[X]$ is $p$-nitrobenzaldehyde ($O_2N-C_6H_4-CHO$).

The subsequent reaction is a Claisen-Schmidt condensation between $p$-nitrobenzaldehyde and acetophenone ($C_6H_5COCH_3$) in the presence of a base ($OH^-$).

The base abstracts an $\alpha$-hydrogen from acetophenone to form an enolate ion, which then performs a nucleophilic attack on the carbonyl carbon of $p$-nitrobenzaldehyde. This is followed by dehydration to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone.

The product $[Y]$ is $p$-nitrobenzalacetophenone, which has the structure $O_2N-C_6H_4-CH=CH-CO-C_6H_5$.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The reaction of propan-1-ol with $\text{SOCl}_2$ follows the Darzens halogenation mechanism to produce 1-chloropropane as product [X].

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{SOCl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{SO}_2 + \text{HCl}$

The reaction of 1-chloropropane [X] with sodium acetylide ($\text{HC} \equiv \text{C}-\text{Na}$) is a nucleophilic substitution ($\text{S}_N2$) reaction, yielding pent-1-yne as product [Y].

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{HC} \equiv \text{C}-\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C} \equiv \text{CH} + \text{NaCl}$

The hydration of pent-1-yne [Y] in the presence of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{HgSO}_4$ (Kucherov reaction) follows Markovnikov addition of water across the triple bond to form an enol intermediate, which tautomerizes to pentan-2-one as product [Z].

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C} \equiv \text{CH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4, \text{HgSO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{OH})=\text{CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$

Answer: Pentan-2-one.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of reactivity of halogens with alkanes is:
questions.solution:
The reactivity of halogens towards alkanes is determined by the bond dissociation energy of the halogen molecule and the enthalpy of the reaction. The reaction of an alkane with a halogen is represented as $R-H + X_2 \rightarrow R-X + H-X$.

The reactivity order is governed by the strength of the $H-X$ bond formed and the ease of breaking the $X-X$ bond. Fluorine is the most reactive due to its high electronegativity and the high bond energy of the $H-F$ bond formed, which makes the reaction highly exothermic. Iodine is the least reactive because the reaction is endothermic and the $H-I$ bond is relatively weak.

The experimental order of reactivity for halogens with alkanes is $F_2 \gt Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt I_2$.

Answer: $F_2 \gt C l_2 \gt B r_2 \gt I_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The number of grams of bromine that will completely react with 5 g of pentene is:
[Atomic mass of $\mathrm{Br}=80 \mathrm{u}$ ]
questions.solution:
The chemical formula for pentene is $C_{5}H_{10}$. The reaction of pentene with bromine is an addition reaction:

$C_{5}H_{10} + Br_{2} \rightarrow C_{5}H_{10}Br_{2}$

The molar mass of pentene ($C_{5}H_{10}$) is $5 \times 12 + 10 \times 1 = 70$ g/mol.

The molar mass of bromine ($Br_{2}$) is $2 \times 80 = 160$ g/mol.

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, 1 mole of pentene reacts with 1 mole of bromine. Therefore, 70 g of pentene reacts with 160 g of bromine.

For 5 g of pentene, the mass of bromine required is:

Mass of $Br_{2} = \dfrac{160}{70} \times 5 = \dfrac{800}{70} = \dfrac{80}{7} \approx 11.428$ g.

Rounding to the nearest provided option, the value is 11.4 g.

Answer: 11.4 g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the final product $[Z]$ formed when the given reactions take place?
questions.solution:
The reaction of phenol with Zn dust under heating conditions leads to the reduction of phenol to benzene. Thus, [X] is benzene ($C_{6}H_{6}$).

The reaction of benzene with a mixture of concentrated $HNO_{3}$ and concentrated $H_{2}SO_{4}$ (nitrating mixture) results in electrophilic aromatic substitution, specifically nitration, to form nitrobenzene. Thus, [Y] is nitrobenzene ($C_{6}H_{5}NO_{2}$).

The reaction of nitrobenzene with $Br_{2}$ in the presence of $FeBr_{3}$ is an electrophilic aromatic substitution. The nitro group ($-NO_{2}$) is a strongly deactivating group and is meta-directing. Therefore, the bromine atom will be substituted at the meta position relative to the nitro group. Thus, [Z] is 3-bromonitrobenzene (also known as m-bromonitrobenzene).

Answer: 3-Bromonitrobenzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unsaturated hydrocarbon $[\mathrm{A}]$ undergoes the following series of reactions. Identify $[\mathrm{A}]$.
questions.solution:
The hydrocarbon [A] reacts with ammoniacal $AgNO_3$ to give no reaction, which indicates that it is not a terminal alkyne. This eliminates but-1-yne and propyne.

The reaction of [A] with $Na/liquid NH_3$ gives a trans product, which is a characteristic reaction of internal alkynes to form trans-alkenes. This suggests [A] is an internal alkyne.

The reaction of [A] with alkaline $KMnO_4$ at 383 K yields 2 moles of a carboxylic acid with formula $C_2H_4O_2$, which is acetic acid ($CH_3COOH$). This implies that the oxidative cleavage of the triple bond in [A] produces two molecules of acetic acid. For an internal alkyne $R-C \equiv C-R$ to yield two molecules of $CH_3COOH$, the structure must be $CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_3$, which is but-2-yne.

Ozonolysis of but-2-yne ($CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_3$) followed by $Zn/H_2O$ yields a diketone, specifically butane-2,3-dione ($CH_3COCOCH_3$), which matches the description of [B].

Therefore, [A] is but-2-yne.

Answer: But-2-yne

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The Electrophilic addition to an unsymmetrical alkene always occurs through the formation of a more stable Carbanion intermediate.

Between the two alkenes - (i) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2-\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$ and (ii). $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$, compound (i) will show geometrical isomerism
Greater the number of alkyl groups attached to the double bonded Carbon atoms, the less stable is the alkene.
The major product formed when 2-Methylpropene reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ is tert. butyl alcohol.
questions.solution:
Electrophilic addition to an unsymmetrical alkene proceeds via the formation of a more stable carbocation intermediate, not a carbanion. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

For geometrical isomerism, each carbon atom of the double bond must be attached to two different groups. In compound (i), $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$, the carbon atom on the left is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism. Thus, the second statement is incorrect.

According to the stability of alkenes, the stability increases with the number of alkyl groups attached to the double-bonded carbon atoms due to hyperconjugation and inductive effects. Thus, the third statement is incorrect.

When 2-methylpropene, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}_2$, reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$, the reaction follows Markovnikov's rule. The proton adds to the terminal carbon to form the more stable tert-butyl carbocation, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{C}^{+}$, which then reacts with water to form tert-butyl alcohol, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{COH}$. Thus, the fourth statement is correct.

Answer: The major product formed when 2-Methylpropene reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ is tert. butyl alcohol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Convert Benzene \rightarrow  3-Bromophenol by choosing appropriate reagents $[(i)$ to (v)] in the correct sequence.
$(i)\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}\left(0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)  \quad (ii) Conc. \mathrm{HNO}_3 / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4  \quad (iii) \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} / 283 \mathrm{~K}  \quad (iv) \mathrm{Fe} / \mathrm{HCl}  \quad (v) \mathrm{Br} 2 / \mathrm{Fe}$
questions.solution:
The conversion of benzene to 3-bromophenol requires the introduction of a meta-directing group followed by bromination, or the use of a group that directs meta and can be converted to a hydroxyl group. Since the hydroxyl group is ortho/para-directing, it must be introduced after the bromine atom is placed in the meta position.

Nitration of benzene using $Conc. HNO_3 / H_2SO_4$ (reagent ii) gives nitrobenzene.

Bromination of nitrobenzene using $Br_2 / Fe$ (reagent v) gives 1-bromo-3-nitrobenzene because the nitro group is meta-directing.

Reduction of the nitro group using $Fe / HCl$ (reagent iv) gives 3-bromoaniline.

Diazotization of 3-bromoaniline using $NaNO_2 / HCl$ at $0^{\circ}C$ (reagent i) gives 3-bromobenzenediazonium chloride.

Hydrolysis of the diazonium salt using $H_2O / 283 K$ (reagent iii) gives 3-bromophenol.

The correct sequence is ii, v, iv, i, iii.

Answer: ii, v, iv, i, iii

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the compound which gives an optically active haloalkane on reaction with $\mathrm{H}_2$ / Ni on heating.
questions.solution:
$H_2$/Ni reduces the double bond to give a haloalkane. The product is optically active only if it contains a chiral centre (4 different groups on the Cl-bearing carbon).

A (3-chloropent-1-ene): Reduction gives 3-chloropentane. Cl-bearing carbon has two identical $-CH_2CH_3$ groups. Achiral — optically inactive.

B (4-chloropent-2-ene): Reduction gives 2-chloropentane. Cl-bearing carbon has $-H$, $-Cl$, $-CH_3$, and $-CH_2CH_2CH_3$ — four different groups. Chiral centre — optically active.

C (3-chloro-2,4-dimethylpent-1-ene): Reduction gives 3-chloro-2,4-dimethylpentane. Cl-bearing carbon has two identical $-CH(CH_3)_2$ groups. Achiral — optically inactive.

D (4-chlorohept-2-ene): Reduction gives 4-chloroheptane. Cl-bearing carbon has two identical $-CH_2CH_2CH_3$ groups. Achiral — optically inactive.

Only compound B gives an optically active haloalkane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Formation of alkanes by action of Zn on alkyl halides is called
questions.solution: Formation of alkanes by action of Zn on alkyl halides is called as Frankland reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the reaction given below, identify $B$.
$\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CHCl} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Cl}_2} A \xrightarrow[363 \mathrm{~K}]{\mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OH})_2} B$
questions.solution:
The complete reaction is as follows,
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CH}_2= & \mathrm{CHCl} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Cl}_2} \mathrm{ClCH}_2-\mathrm{CHCl}_2 \\ & \xrightarrow[363 \mathrm{~K}-\mathrm{HCl}]{\mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OH})_2} \underset{\substack{\text { 1, dichloroethene } \\(B)}}{\mathrm{CH}_2}=\mathrm{CCl}_2\end{aligned}$
During dehydrohalogination of $(A)$, the more acidic hydrogen (i.e. $\mathrm{CHCl}_2$ ) is eliminated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The major product obtained in the following reaction is :
questions.solution:
The reaction of methylcyclohexane with bromine in the presence of light ($h\nu$) is a free-radical substitution reaction. The mechanism involves the formation of a carbon radical intermediate.

The stability of the radical intermediate determines the major product. The possible radicals formed are primary, secondary, or tertiary. The tertiary radical at the C1 position (where the methyl group is attached) is the most stable due to hyperconjugation and inductive effects from the surrounding alkyl groups.

Although the tertiary radical is the most stable, the selectivity of bromine radicals is high. However, in the case of methylcyclohexane, the tertiary hydrogen at the C1 position is significantly more reactive towards abstraction by a bromine radical than the secondary hydrogens on the ring. Therefore, the bromine atom preferentially replaces the hydrogen at the tertiary position to form 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane as the major product.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Predict the final major product 'S' of the following reaction
questions.solution:
The starting material is benzylidenecyclohexane. Ozonolysis of this alkene with $\text{O}_3$ followed by $\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}$ (reductive workup) cleaves the double bond to yield benzaldehyde and cyclohexanone. Thus, $\text{P}$ and $\text{Q}$ are benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$) and cyclohexanone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$).

The reaction of $\text{P}$ and $\text{Q}$ with dilute $\text{NaOH}$ in aqueous ethanol involves an aldol condensation. Benzaldehyde lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens, while cyclohexanone possesses $\alpha$-hydrogens. Therefore, cyclohexanone acts as the nucleophile (enolate donor) and benzaldehyde acts as the electrophile (acceptor). The resulting product $\text{R}$ is 2-benzylidenecyclohexanone.

Subsequent ozonolysis of 2-benzylidenecyclohexanone ($\text{R}$) cleaves the exocyclic double bond. This produces benzaldehyde ($\text{P}$) and cyclohexane-1,2-dione ($\text{S}$).

Thus, the final major product $\text{S}$ is cyclohexane-1,2-dione.

Answer: Cyclohexane-1, 2-dione

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following compounds in the decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitution reaction.
(I) Chlorobenzene
(II) Nitrobenzene
(III) Benzene
(IV) Isopropylbenzene
questions.solution:
The reactivity of benzene derivatives towards electrophilic aromatic substitution depends on the nature of the substituent attached to the benzene ring. Electron-donating groups (EDG) increase the electron density of the ring, making it more reactive, while electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) decrease the electron density, making it less reactive.

Analyzing the substituents:
1. Isopropylbenzene (IV): The isopropyl group ($-CH(CH_3)_2$) is an alkyl group. It acts as an electron-donating group through the inductive effect (+I) and hyperconjugation, which significantly activates the benzene ring.
2. Benzene (III): This is the reference compound with no substituents.
3. Chlorobenzene (I): The chlorine atom is an electron-withdrawing group due to its strong inductive effect (-I), although it is ortho/para directing due to resonance (+M). Overall, it deactivates the ring compared to benzene.
4. Nitrobenzene (II): The nitro group ($-NO_2$) is a very strong electron-withdrawing group due to both -I and -M effects, which strongly deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitution.

Comparing the effects:
Isopropylbenzene is more reactive than benzene because of the +I and hyperconjugation effects of the alkyl group. Benzene is more reactive than chlorobenzene because the -I effect of chlorine deactivates the ring. Chlorobenzene is more reactive than nitrobenzene because the -NO_2$ group is a much stronger electron-withdrawing group than the chlorine atom. \\ \\ Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity is: Isopropylbenzene \gt Benzene \gt Chlorobenzene \gt Nitrobenzene. \\ \\ Answer: $\text { IV }>\text { III }>\text { I }>\text { II }

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions is an example for incomplete combustion?
questions.solution:
Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon involves the reaction of the fuel with sufficient oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water as the only products. Incomplete combustion occurs when there is insufficient oxygen, leading to the formation of products like carbon monoxide or elemental carbon (soot) instead of carbon dioxide.

Analyzing the given reactions:
1. The first reaction is $\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{10} + \dfrac{13}{2}\text{O}_{2} \rightarrow 4\text{CO}_{2} + 5\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$. This is complete combustion of butane.
2. The second reaction is the oxidation of isobutane to tert-butyl alcohol using alkaline $\text{KMnO}_{4}$, which is a controlled oxidation, not combustion.
3. The third reaction is the controlled catalytic oxidation of methane to formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$), not combustion.
4. The fourth reaction is $\text{CH}_{4} + \text{O}_{2} \rightarrow \text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O(l)}$. Here, carbon is produced in the form of soot (solid carbon) instead of carbon dioxide, which is a characteristic feature of incomplete combustion of methane.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A Hydrocarbon [A] (molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_6$) on reaction with $\mathrm{Br}_2 / \mathrm{CCl}_4$ gave [B]. When [B] is heated with 2 moles of alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$, it gave compound [C]. 3 moles of Compound [C] when passed through red hot Iron tube forms [D]. Identify [D].
questions.solution:
The hydrocarbon [A] with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_6$ is propene, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2$.

Reaction of propene with $\mathrm{Br}_2 / \mathrm{CCl}_4$ is an electrophilic addition reaction, which yields 1,2-dibromopropane as compound [B]: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH(Br)}-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$.

Heating [B] with 2 moles of alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ results in dehydrohalogenation, which removes two molecules of $\mathrm{HBr}$ to form propyne, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{CH}$, as compound [C].

Passing 3 moles of propyne through a red hot iron tube at high temperature induces cyclic trimerization, a reaction analogous to the trimerization of acetylene to benzene. In the case of propyne, this reaction yields 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene (mesitylene) as compound [D].

Answer: 1, 3, 5- Trimethylbenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the products C, D and F formed in the following sets of reactions.
questions.solution:
The reaction of benzene ($C_{6}H_{6}$) with $Br_{2}/FeBr_{3}$ is an electrophilic aromatic substitution (bromination) which yields bromobenzene as product B.

Bromobenzene (B) is then subjected to nitration using $conc. HNO_{3}/H_{2}SO_{4}$. Since the bromine atom is ortho/para directing, the products C and D are o-nitrobromobenzene and p-nitrobromobenzene.

In the second pathway, benzene is first nitrated with $conc. HNO_{3}/H_{2}SO_{4}$ to yield nitrobenzene as product E. Nitrobenzene is a deactivating group and is meta-directing. Subsequent bromination of nitrobenzene with $Br_{2}/FeBr_{3}$ yields m-nitrobromobenzene as product F.

Comparing these results with the options, C and D are o-nitrobromobenzene and p-nitrobromobenzene, and F is m-nitrobromobenzene.

Answer: $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{o} \text {-nitrobromobenzene } \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{p} \text {-nitrobromobenzene } \mathrm{F}=\mathrm{m} \text {-nitrobromobenzene }$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are 4 reactions. Two of these reactions will give product which is an equimolar mixture of the d and 1 forms. Identify these 2 reactions.
[A] 2- Methylpropene  + $\mathrm{HI} \rightarrow$ ---------
[B] But-1-ene + $\mathrm{HBr} \rightarrow$ -----------
[C] 3-Methylbut-1-ene + $\mathrm{HI} \rightarrow$ -----------
[D] 3- Phenylpropene + $\mathrm{HBr}$ (Peroxide) \rightarrow  -----------
questions.solution:
For a racemic (equimolar d and l) mixture, the product must have a chiral center formed from an achiral reactant via a planar intermediate (carbocation).

[A] 2-Methylpropene + HI \to Markovnikov addition gives tertiary carbocation \to 2-iodo-2-methylpropane $CH_3 - C(I)(CH_3)_2$. Central carbon has three identical methyl groups \to achiral. No racemic mixture.

[B] But-1-ene + HBr \to Markovnikov addition gives secondary carbocation \to 2-bromobutane $CH_3 - CHBr - CH_2CH_3$. C-2 is bonded to H, Br, $CH_3$, and $C_2H_5\to$ chiral center. Attack from either face equally probable \to racemic mixture.

[C] 3-Methylbut-1-ene + HI \to Markovnikov addition gives secondary carbocation $CH_3 - CH^+ - CH(CH_3)_2\to$ iodide attacks to give 2-iodo-3-methylbutane with chiral center at C-2 \to racemic mixture.

[D] 3-Phenylpropene + HBr (peroxide) \to anti-Markovnikov (radical) addition \to Br adds to terminal carbon \to 1-bromo-3-phenylpropane $C_6H_5 - CH_2 - CH_2 - CH_2Br\to$ no chiral center \to achiral.

Reactions giving racemic mixture: B and C. Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their reactivity when each of them is reacted with chloroethane / anhydrous AlC$l_3$.
questions.solution:
The reaction of chloroethane with anhydrous $AlCl_{3}$ is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction. This reaction is an electrophilic aromatic substitution where the benzene ring acts as a nucleophile. The reactivity of the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution depends on the electron density of the ring. Electron-donating groups increase the electron density and thus increase the reactivity, while electron-withdrawing groups decrease the electron density and decrease the reactivity.

Let us analyze the substituents on the benzene rings:
Compound [A] is benzene, which has no substituents.
Compound [B] is bromobenzene. The $-Br$ group is deactivating due to its strong inductive effect ($-I$) which outweighs its resonance effect ($+M$) in terms of overall reactivity towards electrophilic substitution.
Compound [C] is p-xylene (1,4-dimethylbenzene). The two $-CH_{3}$ groups are electron-donating via inductive effect ($+I$) and hyperconjugation, significantly increasing the electron density of the ring.
Compound [D] is nitrobenzene. The $-NO_{2}$ group is a very strong electron-withdrawing group due to both $-I$ and $-M$ effects, making the ring highly deactivated.

Comparing the reactivity:
Nitrobenzene [D] is the least reactive due to the strong deactivating $-NO_{2}$ group.
Bromobenzene [B] is less reactive than benzene [A] because $-Br$ is deactivating.
Benzene [A] is less reactive than p-xylene [C] because p-xylene has two activating methyl groups.

Therefore, the increasing order of reactivity is D < B < A < C.

Answer: D < B < A < C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\text { Identify }[\mathrm{B}] \text { and }[\mathrm{C}] \text { formed in the reactions given below. }$
questions.solution:
The starting material is $C_{3}H_{4}Br_{4}$. This is a tetrabromo derivative of propane. Reaction with Zn dust (dehalogenation) leads to the formation of an alkyne. Specifically, $CH_{3}-CBr_{2}-CHBr_{2}$ or $CH_{2}Br-CHBr-CH_{2}Br$ (though the formula $C_{3}H_{4}Br_{4}$ corresponds to $CH_{3}-CBr_{2}-CHBr_{2}$ or similar isomers) reacts with Zn dust to form propyne ($CH_{3}-C \equiv CH$) as product [B].

The reaction of propyne with $Hg^{2+}/H^{+}$ (Kucherov reaction) involves the hydration of the alkyne. The alkyne $CH_{3}-C \equiv CH$ undergoes hydration to form an enol intermediate, which tautomerizes to form propanone ($CH_{3}-CO-CH_{3}$) as product [C].

Propanone contains the $CH_{3}CO-$ group, which gives a positive iodoform test. Thus, [B] is propyne and [C] is propanone.

Answer: [B] Propyne [C] Propanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following compounds shows Geometrical isomerism?
questions.solution:
Geometrical isomerism occurs in alkenes when each carbon atom of the double bond is attached to two different groups. We analyze the structure of each compound:

2-Methylhex-2-ene: $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$. The carbon at position 2 is bonded to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

4-Methylhex-2-ene: $CH_3-CH=CH-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$. The carbon at position 2 is bonded to a hydrogen and a methyl group. The carbon at position 3 is bonded to a hydrogen and a sec-butyl group. Since both carbons of the double bond have different groups attached, this compound exhibits geometrical isomerism.

4-Methylhex-1-ene: $CH_2=CH-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$. The terminal carbon (position 1) is bonded to two identical hydrogen atoms, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

2-Methylhex-1-ene: $CH_2=C(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$. The terminal carbon (position 1) is bonded to two identical hydrogen atoms, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

Answer: 4-Methylhex-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An unsaturated hydrocarbon $[\mathrm{A}]$ reacts with $\mathrm{HBr}$ in presence of Benzoyl peroxide to yield [B]
Compound [A] when reacted with cold, dilute alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ gave compound [C], 2-Methylbutane-2, 3-diol But when [A] is reacted with hot $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$, it yielded $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ and a compound [D] Identify compounds [A], [B] and [D]
questions.solution:
Compound [A] reacts with cold, dilute alkaline $\text{KMnO}_{4}$ to form 2-methylbutane-2,3-diol. This reaction is a syn-hydroxylation of an alkene. The structure of 2-methylbutane-2,3-diol is $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(OH)(CH}_{3})-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_{3}$. The corresponding alkene [A] is 2-methylbut-2-ene, which has the structure $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(CH}_{3})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_{3}$.

Reaction of 2-methylbut-2-ene with hot $\text{KMnO}_{4}$ (oxidative cleavage) breaks the double bond: $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(CH}_{3})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_{3} \xrightarrow{\text{hot KMnO}_{4}} \text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH}_{3} + \text{CH}_{3}-\text{COOH}$. Here, $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{COOH}$ is acetic acid and [D] is propanone ($\text{CH}_{3}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_{3}$).

Reaction of 2-methylbut-2-ene with $\text{HBr}$ in the presence of benzoyl peroxide follows anti-Markovnikov addition. The radical mechanism leads to the formation of 2-bromo-3-methylbutane, as the bromine radical adds to the less substituted carbon of the double bond to form the more stable secondary radical intermediate.

Answer: [A] 2-Methylbut-2-ene [B] 2-Bromo-3-methylbutane [D] Propanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An aromatic hydrocarbon $[\mathrm{A}]\left(\mathrm{Molecular}\right.$ formula $\left.\mathrm{C}_9 \mathrm{H}_{12}\right)$, undergoes air oxidation followed by reaction with dil.
$\mathrm{HCl}$ to give [B] as one of the products
Compound [B] forms a white precipitate on treatment with $\mathrm{Br}_2(\mathrm{aq})$
Sodium salt of [B] reacts with $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at $400 \mathrm{~K}$ under high pressure followed by acid hydrolysis to give [C]
Compound [C] reacts with acetic anhydride / conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ to form [D]
Identify compound $[\mathrm{D}]$
questions.solution:
The aromatic hydrocarbon [A] with molecular formula $C_9H_{12}$ that undergoes air oxidation (cumene process) is isopropylbenzene (cumene).

Air oxidation of cumene followed by treatment with dilute $HCl$ yields phenol and acetone as products. Compound [B] is phenol ($C_6H_5OH$), which forms a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol on treatment with $Br_2(aq)$.

The sodium salt of phenol (sodium phenoxide) reacts with $CO_2$ at $400 K$ under high pressure followed by acid hydrolysis (Kolbe-Schmitt reaction) to give salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) as compound [C].

Compound [C] (salicylic acid) reacts with acetic anhydride in the presence of conc. $H_2SO_4$ (acetylation) to form aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid), which is 2-acetoxybenzoic acid. This corresponds to the structure with a benzene ring having a $COOH$ group and an $OCOCH_3$ group at ortho positions.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of mono-chloro derivatives of Ethyl cyclohexane possible?
questions.solution:
Ethyl cyclohexane has the molecular formula $C_8H_{16}$. The structure consists of a cyclohexane ring with an ethyl group attached at one position.

The positions available for substitution are:
1. The alpha-carbon of the ethyl group (1 position).
2. The beta-carbon of the ethyl group (1 position).
3. The ring carbons: The carbon attached to the ethyl group (1 position), the ortho positions (2 equivalent positions), the meta positions (2 equivalent positions), and the para position (1 position).

Counting the distinct positions for chlorine substitution:
1. Alpha-carbon of ethyl group: 1 isomer.
2. Beta-carbon of ethyl group: 1 isomer.
3. Ring carbon attached to ethyl group: 1 isomer.
4. Ortho position on ring: 1 isomer.
5. Meta position on ring: 1 isomer.
6. Para position on ring: 1 isomer.

Total number of mono-chloro derivatives = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6.

Answer: 6

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
From among the following, identify the compound which forms two moles of a ketone on ozonolysis.
[A] 2,3-Dimethylbutane.
[B] 3-Methyl-1-pentene.
[C] 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butene.
[D] 2-Methyl-2-pentane.
questions.solution:
Ozonolysis of an alkene involves the cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond to form carbonyl compounds. The general reaction is $R_1R_2C=CR_3R_4 \xrightarrow{O_3, Zn/H_2O} R_1R_2C=O + R_3R_4C=O$.

For the product to be two moles of a ketone, the alkene must be symmetric and substituted such that each carbon of the double bond is attached to two alkyl groups.

Analyzing the options:
[A] 2,3-Dimethylbutane is an alkane and does not undergo ozonolysis.
[B] 3-Methyl-1-pentene is $CH_2=CH-CH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3$. Ozonolysis yields formaldehyde ($HCHO$) and 2-methylbutanal.
[C] 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butene is $(CH_3)_2C=C(CH_3)_2$. Ozonolysis yields two moles of acetone ($CH_3COCH_3$), which is a ketone.
[D] 2-Methyl-2-pentene (assuming the intended structure) is $(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH_2CH_3$. Ozonolysis yields acetone and propanal.

Answer: [C]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The conversion of Propyne to Benzene can be brought out in 4 steps.
Choose the reagents to be used, in the proper sequential order, to bring out the conversion.
Reagents provided: alc. $\mathrm{KOH}, \mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{Pd}, \mathrm{Na} /$ dry ether, $\mathrm{HBr}, \mathrm{HBr} /\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CO}\right)_2 \mathrm{O}_2$,
Soda-lime, $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ (high T and P), Conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$
questions.solution:
The conversion of propyne ($CH_3-C \equiv CH$) to benzene ($C_6H_6$) involves the following steps:

Partial hydrogenation of propyne to propene using $H_2 / Pd$ (Lindlar catalyst or poisoned Pd).
$CH_3-C \equiv CH + H_2 \xrightarrow{Pd} CH_3-CH=CH_2$

Anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr to propene using peroxide ($HBr / (C_6H_5CO)_2O_2$) to obtain 1-bromopropane.
$CH_3-CH=CH_2 + HBr \xrightarrow{peroxide} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Br$

Wurtz reaction using $Na / dry ether$ to convert 1-bromopropane to n-hexane.
$2 CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Br + 2 Na \xrightarrow{dry ether} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$

Aromatization of n-hexane to benzene using $Cr_2O_3$ at high temperature and pressure.
$CH_3(CH_2)_4CH_3 \xrightarrow{Cr_2O_3, \Delta, P} C_6H_6 + 4H_2$

Answer: $\mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{Pd}, \mathrm{HBr} /\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CO}\right)_2 \mathrm{O}_2, \mathrm{Na} /$ dry ether, $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ (high $\mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{P}$)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagents $\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}$ and $\mathrm{Z}$ used to bring out the following reactions.
questions.solution:
The conversion of 2-phenylpropane (cumene) to phenol ($C_6H_5OH$) is a standard industrial process known as the cumene process. In this process, cumene is first oxidized to cumene hydroperoxide using air (or $O_2$), followed by acid-catalyzed cleavage using dilute $H_2SO_4$ to yield phenol and acetone. Thus, X = Air and Y = dil. $H_2SO_4$.

The second step involves the oxidation of phenol to p-benzoquinone. This transformation is typically achieved using strong oxidizing agents such as chromic acid ($H_2CrO_4$) or dichromate ions in acidic medium ($Cr_2O_7^{2-} / H^{+}$). Therefore, Z = $Cr_2O_7^{2-} / H^{+}$.

Comparing these reagents with the given options, the correct set is X = Air, Y = dil. $H_2SO_4$, and Z = $Cr_2O_7^{2-} / H^{+}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{X}=\text { Air } \quad \mathrm{Y}=\text { dil. } \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 \quad \mathrm{Z}=\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7{ }^{2-} / \mathrm{H}^{+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following will show geometrical isomerism?
questions.solution:
Geometrical isomerism is exhibited by alkenes if both carbon atoms of the double bond are attached to two different groups.

For 2-methylbut-2-ene, the structure is $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3$. One carbon of the double bond is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

For 1,2-dibromopropene, the structure is $CH_3-C(Br)=CH-Br$. The first carbon is attached to a methyl group and a bromine atom, while the second carbon is attached to a hydrogen atom and a bromine atom. Since both carbons have two different groups attached, it exhibits geometrical isomerism.

For cyclohexene, the ring strain prevents the formation of a trans-isomer in a six-membered ring, and it exists only in the cis-form.

For 2-methylpropene, the structure is $(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$. The first carbon is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

Answer: 1,2-dibromopropene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Total number of $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds in ethene molecule is
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of ethene is $C_{2}H_{4}$. The structural formula is $CH_{2}=CH_{2}$.

In the molecule, there are four $C-H$ single bonds and one $C=C$ double bond.

Each single bond consists of one $\sigma$ bond. Thus, there are four $\sigma$ bonds from the $C-H$ bonds.

The $C=C$ double bond consists of one $\sigma$ bond and one $\pi$ bond.

Total $\sigma$ bonds = $4$ (from $C-H$) + $1$ (from $C=C$) = $5\sigma$ bonds.

Total $\pi$ bonds = $1$ (from $C=C$) = $1\pi$ bond.

Answer: $5 \sigma$ and $1 \pi$ bonds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ammoniacal silver nitrate forms a white precipitate easily with
questions.solution:
Ammoniacal silver nitrate, also known as Tollens reagent, reacts with terminal alkynes to form a white precipitate of silver acetylide.

The general reaction is $R-C\equiv CH + [Ag(NH_3)_2]^+ OH^- \rightarrow R-C\equiv C-Ag \downarrow + 2NH_3 + H_2O$.

Among the given options, $\mathrm{CH}_3 C\equiv CH$ (propyne) is a terminal alkyne, meaning it has an acidic hydrogen atom attached to the triply bonded carbon.

The other compounds, $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2$ (propene), $\mathrm{CH}_3 C\equiv CCH_3$ (but-2-yne, an internal alkyne), and $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}_2$ (ethene), do not possess an acidic terminal hydrogen atom and therefore do not form a precipitate with ammoniacal silver nitrate.

Answer: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What can be $A$ and $B$ in the following reaction?
questions.solution:
The conversion of propene ($\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}=\text{CH}_{2}$) to 1-bromopropane ($\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Br}$) is an anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr. This reaction occurs in the presence of organic peroxides (Kharasch effect or peroxide effect). Thus, reagent A is $\text{HBr}$ with peroxide.

The conversion of 1-bromopropane ($\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Br}$) to propan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{OH}$) is a nucleophilic substitution reaction. Alkyl halides react with aqueous potassium hydroxide ($\text{aq. KOH}$) under heating to undergo hydrolysis, yielding the corresponding alcohol. Thus, reagent B is $\text{aq. KOH}, \Delta$.

Comparing these with the given options, reagent A is $\text{HBr}$, Peroxide and reagent B is $\text{aq. KOH}, \Delta$.

Answer: A. $\mathrm{HBr}$, Peroxide $\quad$ B. aq. $\mathrm{KOH}, \Delta$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Coupling reaction is an example of
questions.solution:
Coupling reactions, such as the formation of azo dyes from diazonium salts and aromatic compounds (like phenols or amines), involve the attack of a diazonium cation on an electron-rich aromatic ring.

The diazonium cation, $Ar-N_{2}^{+}$, acts as a weak electrophile. It attacks the electron-rich aromatic ring, which acts as a nucleophile.

This process results in the replacement of a hydrogen atom on the aromatic ring by the diazonium group, which is a characteristic feature of electrophilic aromatic substitution.

Therefore, the coupling reaction is classified as an electrophilic substitution reaction.

Answer: electrophilic substitution reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The hydrocarbon that cannot be prepared effectively by Wurtz reaction
questions.solution:
The Wurtz reaction $2R$-$X + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} R$-$R + 2NaX$ is effective only for symmetrical alkanes (even carbon count). Using two different alkyl halides gives a mixture of three products (R-R, R-R', R'-R'), making it ineffective for unsymmetrical alkanes.

(1) 2,7-dimethyloctane: Symmetrical — can be split into two identical isopentyl fragments. Can be prepared effectively.

(3) 1,4-dicyclohexylbutane: Symmetrical around the center. Can be prepared effectively.

(4): Symmetrical structure with two identical cyclopentyl-cyclohexyl fragments. Can be prepared effectively.

(2) 2,5-dimethylheptane: Unsymmetrical with 9 carbons (odd number). Cannot be split into two identical alkyl fragments, so it requires two different alkyl halides, yielding a mixture of products.

The hydrocarbon that cannot be prepared effectively by Wurtz reaction is option (2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Para and ortho hydrogen differ in:
questions.solution:
Hydrogen gas exists in two isomeric forms known as ortho-hydrogen and para-hydrogen.

In ortho-hydrogen, the spins of the two nuclei (protons) are in the same direction (parallel).

In para-hydrogen, the spins of the two nuclei (protons) are in opposite directions (antiparallel).

Both forms have the same atomic number, the same number of neutrons (zero in the case of protium), and the same size, as they are both molecules of $H_2$.

Therefore, they differ only in the relative orientation of the nuclear spins.

Answer: Spins of protons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Decomposition of hydrogen peroxide can be prevented by adding
questions.solution:
The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide ($H_2O_2$) is a catalytic reaction that is often accelerated by impurities, dust, or metal surfaces. To stabilize $H_2O_2$ and prevent its decomposition, negative catalysts or stabilizers are added to the solution.

Acetanilide, phosphoric acid, and urea are commonly used as stabilizers for hydrogen peroxide. These substances act by inhibiting the catalytic activity of trace metal ions that would otherwise promote the decomposition of $H_2O_2$ into water and oxygen.

Among the given options, urea acts as a stabilizer for hydrogen peroxide.

Answer: urea

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect for $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ structure?
options: It has an open book structure.
It $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length is 145.8 and $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ is 98.8 .
questions.solution:
The structure of hydrogen peroxide ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2$) is non-planar and is commonly described as an open book structure.

In the gaseous phase, the dihedral angle between the two O-H planes is approximately $111.5^{\circ}$, not $180^{\circ}$. A dihedral angle of $180^{\circ}$ would imply a planar structure, which is not the case for $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2$.

The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length in $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2$ is $145.8$ pm and the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond length is $98.8$ pm.

The dihedral angle (angle between the two planes containing the O-H bonds) in the solid state is $90.2^{\circ}$.

Since the dihedral angle is not $180^{\circ}$, the statement that its dihedral angle is $180^{\circ}$ is incorrect.

Answer: Its dihedral angle is $180^{\circ}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the hydrides of group 15 in correct decreasing order of reducing nature.
questions.solution:
The reducing nature of the hydrides of group 15 elements depends on the stability of the M-H bond. As we move down the group from N to Bi, the atomic size of the central atom increases, which leads to a decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy of the M-H bond.

The bond strength decreases in the order $\mathrm{NH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{PH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{AsH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{SbH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{BiH}_{3}$.

Since the reducing character is directly proportional to the ease of releasing hydrogen atoms, the reducing nature increases as the bond strength decreases. Therefore, the correct decreasing order of reducing nature is $\mathrm{BiH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{SbH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{AsH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{PH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{NH}_{3}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{BiH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{SbH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{AsH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{PH}_{3} \gt \mathrm{NH}_{3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At 30°C the solubility of PbI_2$ salt in 0.2 M KI solution will be X, if the solubility product of PbI_2$ at 30°C is $2.4 \times 10^{-8}$. Identify the value of X.
questions.solution:
The dissociation of $PbI_2$ is given by:

$PbI_2(s) \rightleftharpoons Pb^{2+}(aq) + 2I^-(aq)$

Let the solubility of $PbI_2$ in $0.2$ M $KI$ solution be $s$.

The concentration of $I^-$ ions from $KI$ is $0.2$ M. Since $KI$ is a strong electrolyte, it completely dissociates. The total concentration of $I^-$ ions is $(2s + 0.2)$ M. Because $K_{sp}$ is very small, $2s$ can be neglected compared to $0.2$.

$[I^-] \approx 0.2$ M

The expression for the solubility product is:

$K_{sp} = [Pb^{2+}][I^-]^2$

Substituting the given values:

$2.4 \times 10^{-8} = s \times (0.2)^2$

$2.4 \times 10^{-8} = s \times 0.04$

$s = \dfrac{2.4 \times 10^{-8}}{0.04} = 6.0 \times 10^{-7}$ M

Thus, the solubility $X$ is $6.0 \times 10^{-7}$ M.

Answer: $6.0 \times 10^{-7}$M

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A buffer solution was prepared by mixing 5 g of acetic acid with 7.5 g of sodium acetate. The solution was made upto 500 mL . The pH of the resulting solution is:
$\left[p K_a=4.76\right]$
questions.solution:
The molar mass of acetic acid ($CH_{3}COOH$) is $60\text{ g/mol}$. The number of moles of acetic acid is $n_{acid} = \dfrac{5}{60} = \dfrac{1}{12}\text{ mol}$.

The molar mass of sodium acetate ($CH_{3}COONa$) is $82\text{ g/mol}$. The number of moles of sodium acetate is $n_{salt} = \dfrac{7.5}{82} \approx 0.09146\text{ mol}$.

Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer: $pH = pK_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{[salt]}{[acid]} \right)$.

Since the volume is the same for both components in the $500\text{ mL}$ solution, the ratio of concentrations is equal to the ratio of moles: $pH = pK_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{n_{salt}}{n_{acid}} \right)$.

$pH = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{7.5/82}{5/60} \right) = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{7.5}{82} \times \dfrac{60}{5} \right) = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{1.5 \times 60}{82} \right) = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{90}{82} \right)$.

$pH = 4.76 + \log(1.0976) \approx 4.76 + 0.04 = 4.8$.

Answer: 4.8

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ionisation constant of the weak acid HF whose concentration is $0.1\text{ M}$ is $3.5 \times 10^{-4}$. The Equilibrium constant value for the reaction $\text{F}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HF} + \text{OH}^-$ is _____ and the pH of aqueous solution of the weak acid is _____.
questions.solution:
The reaction $F^- + H_2O \rightleftharpoons HF + OH^-$ is hydrolysis of the conjugate base, so $K_{eq} = K_b = \dfrac{K_w}{K_a}$:

$K_{eq} = \dfrac{1.0 \times 10^{-14}}{3.5 \times 10^{-4}} \approx 2.86 \times 10^{-11}$

For pH, using $[H^+] \approx \sqrt{K_a \cdot C}$:

$[H^+] = \sqrt{3.5 \times 10^{-4} \times 0.1} = \sqrt{3.5 \times 10^{-5}} \approx 5.92 \times 10^{-3}$ M

$pH = -\log(5.92 \times 10^{-3}) \approx 2.23$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What volume of $0.2 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ needs to be added to $100 \mathrm{ml}$ of $0.4 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COONa}^2$ solution to prepare a buffer of pH equal to 4.91 ? ($\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ is 4.76)
questions.solution:
The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer is given by:

$\text{pH} = \text{pK}_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} \right)$

Given $\text{pH} = 4.91$, $\text{pK}_{a} = 4.76$, and the concentration of salt $[\text{CH}_{3}\text{COONa}] = 0.4 \text{ M}$ with volume $V_{s} = 100 \text{ ml}$.

Substituting the values into the equation:

$4.91 = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{n_{\text{salt}}}{n_{\text{acid}}} \right)$

$0.15 = \log \left( \dfrac{0.4 \times 100}{0.2 \times V_{a}} \right)$

Taking the antilog of both sides:

$10^{0.15} = \dfrac{40}{0.2 \times V_{a}}$

$1.4125 = \dfrac{40}{0.2 \times V_{a}}$

$0.2 \times V_{a} = \dfrac{40}{1.4125}$

$0.2 \times V_{a} = 28.3186$

$V_{a} = \dfrac{28.3186}{0.2} = 141.59 \text{ ml}$

Answer: 141.59 ml

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Solubility product of the sparingly soluble salt $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ in aqueous medium is $9.3 \times 10^{-10}$ Calculate the mass in gram of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ present in 100 ml of its saturated solution.
(Molar mass of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ is $236 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ )
questions.solution:
The solubility equilibrium for $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ is given by:
$\mathrm{AgBrO}_3(s) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Ag}^{+}(aq) + \mathrm{BrO}_3^{-}(aq)$

Let $s$ be the solubility of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ in mol/L. Then $[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}] = s$ and $[\mathrm{BrO}_3^{-}] = s$.

The solubility product constant $K_{sp}$ is defined as:
$K_{sp} = [\mathrm{Ag}^{+}][\mathrm{BrO}_3^{-}] = s^2$

Given $K_{sp} = 9.3 \times 10^{-10}$, we have:
$s = \sqrt{9.3 \times 10^{-10}} = \sqrt{93 \times 10^{-11}} = \sqrt{9.3} \times 10^{-5} \approx 3.04959 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol/L}$

The volume of the solution is $100 \text{ ml} = 0.1 \text{ L}$.

The number of moles of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ in $0.1 \text{ L}$ is:
$n = s \times V = 3.04959 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol/L} \times 0.1 \text{ L} = 3.04959 \times 10^{-6} \text{ mol}$

The molar mass of $\mathrm{AgBrO}_3$ is $236 \text{ g/mol}$. The mass $m$ is:
$m = n \times \text{Molar Mass} = 3.04959 \times 10^{-6} \text{ mol} \times 236 \text{ g/mol}$
$m = 719.705 \times 10^{-6} \text{ g} = 7.19705 \times 10^{-4} \text{ g}$

Answer: $7.197 \times 10^{-4}$

questions.q: The pH at which an acid indicator with $K_\alpha=1 \times 10^{-5}$ changes colour when the indicator concentration is $1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$ is
questions.solution:
An acid indicator is a weak acid. It dissociates
$\underset{\text { Colour } A}{\operatorname{HIn}} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}^{+}+\underset{\text { Colour } B}{\operatorname{In}^{-}}$
$K_{\mathrm{In}}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]\left[\mathrm{In}^{-}\right]}{[\mathrm{HIn}]}$
The indicator HIn will show a colour change at mid point, i.e. the point at which $\left[\mathrm{In}^{-}\right]=[\mathrm{HIn}]$
Hence, $K_{\mathrm{in}}=\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=10^{-5}$
or $\quad \mathrm{pH}=5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $1 \mathrm{~cm}^3 \text { of } 0.01 \mathrm{~M} \mathrm{~HCl} \text { is added to } 1 \mathrm{~L} \text { of } \mathrm{NaCl} \text { solution. The } \mathrm{pH} \text { of the resulting solution is: }$
questions.solution:
The volume of the HCl solution added is $V_1 = 1 \text{ cm}^3 = 1 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L}$.

The concentration of the HCl solution is $M_1 = 0.01 \text{ M} = 10^{-2} \text{ M}$.

The total volume of the resulting solution is $V_2 = 1 \text{ L} + 0.001 \text{ L} \approx 1 \text{ L}$.

The number of moles of $\text{H}^{+}$ ions added is $n = M_1 \times V_1 = 10^{-2} \text{ mol/L} \times 10^{-3} \text{ L} = 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

The concentration of $\text{H}^{+}$ ions in the final solution is $[\text{H}^{+}] = \dfrac{n}{V_2} = \dfrac{10^{-5} \text{ mol}}{1 \text{ L}} = 10^{-5} \text{ M}$.

The pH of the solution is given by $\text{pH} = -\log[\text{H}^{+}] = -\log(10^{-5}) = 5$.

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What volume of $0.2 \mathrm{~M}$ Acetic acid is to be added to $100 \mathrm{ml}$ of $0.4 \mathrm{M}$ Sodium acetate so that a Buffer solution of $\mathrm{pH}$ equal to 4.94 is obtained? $(\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}=4.76)$
questions.solution:
The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer is given by:

$\text{pH} = \text{pK}_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} \right)$

Given $\text{pH} = 4.94$, $\text{pK}_{a} = 4.76$, and the volume of salt ($V_{s}$) = $100 \text{ ml}$ with concentration ($M_{s}$) = $0.4 \text{ M}$. Let the volume of acid be $V_{a}$ with concentration ($M_{a}$) = $0.2 \text{ M}$.

Substituting the values into the equation:

$4.94 = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{M_{s} V_{s} / (V_{s} + V_{a})}{M_{a} V_{a} / (V_{s} + V_{a})} \right)$

$4.94 - 4.76 = \log \left( \dfrac{0.4 \times 100}{0.2 \times V_{a}} \right)$

$0.18 = \log \left( \dfrac{40}{0.2 V_{a}} \right)$

Taking the antilog of both sides ($10^{0.18} \approx 1.5136$):

$1.5136 = \dfrac{40}{0.2 V_{a}}$

$0.2 V_{a} = \dfrac{40}{1.5136}$

$0.2 V_{a} \approx 26.427$

$V_{a} = \dfrac{26.427}{0.2} = 132.135 \text{ ml}$

Answer: 132.1 ml

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $300 \mathrm{ml}$ of an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ with $\mathrm{pH}$ value of 10 is mixed with $200 \mathrm{ml}$ of an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{HCl}$ with a $\mathrm{pH}$ value of 4. What will be the $\mathrm{pH}$ of the resultant solution at room temperature?
questions.solution:
For the NaOH solution, $\text{pH} = 10$, so $\text{pOH} = 14 - 10 = 4$.

$[\text{OH}^{-}] = 10^{-4} \text{ M}$.

Moles of $\text{OH}^{-} = 300 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L} \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol/L} = 3 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

For the HCl solution, $\text{pH} = 4$, so $[\text{H}^{+}] = 10^{-4} \text{ M}$.

Moles of $\text{H}^{+} = 200 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L} \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol/L} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

Since $\text{OH}^{-}$ reacts with $\text{H}^{+}$ to form water, the remaining moles of $\text{OH}^{-}$ are $3 \times 10^{-5} - 2 \times 10^{-5} = 1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

Total volume of the mixture $= 300 \text{ ml} + 200 \text{ ml} = 500 \text{ ml} = 0.5 \text{ L}$.

Resultant concentration of $\text{OH}^{-} = \dfrac{1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}}{0.5 \text{ L}} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ M}$.

$\text{pOH} = -\log(2 \times 10^{-5}) = 5 - \log 2 = 5 - 0.301 = 4.699$.

$\text{pH} = 14 - 4.699 = 9.301$.

Answer: 9.301

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{~B}_4$ is a sparingly soluble salt with a solubility of $\mathrm{s} g / \mathrm{L}$. If the Molar mass of $\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{~B}_4$ is $\mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{mol}$, what is the expression for its $\mathrm{K}_{\text {sp }}$ ?
questions.solution:
The salt $\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{B}_4$ dissociates in water as follows:

$\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{B}_4 (s) \rightleftharpoons 3 \mathrm{A}^{4+} (aq) + 4 \mathrm{B}^{3-} (aq)$

The solubility of the salt is given as $s$ g/L. The molar mass of the salt is $M$ g/mol. Therefore, the molar solubility $S$ in mol/L is given by:

$S = \dfrac{s}{M}$ mol/L

From the stoichiometry of the dissociation, the concentration of $\mathrm{A}^{4+}$ is $3S$ and the concentration of $\mathrm{B}^{3-}$ is $4S$.

The solubility product constant $K_{sp}$ is defined as:

$K_{sp} = [\mathrm{A}^{4+}]^3 [\mathrm{B}^{3-}]^4$

Substituting the concentrations in terms of $S$:

$K_{sp} = (3S)^3 (4S)^4$

$K_{sp} = (27 S^3) (256 S^4)$

$K_{sp} = 27 \times 256 \times S^7$

$K_{sp} = 6912 S^7$

Substituting $S = \dfrac{s}{M}$:

$K_{sp} = 6912 \left( \dfrac{s}{M} \right)^7$

Answer: $6912(\mathrm{~s} / \mathrm{M})^7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What would be the volume of water required to dissolve $0.2 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{PbCl}_2$ of molar mass $278 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ to prepare a saturated solution of the salt? $(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{SP}}$ of $\mathrm{PbCl}_2=3.2 \times 10^{-8})$
questions.solution:
The solubility equilibrium for $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ is given by $\text{PbCl}_{2}(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{Pb}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{Cl}^{-}(aq)$.

Let $s$ be the solubility of $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ in mol/L. Then $[\text{Pb}^{2+}] = s$ and $[\text{Cl}^{-}] = 2s$.

The solubility product constant is $K_{sp} = [\text{Pb}^{2+}][\text{Cl}^{-}]^{2} = s(2s)^{2} = 4s^{3}$.

Given $K_{sp} = 3.2 \times 10^{-8}$, we have $4s^{3} = 3.2 \times 10^{-8} \Rightarrow s^{3} = 0.8 \times 10^{-8} = 8 \times 10^{-9}$.

Taking the cube root, $s = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol/L}$.

The number of moles of $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ in $0.2 \text{ g}$ is $n = \dfrac{0.2 \text{ g}}{278 \text{ g/mol}} \approx 7.194 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$.

The volume $V$ required to dissolve this amount is $V = \dfrac{n}{s} = \dfrac{7.194 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}}{2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol/L}} = 0.3597 \text{ L}$.

Converting to milliliters, $V = 0.3597 \times 1000 \text{ ml} = 359.7 \text{ ml}$.

Answer: 359.7 ml

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A buffer solution has equal volumes of $0.1 \mathrm{~M} \mathrm{~NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ and $0.01 \mathrm{~M} \mathrm{~NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$. The $\mathrm{pK}_b$ of the base is 5. The $\mathrm{pH}$ is
questions.solution:
The buffer solution consists of a weak base $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ and its salt $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$. The concentration of the base $[\text{B}]$ is $0.1 \text{ M}$ and the concentration of the salt $[\text{BH}^+]$ is $0.01 \text{ M}$ after mixing equal volumes, as the dilution factor is the same for both.

Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for a basic buffer:

$\text{pOH} = \text{pK}_b + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]} \right)$

Given $\text{pK}_b = 5$, $[\text{salt}] = 0.01 \text{ M}$, and $[\text{base}] = 0.1 \text{ M}$:

$\text{pOH} = 5 + \log \left( \dfrac{0.01}{0.1} \right)$

$\text{pOH} = 5 + \log(10^{-1}) = 5 - 1 = 4$

The relationship between $\text{pH}$ and $\text{pOH}$ at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$ is $\text{pH} + \text{pOH} = 14$.

$\text{pH} = 14 - \text{pOH} = 14 - 4 = 10$

Answer: 10

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a $0.2 \mathrm{~M}$ aqueous solution, lactic acid is $6.9 \%$ dissociated. The value of dissociation constant is
questions.solution:
For a weak acid dissociation $HA \rightleftharpoons H^{+} + A^{-}$, the dissociation constant $K_a$ is given by the expression $K_a = \dfrac{c \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$.

Given concentration $c = 0.2 \text{ M}$ and degree of dissociation $\alpha = 6.9 \% = 0.069$.

Since $\alpha$ is small, we can approximate $1 - \alpha \approx 1$, so $K_a \approx c \alpha^2$.

Substituting the values: $K_a = 0.2 \times (0.069)^2$.

$K_a = 0.2 \times 0.004761 = 0.0009522$.

Expressing in scientific notation, $K_a = 9.522 \times 10^{-4} \approx 9.5 \times 10^{-4}$.

Answer: $9.5 \times 10^{-4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\mathrm{pH}$ of $10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$ solution of $\mathrm{KOH}$ is.
questions.solution:
KOH is a strong base, which dissociates completely in aqueous solution as follows:

$\mathrm{KOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{K}^{+} + \mathrm{OH}^{-}$

The concentration of hydroxide ions is equal to the concentration of the KOH solution:

$[\mathrm{OH}^{-}] = 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$

The pOH of the solution is calculated using the formula:

$\mathrm{pOH} = -\log[\mathrm{OH}^{-}] = -\log(10^{-3}) = 3$

Using the relation $\mathrm{pH} + \mathrm{pOH} = 14$ at $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$:

$\mathrm{pH} = 14 - \mathrm{pOH} = 14 - 3 = 11$

Answer: 11

questions.q: The order of acidic strength of boron trihalides is
questions.solution: Boron trihalides are Lewis acids. The back bonding determines its acidic strength, more is the $\pi$-back bonding, less is the acidity. Thus, due to better overlapping of orbitals it promotes better $\pi$-back bonding, hence $\mathrm{BF}_3$ is least acidic in nature. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Find the correct matches of the substances, given in Column I, from their characteristic properties given in Column II.
S.No.Column IS.No.Column II
WTlADecomposes steam to form its dioxide and dihydrogen gas.
X$CCl_4$BConsists of twenty 6-membered rings and twelve 5 membered rings.
YTinC+3 oxidation state is highly oxidising.

questions.solution:
Thallium (Tl) belongs to Group 13. Due to the inert pair effect, the +1 oxidation state is more stable than the +3 oxidation state. Consequently, the +3 oxidation state of Tl is highly oxidising, which matches property C.

Carbon tetrachloride (CCl_{4}$) has a central carbon atom bonded to four chlorine atoms. It has a complete octet and no lone pairs, making it an electron-precise species that acts neither as an electron donor nor as an electron acceptor. This matches property A. \\ \\ Fullerene (C_{60}$) is a cage-like molecule consisting of twenty 6-membered rings and twelve 5-membered rings, which matches property B.

Therefore, the correct mapping is W=C, X=D, Y=A, Z=B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The order of acidic strength of boron trihalides is
questions.solution:
Boron trihalides are Lewis acids because the boron atom is electron-deficient, having only six electrons in its valence shell. The acidic strength depends on the extent of back-bonding between the lone pair of the halogen atom and the empty $2p$ orbital of the boron atom.

The back-bonding involves the overlap of the $2p$ orbital of boron with the $np$ orbital of the halogen. The extent of this overlap is maximum for $\mathrm{BF}_3$ because both boron and fluorine have $2p$ orbitals, leading to effective $p\pi-p\pi$ back-bonding. This reduces the electron deficiency of boron significantly.

As the size of the halogen increases from fluorine to iodine, the energy gap between the boron $2p$ orbital and the halogen $np$ orbital increases, and the overlap becomes less effective. Consequently, the extent of back-bonding decreases in the order $\mathrm{BF}_3 \gt \mathrm{BCl}_3 \gt \mathrm{BBr}_3 \gt \mathrm{BI}_3$.

Since back-bonding reduces the Lewis acidity, the acidic strength follows the reverse order: $\mathrm{BF}_3 \lt \mathrm{BCl}_3 \lt \mathrm{BBr}_3 \lt \mathrm{BI}_3$.

Answer: $\mathrm{BF}_3\lt \mathrm{BCl}_3\lt \mathrm{BBr}_3\lt \mathrm{BI}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The increasing order of atomic radii of the following group 13 elements is
questions.solution:
The group 13 elements are Boron (B), Aluminium (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In), and Thallium (Tl).

Moving down the group, the atomic radius generally increases due to the addition of new electron shells.

However, there is an anomaly between Aluminium (Al) and Gallium (Ga). Gallium follows the 3d transition series, which contains electrons that provide poor shielding of the nuclear charge. This results in a higher effective nuclear charge for Gallium, causing its atomic radius to be slightly smaller than that of Aluminium.

The atomic radii values are approximately: Al (143 pm), Ga (135 pm), In (167 pm), and Tl (170 pm).

Therefore, the increasing order of atomic radii is $\mathrm{Ga} \lt \mathrm{Al} \lt \mathrm{In} \lt \mathrm{Tl}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Ga} \lt \mathrm{Al} \lt \mathrm{In} \lt \mathrm{Tl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is NOT in accordance with the property stated against it?
options: $HI  \gt  HBr  \gt  HCl  \gt  HF$ [Acidic Property in Water]
questions.solution:
The oxidising power of halogens decreases down the group: $F_2 \gt Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt I_2$.

The acidic strength of hydrogen halides in water increases down the group due to a decrease in bond dissociation enthalpy: $HI \gt HBr \gt HCl \gt HF$.

Electronegativity decreases down the group: $F \gt Cl \gt Br \gt I$.

The bond dissociation energy of halogens does not follow a regular trend. Due to strong interelectronic repulsions between the lone pairs on the small fluorine atoms, the $F-F$ bond is weaker than the $Cl-Cl$ and $Br-Br$ bonds. The correct order of bond dissociation energy is $Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt F_2 \gt I_2$.

Thus, the order $F_2 \gt Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt I_2$ for bond dissociation energy is incorrect.

Answer: $F_2 \gt Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt I_2$ [Bond Dissociation Energy]

questions.solution: Phosphorus acid $\left(\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_3\right)$ is a diprotic acid. If forms two series of salts such as $\mathrm{NaH}_2 \mathrm{PO}_3$ and $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{HPO}_3$ but none of the type $\mathrm{NaPO}_3$ with $\mathrm{NaOH}$. Its structure is as

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given are $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_2, \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_3, \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_4$ and $\mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$. Which of the above oxacids results into two series of salts?
questions.solution:
The number of series of salts formed by an oxoacid is equal to its basicity, which corresponds to the number of ionizable hydrogen atoms attached to oxygen atoms (P-OH groups).

For $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_2$ (hypophosphorous acid), the structure is $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{P(O)OH}$. It has only one P-OH group, so it is monobasic and forms one series of salts.

For $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_3$ (phosphorous acid), the structure is $\mathrm{HP(O)(OH)}_2$. It has two P-OH groups, so it is dibasic and forms two series of salts (acid salts and normal salts).

For $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4$ (phosphoric acid), the structure is $\mathrm{OP(OH)}_3$. It has three P-OH groups, so it is tribasic and forms three series of salts.

For $\mathrm{H}_4\mathrm{P}_2\mathrm{O}_7$ (pyrophosphoric acid), the structure is $\mathrm{(HO)}_2\mathrm{P(O)OP(O)(OH)}_2$. It has four P-OH groups, so it is tetrabasic and forms four series of salts.

Therefore, $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_3$ results in two series of salts.

Answer: $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following will not liberate nitrogen on reaction with nitrous acid?
questions.solution:
Nitrous acid ($HNO_{2}$) reacts with primary aliphatic amines ($R-NH_{2}$) to form unstable diazonium salts, which decompose to evolve nitrogen gas ($N_{2}$) and form alcohols. Ethylamine ($CH_{3}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), methylamine ($CH_{3}NH_{2}$), and 2-aminopropane ($(CH_{3})_{2}CHNH_{2}$) are all primary aliphatic amines and will liberate nitrogen gas.

Dimethylamine ($(CH_{3})_{2}NH$) is a secondary aliphatic amine. Secondary amines react with nitrous acid to form N-nitrosamines, which are yellow oily compounds. The reaction is: $(CH_{3})_{2}NH + HNO_{2} \rightarrow (CH_{3})_{2}N-N=O + H_{2}O$. No nitrogen gas is evolved in this reaction.

Answer: dimethylamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the chemical reaction, $\mathrm{N}_{2}+3 \mathrm{H}_{2} \rightleftarrows 2 \mathrm{NH}_{3}$ at equilibrium point.
options: equal volumes of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ are reacting.
equal manes of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ are reacting.
the same amount of ammonia is formed, as it is decomposed into $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$.
questions.solution:
The chemical reaction $\mathrm{N}_{2} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2} \rightleftarrows 2\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ represents a reversible process at equilibrium.

At equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction (formation of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$) is equal to the rate of the backward reaction (decomposition of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ into $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$).

This implies that the amount of ammonia being formed per unit time is exactly equal to the amount of ammonia being decomposed per unit time, maintaining constant concentrations of all species involved.

Therefore, the condition at equilibrium is that the rate of formation of ammonia equals the rate of its decomposition.

Answer: the same amount of ammonia is formed, as it is decomposed into $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is an example of step growth polymerisation?
questions.solution:
Step growth polymerization, also known as condensation polymerization, involves the reaction of bifunctional or polyfunctional monomers with the elimination of small molecules like water, alcohol, or ammonia. In this process, the polymer chain grows by the reaction of any two species present in the mixture.

Nylon 6,6 is formed by the condensation reaction between hexamethylenediamine ($H_{2}N(CH_{2})_{6}NH_{2}$) and adipic acid ($HOOC(CH_{2})_{4}COOH$). This reaction proceeds with the elimination of water molecules, which is a characteristic feature of step growth polymerization.

In contrast, Buna-S, Neoprene, and Teflon are formed via chain growth polymerization (addition polymerization), where the reaction proceeds through the addition of monomer units to an active center (free radical or ionic) without the elimination of small molecules.

Answer: Nylon 6,6

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: x moles of $K_2$Cr_2$O_7$ oxidises 1 mole of ferrous oxalate, in acidic medium. Hence 'x' is:
questions.solution:
In acidic medium, potassium dichromate acts as an oxidizing agent and its n-factor is $6$.

$Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_2O$

Ferrous oxalate ($FeC_2O_4$) undergoes oxidation where both $Fe^{2+}$ and $C_2O_4^{2-}$ are oxidized.

$Fe^{2+} \rightarrow Fe^{3+} + e^-$
$C_2O_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2CO_2 + 2e^-$

Total electrons lost per mole of $FeC_2O_4$ is $1 + 2 = 3$. Thus, the n-factor of $FeC_2O_4$ is $3$.

Using the law of equivalence:
Equivalents of $K_2Cr_2O_7$ = Equivalents of $FeC_2O_4$

$x \times 6 = 1 \times 3$

$x = \dfrac{3}{6} = 0.5$

Answer: $0.5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the redox reaction, taking place in acidic medium:
$\text{X}\ \text{MnO}_4^-\ (aq) + \text{Y}\ \text{SO}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{+2}(aq) + \text{HSO}_4^-\ (aq)$,
the ratio of X:Y in a stoichiometrically balanced equation will be
questions.solution:
The given redox reaction can be balanced by splitting it into two half-reactions.

Reduction half-reaction:
$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{+2} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Oxidation half-reaction:
$\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{HSO}_4^- + 3\text{H}^+ + 2e^-$

To equalize the number of electrons transferred, multiply the reduction half-reaction by $2$ and the oxidation half-reaction by $5$:

$2\text{MnO}_4^- + 16\text{H}^+ + 10e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{+2} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$
$5\text{SO}_2 + 10\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 5\text{HSO}_4^- + 15\text{H}^+ + 10e^-$

Adding the two balanced half-reactions, we get the overall balanced equation:
$2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{SO}_2 + \text{H}^+ + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{+2} + 5\text{HSO}_4^-$

Comparing this with the given equation $\text{X}\ \text{MnO}_4^- + \text{Y}\ \text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \dots$, we find:
$\text{X} = 2$
$\text{Y} = 5$

Therefore, the ratio of $\text{X}:\text{Y}$ is $2:5$.

Answer: $2:5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
