questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the same point, two stones A and B are thrown simultaneously, A is thrown up vertically with a velocity of $10\ ms^{-1}$ and B is thrown up with the same velocity at $30^\circ$ with the horizontal. The separation between the balls at 2 s is
questions.solution:
Let the point of projection be the origin $(0,0)$.

Position vector of stone A at time $t$ is:

$\vec{r}_A = (10t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2)\hat{j}$

Position vector of stone B at time $t$ is:

$\vec{r}_B = (10\cos 30^\circ t)\hat{i} + (10\sin 30^\circ t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2)\hat{j}$

$\vec{r}_B = 5\sqrt{3}t\hat{i} + (5t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2)\hat{j}$

The relative position vector of A with respect to B is:

$\vec{r}_{AB} = \vec{r}_A - \vec{r}_B = -5\sqrt{3}t\hat{i} + 5t\hat{j}$

The separation between the stones is the magnitude of $\vec{r}_{AB}$:

$|\vec{r}_{AB}| = \sqrt{(-5\sqrt{3}t)^2 + (5t)^2}$

$|\vec{r}_{AB}| = \sqrt{75t^2 + 25t^2} = \sqrt{100t^2} = 10t$

At $t = 2\text{ s}$, the separation is:

$d = 10 \times 2 = 20\text{ m}$

Answer: $20\ \text{m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a projectile, the square of its horizontal range is equal to 8 times the square of the maximum height it reached. What is the angle of projection of the projectile?
questions.solution:
The horizontal range $R$ of a projectile is given by $R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g} = \dfrac{2u^2 \sin\theta \cos\theta}{g}$.

The maximum height $H$ of a projectile is given by $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$.

The problem states that $R^2 = 8H^2$. Substituting the expressions for $R$ and $H$:

$\left( \dfrac{2u^2 \sin\theta \cos\theta}{g} \right)^2 = 8 \left( \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} \right)^2$

$\dfrac{4u^4 \sin^2\theta \cos^2\theta}{g^2} = 8 \left( \dfrac{u^4 \sin^4\theta}{4g^2} \right)$

$\dfrac{4u^4 \sin^2\theta \cos^2\theta}{g^2} = \dfrac{2u^4 \sin^4\theta}{g^2}$

Dividing both sides by $\dfrac{2u^4 \sin^2\theta}{g^2}$ (assuming $\sin\theta \neq 0$):

$2 \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta$

$\tan^2\theta = 2$

$\tan\theta = \sqrt{2}$

$\theta = \tan^{-1}(\sqrt{2})$

Answer: $\theta=\tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2})$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Rain is falling vertically downwards at a velocity $9 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. And wind starts blowing at a speed of $4 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ in the west to east direction. In which direction should the girl hold her umbrella to protect herself from the rain?
questions.solution:
Let the velocity of rain be $\vec{v}_{r} = -9 \hat{j} \text{ ms}^{-1}$, where $\hat{j}$ is the unit vector in the upward vertical direction.

The velocity of the wind is $\vec{v}_{w} = 4 \hat{i} \text{ ms}^{-1}$, where $\hat{i}$ is the unit vector in the west to east direction.

The velocity of the rain with respect to the girl (who is assumed to be stationary) is $\vec{v}_{rg} = \vec{v}_{r} - \vec{v}_{w} = -4 \hat{i} - 9 \hat{j} \text{ ms}^{-1}$.

To protect herself from the rain, the girl must hold the umbrella in the direction of the relative velocity of the rain, which is $\vec{v}_{rg} = -4 \hat{i} - 9 \hat{j}$.

The angle $\theta$ that the umbrella makes with the vertical is given by $\tan \theta = \dfrac{|v_{x}|}{|v_{y}|} = \dfrac{4}{9}$.

Calculating the value, $\tan \theta = 0.444... \approx 0.44$.

Since the horizontal component of the relative velocity is $-4 \hat{i}$ (directed towards the west), the girl must tilt the umbrella towards the west to counter the rain coming from the east.

Answer: $\theta=\tan ^{-1}(0.44)$ with the vertical towards west

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A gun is used to fire a bullet at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ and at $60^{\circ}$ respectively. The ratios of heights and Ranges reached by the bullet are
questions.solution:
Maximum height: $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$

$H_1 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 30°}{2g} = \dfrac{u^2}{8g}$, $\quad H_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 60°}{2g} = \dfrac{3u^2}{8g}$

$H_1 : H_2 = 1 : 3$

Range: $R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$

$R_1 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin 60°}{g}$, $\quad R_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin 120°}{g}$

Since $\sin 60° = \sin 120°$, $R_1 = R_2 \Rightarrow R_1 : R_2 = 1 : 1$

Ratio of heights : ranges $= 1:3,\ 1:1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boy is running along a straight horizontal road with a constant speed $5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. While running he throws a stone with a velocity $30 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ at an angle $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. Then the time of flight of the stone is: (Given $g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ )
questions.solution:
The velocity of the stone is given with respect to the boy. Let the velocity of the boy be $\vec{v}_b = 5 \hat{i} \text{ ms}^{-1}$. The velocity of the stone with respect to the boy is $\vec{v}_{s/b} = 30 \cos 60^{\circ} \hat{i} + 30 \sin 60^{\circ} \hat{j} \text{ ms}^{-1}$.

The velocity of the stone with respect to the ground is $\vec{v}_s = \vec{v}_{s/b} + \vec{v}_b = (30 \times 0.5 + 5) \hat{i} + (30 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \hat{j} \text{ ms}^{-1} = 20 \hat{i} + 15\sqrt{3} \hat{j} \text{ ms}^{-1}$.

The time of flight $T$ for a projectile depends only on the vertical component of the initial velocity $u_y$ and the acceleration due to gravity $g$.

$T = \dfrac{2 u_y}{g} = \dfrac{2 \times 15\sqrt{3}}{10} = \dfrac{30\sqrt{3}}{10} = 3\sqrt{3} \text{ s}$.

Answer: $3 \sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three identical conducting balls A, B and C, each of mass m, are thrown upward at an angle $\Theta$ to the horizontal with an initial speed $v$ in a region of space that has a uniform electric field $E$ downward along with the gravitational field $g$. A is positively charged, B is uncharged and C is negatively charged. Rank the ranges R of these three balls in increasing order.
questions.solution:
The range $R$ of a projectile launched with initial speed $v$ at an angle $\Theta$ is given by $R = \dfrac{v^2 \sin(2\Theta)}{g_{eff}}$, where $g_{eff}$ is the effective acceleration acting on the particle in the downward direction.

For ball B (uncharged), the only force acting is gravity, so $g_{eff, B} = g$.

For ball A (positively charged), the electric force $qE$ acts in the same direction as gravity (downward), so the effective acceleration is $g_{eff, A} = g + \dfrac{qE}{m}$. Since $g_{eff, A} \gt g$, the range $R_A$ is smaller than $R_B$.

For ball C (negatively charged), the electric force $qE$ acts in the opposite direction to gravity (upward), so the effective acceleration is $g_{eff, C} = g - \dfrac{qE}{m}$. Since $g_{eff, C} \lt g$, the range $R_C$ is larger than $R_B$.

Comparing the effective accelerations, $g_{eff, A} \gt g_{eff, B} \gt g_{eff, C}$.

Since the range is inversely proportional to the effective acceleration, we have $R_A \lt R_B \lt R_C$.

Answer: $R_A \lt R_B \lt R_C$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A piece of marble is projected from Earth's surface with velocity of $19.6 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ at $45^{\circ}$. After 2 s , its velocity makes an angle $\alpha$ with horizontal, where $\alpha$ is
questions.solution: $u_x=19.6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $u_y=19.6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. After 2 s , vertical component of velocity $v_y$ will become zero. So, particle is at its highest point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two balls are thrown horizontally, one from the window of first floor which is $3 \mathrm{~m}$ high from the ground and second from the second floor which is $6 \mathrm{~m}$ high from the ground, of a multi storey building, with the same speed of $6 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. Calculate the distance that will separate the two balls when they hit the ground.
questions.solution:
The time taken for a ball thrown horizontally from a height $h$ to reach the ground is given by $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

For the first ball thrown from height $h_1 = 3$ m:
$t_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 3}{9.8}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{6}{9.8}} \approx 0.7825$ s.

The horizontal distance covered by the first ball is $x_1 = v \times t_1 = 6 \times 0.7825 = 4.695$ m.

For the second ball thrown from height $h_2 = 6$ m:
$t_2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 6}{9.8}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{12}{9.8}} \approx 1.1066$ s.

The horizontal distance covered by the second ball is $x_2 = v \times t_2 = 6 \times 1.1066 = 6.6396$ m.

The distance separating the two balls when they hit the ground is the difference in their horizontal ranges:
$\Delta x = x_2 - x_1 = 6.6396 - 4.695 = 1.9446$ m.

Rounding to two decimal places, the distance is $1.94$ m.

Answer: 1.94 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cricketer of height $2.5 \mathrm{~m}$ throws a ball at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal such that it is received by another cricketer of same height standing at a distance of $50 \mathrm{~m}$ from the first one. The maximum height attained by the ball is ($\tan 30^{\circ}=0.577$)
questions.solution:
The height of both cricketers is $h = 2.5 \text{ m}$. Since the ball is thrown and received at the same height, the vertical displacement is zero. The horizontal range $R$ is given by $R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g}$.

Given $R = 50 \text{ m}$ and $\theta = 30^{\circ}$, we have $50 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(60^{\circ})}{g} = \dfrac{u^2 \sqrt{3}}{2g}$.

Thus, $\dfrac{u^2}{g} = \dfrac{100}{\sqrt{3}}$.

The maximum height $H$ attained by the projectile above the point of projection is given by $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$.

Substituting the value of $\dfrac{u^2}{g}$:

$H = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left( \dfrac{u^2}{g} \right) \times \sin^2(30^{\circ}) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{100}{\sqrt{3}} \times \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^2 = \dfrac{100}{8\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{12.5}{1.732} \approx 7.216 \text{ m}$.

The total maximum height from the ground is $H_{total} = h + H = 2.5 + 7.216 = 9.716 \text{ m}$.

Rounding to the nearest value provided in the options, we get $9.7 \text{ m}$.

Answer: 9.7 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is moving in a circular path of radius $5 \mathrm{~m}$. If tangential acceleration at any instant is $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ and the net acceleration makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the centripetal acceleration, then, the instantaneous speed is
questions.solution:
The tangential acceleration is given as $a_t = 10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$.

The centripetal acceleration is given by $a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{r}$, where $v$ is the instantaneous speed and $r = 5 \mathrm{~m}$. Thus, $a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{5}$.

The net acceleration $\vec{a}$ is the vector sum of the tangential acceleration $\vec{a}_t$ and the centripetal acceleration $\vec{a}_c$. Since $\vec{a}_t$ and $\vec{a}_c$ are perpendicular, the angle $\theta$ between the net acceleration $\vec{a}$ and the centripetal acceleration $\vec{a}_c$ is given by $\tan \theta = \dfrac{a_t}{a_c}$.

Given $\theta = 30^{\circ}$, we have $\tan 30^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

Substituting the values, $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{10}{v^2 / 5} = \dfrac{50}{v^2}$.

Therefore, $v^2 = 50 \sqrt{3}$.

Calculating the value, $v^2 = 50 \times 1.732 = 86.6$.

$v = \sqrt{86.6} \approx 9.3 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$.

Answer: $9.3 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body is moving along a circular path of radius '$r$' with a frequency of revolution numerically equal to the radius of the circular path. What is the acceleration of the body if radius of the path is $\left(\dfrac{5}{\pi}\right) m$ ?
questions.solution:
The acceleration of a body moving in a circular path is the centripetal acceleration, given by $a = \omega^2 r$.

The angular velocity $\omega$ is related to the frequency $f$ by the formula $\omega = 2 \pi f$.

Given that the frequency $f$ is numerically equal to the radius $r$, we have $f = r$.

Substituting $f = r$ into the expression for $\omega$, we get $\omega = 2 \pi r$.

The acceleration $a$ becomes $a = (2 \pi r)^2 r = 4 \pi^2 r^3$.

Given the radius $r = \dfrac{5}{\pi}$ m, we substitute this value into the expression for $a$:

$a = 4 \pi^2 \left( \dfrac{5}{\pi} \right)^3$

$a = 4 \pi^2 \left( \dfrac{125}{\pi^3} \right)$

$a = \dfrac{4 \times 125}{\pi} = \dfrac{500}{\pi} \text{ ms}^{-2}$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{500}{\pi}\right) \mathrm{ms}^{-2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metal ball of $20 \mathrm{~g}$ is projected at an angle $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal with an initial velocity $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. If the mass and angle of projection are doubled keeping the initial velocity the same, the ratio of the maximum height attained in the former to the latter case is :
questions.solution:
The maximum height $H$ attained by a projectile is given by the formula $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$, where $u$ is the initial velocity, $\theta$ is the angle of projection, and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity.

In the first case, $u_1 = 10 \text{ ms}^{-1}$ and $\theta_1 = 30^{\circ}$. The maximum height is $H_1 = \dfrac{u_1^2 \sin^2(30^{\circ})}{2g} = \dfrac{10^2 \times (1/2)^2}{2g} = \dfrac{100 \times 1/4}{2g} = \dfrac{25}{2g}$.

In the second case, the mass is doubled (which does not affect the height), the velocity remains $u_2 = 10 \text{ ms}^{-1}$, and the angle is doubled, so $\theta_2 = 2 \times 30^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$. The maximum height is $H_2 = \dfrac{u_2^2 \sin^2(60^{\circ})}{2g} = \dfrac{10^2 \times (\sqrt{3}/2)^2}{2g} = \dfrac{100 \times 3/4}{2g} = \dfrac{75}{2g}$.

The ratio of the maximum height in the former case to the latter case is $\dfrac{H_1}{H_2} = \dfrac{25/2g}{75/2g} = \dfrac{25}{75} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Answer: 1 : 3

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One end of the string of length $l$ is connected to a particle of mass $m$ and the other end is connected to a small peg on a smooth horizontal table. If the particle moves in circle with speed $v$, the net force on the particle (directed towards centre) will be ( $T$ represents the tension in the string)
questions.solution:
Consider the string of length $l$ connected to a particle as shown in the figure
Speed of the particle is $v$. As, the particle is in uniform circular motion, the net force on the particle must be equal to centripetal force which is provided by the tension $(T)$. $\begin{aligned} \therefore \text { Net force } & =\text { Centripetal force } \\ & =\text { Tension in string } \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{m v^2}{l} & =T \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A hockey player hits the ball at an angle of $37^{\circ}$ from the horizontal with an initial speed of $40 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ (a right angled triangle with one of the angle is $37^{\circ}$ and their sides in the ratio of $6: 8: 10$). Assume that the ball is in a vertical plane. The time at which the ball reaches the highest point of its path is
questions.solution:
The initial velocity of the ball is $u = 40 \text{ m/s}$ and the angle of projection is $\theta = 37^{\circ}$.

The vertical component of the initial velocity is given by $u_y = u \sin \theta$.

Given the triangle with sides in ratio $3:4:5$ (which is equivalent to $6:8:10$), $\sin 37^{\circ} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Substituting the values, $u_y = 40 \times \dfrac{3}{5} = 8 \times 3 = 24 \text{ m/s}$.

At the highest point of the trajectory, the vertical component of the velocity becomes zero, $v_y = 0$.

Using the equation of motion $v_y = u_y - gt$, where $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$ is the acceleration due to gravity:

$0 = 24 - 10t$

$10t = 24$

$t = 2.4 \text{ s}$.

Answer: 2.4 s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is projected horizontally with a velocity of $5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ from the top of a building $19.6 \mathrm{~m}$ high. How long will the ball take to hit the ground?
questions.solution:
The motion of the ball in the vertical direction is governed by the equation of motion under constant acceleration due to gravity $g = 9.8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$.

The vertical displacement $h$ is given by $h = u_y t + \dfrac{1}{2} g t^2$, where $u_y$ is the initial vertical velocity.

Since the ball is projected horizontally, the initial vertical velocity $u_y = 0$.

Substituting the given values $h = 19.6 \mathrm{~m}$ and $g = 9.8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ into the equation:

$19.6 = 0 \times t + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times t^2$

$19.6 = 4.9 t^2$

$t^2 = \dfrac{19.6}{4.9}$

$t^2 = 4$

$t = 2 \mathrm{~s}$

Answer: $2 \mathrm{~s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two guns $P$ and $Q$ can fire bullets at speeds $2 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{s}$ and $4 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{s}$, respectively. From a point on a horizontal ground, they are fired in all possible directions. The ratio of maximum or areas covered by the bullets fired by the two guns, on the ground is
questions.solution:
The maximum horizontal range $R$ of a projectile fired with speed $v$ is given by the formula $R = \dfrac{v^2}{g}$, where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity.

The bullets are fired in all possible directions, so the area covered on the ground is a circle with radius $R$. The area $A$ is given by $A = \pi R^2 = \pi \left( \dfrac{v^2}{g} \right)^2 = \dfrac{\pi v^4}{g^2}$.

For gun $P$, the speed is $v_P = 2 \text{ km/s}$. The area covered is $A_P = \dfrac{\pi (2)^4}{g^2} = \dfrac{16\pi}{g^2}$.

For gun $Q$, the speed is $v_Q = 4 \text{ km/s}$. The area covered is $A_Q = \dfrac{\pi (4)^4}{g^2} = \dfrac{256\pi}{g^2}$.

The ratio of the areas covered is $\dfrac{A_P}{A_Q} = \dfrac{16\pi / g^2}{256\pi / g^2} = \dfrac{16}{256} = \dfrac{1}{16}$.

Answer: $1: 16$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angle of projection with the horizontal in terms of maximum height attained and horizontal range is given by
questions.solution:
The maximum height $H$ attained by a projectile is given by $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$.

The horizontal range $R$ of the projectile is given by $R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g} = \dfrac{2u^2 \sin \theta \cos \theta}{g}$.

Dividing the expression for $H$ by the expression for $R$, we get:

$\dfrac{H}{R} = \dfrac{\dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}}{\dfrac{2u^2 \sin \theta \cos \theta}{g}}$

$\dfrac{H}{R} = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g} \times \dfrac{g}{2u^2 \sin \theta \cos \theta}$

$\dfrac{H}{R} = \dfrac{\sin \theta}{4 \cos \theta} = \dfrac{1}{4} \tan \theta$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $\tan \theta$:

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{4H}{R}$

Therefore, the angle of projection $\theta$ is given by:

$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4H}{R}\right)$

Answer: $\tan ^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4 H}{R}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body is projected vertically upwards. The times corresponding to height $h$, while ascending and while descending are $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$, respectively. Then, the velocity of projection is ( $g$ is acceleration due to gravity)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the top of a tower, two stones whose masses are in the ratio $1: 2$ are thrown-one straight up with an initial speed $u$ and the second straight down with the same speed $u$. Then, neglecting air resistance
options: the heavier stone hits the ground with a higher speed
the lighter stone hits the ground with a higher speed
Both the stones will have the same speed when they hit the ground
the speed can't be determined with the given data
questions.solution:
The first stone move up to some height and then its velocity becomes zero. Now, it move downward and at the level of top of tower, it acquires the same initial velocity $u$ and gravitational acceleration $g$ in downward direction.
The second stone is moving with the same speed $u$ and with downward acceleration $g$. So, both will have same final velocity when they reach the bottom and hit the ground.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is moving eastward with a velocity $5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. In $10 \mathrm{~s}$ the velocity changes to $5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ northwards. The average acceleration in this time is
questions.solution:
Given, $u=5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$, Eastwards 
$v=5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$, Northwards
and $\Delta t=10 \mathrm{~s}$
Change in velocity $|\Delta v|=\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}$
=\sqrt{5^{2}+5^{2}}=5 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}

Direction of $\Delta v$,

\tan \theta=\frac{v}{u}=\frac{-5}{5}=-1

(taking eastward direction positive)

\Rightarrow \quad \theta=135^{\circ}

$\therefore$ Average acceleration, 
$a_{\text {avg }}=\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}=\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{10}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$, towards North-West

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is projected at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal with a momentum $p$. At the highest point its momentum is
questions.solution:
Let $m$ be the mass of particle and $u$ be its initial velocity, then Initial momentum, $p=m u \quad \text{...(i)}$ At highest point,

$\begin{aligned} v_{x} &=u \cos \theta=u \cos 30^{\circ} \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} u \\ v_{y} &=0 \end{aligned}\therefore$ Momentum at highest point is $\begin{array}{rlr}p^{\prime}=m v_{x} & =m u\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) & \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} p \quad \text { [using Eq. (i)] }\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The main function of cadmium used in the nuclear reactor is:
options: To capture the slow neutron produced in the nuclear reactor
It slows down the fast moving secondary neutrons produced during the nuclear fission
It gives energy to the secondary neutrons produced in the nuclear fission
It removes the heat produced at the core of the reactor
questions.solution:
In a nuclear reactor, cadmium rods are used as control rods.

The primary function of control rods is to absorb or capture the slow neutrons produced during the nuclear fission reaction, thereby controlling the rate of the chain reaction.

Moderators (like heavy water or graphite) are used to slow down fast-moving neutrons, while coolants (like water or liquid sodium) are used to remove the heat produced at the core.

Answer: To capture the slow neutron produced in the nuclear reactor

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The atomic mass of an element ${}_{10}X^{20}$ is 19.98170 amu. The binding energy per nucleon of that element is:
[given mass of neutron = 1.00867 amu and mass of proton = 1.00783 amu and 1amu = 931 MeV]
questions.solution:
Number of protons, $Z = 10$

Number of neutrons, $A - Z = 20 - 10 = 10$

Total mass of nucleons $= 10 m_p + 10 m_n$

Total mass of nucleons $= 10(1.00783) + 10(1.00867) = 10.0783 + 10.0867 = 20.1650$ amu

Mass defect, $\Delta m = \text{Mass of nucleons} - \text{Mass of nucleus}$

$\Delta m = 20.1650 - 19.98170 = 0.1833$ amu

Total binding energy, $BE = \Delta m \times 931$ MeV

$BE = 0.1833 \times 931 = 170.6523$ MeV

Binding energy per nucleon $= \dfrac{BE}{A} = \dfrac{170.6523}{20} = 8.5326$ MeV/nucleon $\approx 8.533$ MeV/nucleon

Answer: $8.533$ MeV / nucleon

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the ratio of the nuclear radii of two atoms is 2:3 then the ratio of their mass numbers is:
questions.solution:
The nuclear radius $R$ is related to the mass number $A$ by the empirical formula:

$R = R_0 A^{1/3}$

where $R_0$ is a constant.

The ratio of the nuclear radii of two atoms is given by:

$\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \left(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}\right)^{1/3}$

Given $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{2}{3}$, substituting this value:

$\dfrac{2}{3} = \left(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}\right)^{1/3}$

Cubing both sides:

$\dfrac{A_1}{A_2} = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^3 = \dfrac{8}{27}$

The ratio of their mass numbers is $8:27$.

Answer: $8:27$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two deuterons are fused to form one alpha particle. If binding energy per nucleon of deuterium is 1.05 MeV and that of alpha particle is 7 MeV, what is the energy released in the formation of one alpha particle from the fusing of two deuterons?
questions.solution:
The fusion reaction is given by:

$2\ ^{2}_{1}\text{H} \rightarrow\ ^{4}_{2}\text{He}$

Total binding energy of two deuterons = $2 \times (2 \times 1.05) = 4.2\ \text{MeV}$

Total binding energy of one alpha particle = $4 \times 7 = 28\ \text{MeV}$

Energy released = Total binding energy of products - Total binding energy of reactants

Energy released = $28 - 4.2 = 23.8\ \text{MeV}$

Answer: $23.8\ \text{MeV}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A nucleus of uranium-235 absorbs a slow neutron and undergoes nuclear fission according to the reaction: ${}^{235}_{92}U + {}^{1}_{0}n \rightarrow {}^{141}_{56}Ba + {}^{92}_{36}Kr + 3{}^{1}_{0}n + Q$
If the average energy released per fission is 202 MeV, the energy released when 2.35 g of $U^{235}$ undergoes complete fission is approximately;
[Given $1eV = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ J$, Avogadro number $= 6.02 \times 10^{23}$]
questions.solution:
Number of moles of $U^{235} = \dfrac{2.35}{235} = 0.01$ mol

Number of atoms of $U^{235} = 0.01 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 6.02 \times 10^{21}$

Energy released per fission $= 202 \text{ MeV} = 202 \times 10^6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J} = 3.232 \times 10^{-11}\text{ J}$

Total energy released $= 6.02 \times 10^{21} \times 3.232 \times 10^{-11}\text{ J}$

Total energy released $= 19.456 \times 10^{10}\text{ J}$

Answer: $19.45 \times 10^{10}\ J$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A mercury-198 nucleus is bombarded by a neutron, which causes a nuclear reaction
${}^{1}_{0}n + {}^{198}_{80}Hg \longrightarrow {}^{197}_{79}Au + X$
What is the unknown product particle X?
questions.solution:
Let the unknown particle $X$ be represented as ${}^{A}_{Z}X$.

Applying the principle of conservation of mass number:
$1 + 198 = 197 + A$
$199 = 197 + A$
$A = 2$

Applying the principle of conservation of atomic number:
$0 + 80 = 79 + Z$
$80 = 79 + Z$
$Z = 1$

The particle with mass number $A = 2$ and atomic number $Z = 1$ is ${}^{2}_{1}H$, which is a deuteron.

Answer: Deuteron

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a nitrogen-14 nucleus is bombarded by a deuteron, the products formed are:
options: Nitrogen-15 nucleus and an alpha particle
Nitrogen-15 nucleus and a beta particle
Carbon-12 nucleus and an alpha particle
Carbon- 12 nucleus and a beta particle
questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction: $^{14}_7N + ^2_1H \to ^A_ZX + ^4_2He$

Conservation of mass number: $14 + 2 = A + 4 \Rightarrow A = 12$

Conservation of atomic number: $7 + 1 = Z + 2 \Rightarrow Z = 6$

$Z = 6$ corresponds to Carbon, $A = 12$ gives Carbon-12.

$^{14}_7N + ^2_1H \to ^{12}_6C + ^4_2He$

The products are Carbon-12 nucleus and an alpha particle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a deuterium-tritium fusion reaction given by ${ }_1^2 \mathrm{H}+{ }_1^3 \mathrm{H} \rightarrow{ }_2^4 \mathrm{He}+{ }_0^1 n$ the mass defect is given as 0.0188 u . The total energy released in the fusion reaction is:
questions.solution:
The energy released in a nuclear reaction is calculated using the mass defect $\Delta m$ and the conversion factor $1 \text{ u} = 931.5 \text{ MeV}/c^2$.

Given the mass defect $\Delta m = 0.0188 \text{ u}$.

The energy released $Q$ is given by $Q = \Delta m \times 931.5 \text{ MeV}/\text{u}$.

$Q = 0.0188 \times 931.5 \text{ MeV}$.

$Q \approx 17.5122 \text{ MeV}$.

Rounding to the nearest provided option, the energy released is $17.5 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 17.5 MeV

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a nuclear reaction ${ }_4^{10} \mathrm{Be}+{ }_1^1 p \rightarrow{ }_5^{10} \mathrm{~B}+{ }_0^1 n$, what is the total energy released if the binding energy of beryllium -9 is 58.2 MeV and that of boron- 10 is 64.7 MeV ?
questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction is given by ${}_{4}^{10}\text{Be} + {}_{1}^{1}\text{p} \rightarrow {}_{5}^{10}\text{B} + {}_{0}^{1}\text{n}$.

The energy released in a nuclear reaction is given by the difference in the total binding energy of the products and the reactants. $Q = \text{BE}(\text{products}) - \text{BE}(\text{reactants})$.

The binding energy of ${}_{1}^{1}\text{p}$ (proton) is $0$ MeV and the binding energy of ${}_{0}^{1}\text{n}$ (neutron) is $0$ MeV.

The binding energy of ${}_{4}^{10}\text{Be}$ is given as $58.2$ MeV and the binding energy of ${}_{5}^{10}\text{B}$ is $64.7$ MeV.

$Q = [\text{BE}({}_{5}^{10}\text{B}) + \text{BE}({}_{0}^{1}\text{n})] - [\text{BE}({}_{4}^{10}\text{Be}) + \text{BE}({}_{1}^{1}\text{p})]$

$Q = [64.7 + 0] - [58.2 + 0] = 6.5 \text{ MeV}$.

To convert the energy from MeV to Joules, we use the conversion factor $1 \text{ eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$.

$Q = 6.5 \times 10^{6} \times 1.602 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J} \approx 10.413 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J} = 1.0413 \times 10^{-12} \text{ J}$.

Rounding to the nearest value provided in the options, we get $1.04 \times 10^{-12} \text{ J}$.

Answer: $1.04 \times 10^{-12} J$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Fusion reaction is more energetic than fission reaction because
options: In the fusion reaction lighter nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus
Uncontrolled chain reaction is taking place In the fusion reaction.
The energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fusion reaction is larger than the energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fission reaction.
Fusion reaction is taking place at very high temperature
questions.solution:
The energy released in a nuclear reaction is determined by the mass defect, which is the difference between the mass of the reactants and the mass of the products. This mass defect is converted into energy according to Einstein's mass-energy equivalence relation, $E = \Delta m c^2$.

In fission, a heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei, whereas in fusion, two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus. The binding energy per nucleon curve shows that the binding energy per nucleon increases significantly when light nuclei fuse to form a medium-mass nucleus, compared to the change when a heavy nucleus undergoes fission.

Consequently, the energy released per unit mass of the fuel (the mass defect per unit mass of the reactants) is significantly higher for fusion reactions than for fission reactions. This makes fusion reactions more energetic per unit mass of the fuel involved.

Answer: The energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fusion reaction is larger than the energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fission reaction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The nucleus of oxygen atom contains 8 protons and 8 neutrons. What is the mass defect in amu?
[Given Mass of proton $=1.00727$ amu Mass of neutron $=1.00866 \mathrm{amu}$ and the mass of oxygen nucleus $=15.99053 \mathrm{amu}$.]
questions.solution:
The mass defect $\Delta m$ of a nucleus is defined as the difference between the sum of the masses of individual nucleons and the actual mass of the nucleus.

The formula for mass defect is given by:
$\Delta m = [Z \times m_p + (A - Z) \times m_n] - M_{nucleus}$

Given:
Number of protons $Z = 8$
Number of neutrons $N = A - Z = 16 - 8 = 8$
Mass of proton $m_p = 1.00727$ amu
Mass of neutron $m_n = 1.00866$ amu
Mass of oxygen nucleus $M_{nucleus} = 15.99053$ amu

Substituting the values:
$\Delta m = [8 \times 1.00727 + 8 \times 1.00866] - 15.99053$
$\Delta m = [8.05816 + 8.06928] - 15.99053$
$\Delta m = 16.12744 - 15.99053$
$\Delta m = 0.13691$ amu

Answer: 0.13691 amu

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To get 300 MW electric power for half an hour, how much mass is to be completely converted into energy?
questions.solution:
The total energy $E$ required is given by the product of power $P$ and time $t$.

$P = 300 \text{ MW} = 300 \times 10^{6} \text{ W}$

$t = 30 \text{ minutes} = 30 \times 60 \text{ seconds} = 1800 \text{ s}$

$E = P \times t = 300 \times 10^{6} \times 1800 = 540000 \times 10^{6} = 5.4 \times 10^{11} \text{ J}$

Using Einstein mass-energy equivalence relation $E = mc^{2}$, where $c = 3 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$ is the speed of light:

$m = \dfrac{E}{c^{2}} = \dfrac{5.4 \times 10^{11}}{(3 \times 10^{8})^{2}}$

$m = \dfrac{5.4 \times 10^{11}}{9 \times 10^{16}}$

$m = 0.6 \times 10^{-5} \text{ kg} = 6 \times 10^{-6} \text{ kg}$

Answer: $6 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~kg}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When ${ }^{10} \mathrm{~B}_5$ nuclei are bombarded by neutrons, one of the resultant nuclei is ${ }^7 \mathrm{Li}_3$. Then the emitted particle will be:
questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction can be represented as follows:

${}^{10}_{5}\text{B} + {}^{1}_{0}\text{n} \rightarrow {}^{7}_{3}\text{Li} + {}^{A}_{Z}\text{X}$

Applying the law of conservation of mass number (A):

$10 + 1 = 7 + A \Rightarrow 11 = 7 + A \Rightarrow A = 4$

Applying the law of conservation of atomic number (Z):

$5 + 0 = 3 + Z \Rightarrow 5 = 3 + Z \Rightarrow Z = 2$

The particle with mass number 4 and atomic number 2 is the alpha particle (${}^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ or $\alpha$).

Answer: Alpha particle

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Radium having mass number 200 and binding energy per nucleon 5.6 MeV , splits into two fragments Cadmium of mass number 112 and Hassium of mass number 108. If the binding energy per nucleon for Cadmium and Hassium is approximately 8.0 MeV , then the energy Q released per fission will be:
questions.solution:
The total binding energy of the parent nucleus (Radium) is given by the product of its mass number and its binding energy per nucleon.

Total binding energy of Radium = $200 \times 5.6 \text{ MeV} = 1120 \text{ MeV}$.

The total binding energy of the daughter nuclei (Cadmium and Hassium) is the sum of their individual binding energies.

Total binding energy of fragments = $(112 \times 8.0 \text{ MeV}) + (108 \times 8.0 \text{ MeV}) = (112 + 108) \times 8.0 \text{ MeV} = 220 \times 8.0 \text{ MeV} = 1760 \text{ MeV}$.

The energy released $Q$ in the fission process is the difference between the total binding energy of the products and the total binding energy of the reactant.

$Q = 1760 \text{ MeV} - 1120 \text{ MeV} = 640 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 640 MeV

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the mass numbers of two nuclei are in the ratio \(5: 2\) and their diameters are in ratio \(2: 6\), Then their nuclear densities will be in the ratio
questions.solution:
The nuclear radius $R$ is related to the mass number $A$ by the formula $R = R_{0} A^{1/3}$, where $R_{0}$ is a constant. The diameter $D$ is proportional to the radius, so $D \propto A^{1/3}$.

The nuclear density $\rho$ is defined as the ratio of the mass of the nucleus to its volume. The mass of a nucleus is approximately $M = A \times m_{p}$, where $m_{p}$ is the mass of a nucleon. The volume of a nucleus is $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi (R_{0} A^{1/3})^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_{0}^{3} A$.

The nuclear density is $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{A m_{p}}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_{0}^{3} A} = \dfrac{m_{p}}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_{0}^{3}}$.

Since $m_{p}$, $R_{0}$, and $\pi$ are constants, the nuclear density $\rho$ is independent of the mass number $A$. Therefore, the ratio of the nuclear densities of any two nuclei is always $1: 1$.

Answer: \(1: 1\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Select the correct statement from the following:
options: Nuclear force is the weakest force in nature
Nuclear force is a non central force
Nuclear force depends on the charge of the nucleons
Nuclear force is a long range force
questions.solution:
Nuclear forces are the strongest forces in nature, acting between nucleons within the nucleus. They are short-range forces, effective only up to distances of the order of $10^{-15}$ m (femtometers).

Nuclear forces are charge-independent, meaning they act equally between proton-proton, neutron-neutron, and proton-neutron pairs, provided the distance is the same.

Nuclear forces are non-central forces, as they do not act only along the line joining the centers of the two nucleons; they depend on the spin and orientation of the nucleons.

Answer: Nuclear force is a non central force

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the binding energy per nucleon in ${ }_3 \mathrm{Li}^7$ and ${ }_2 \mathrm{He}^4$ nuclei are respectively 5.60 MeV and 7.06 MeV, then energy of p in the reaction $p+{ }_3 L i^7 \rightarrow 2{ }_2 H e^4$ is
questions.solution:
The given nuclear reaction is $p + _{3}Li^{7} \rightarrow 2_{2}He^{4}$.

The total binding energy of the reactants is:
Binding energy of $p$ = 0 MeV (since it is a single nucleon).
Binding energy of _{3}Li^{7} = 7 \times 5.60 \text{ MeV} = 39.20 \text{ MeV}$. \\ Total binding energy of reactants = $0 + 39.20 = 39.20 \text{ MeV}$. \\ \\ The total binding energy of the products is: \\ Binding energy of $2_{2}He^{4} = 2 \times (4 \times 7.06 \text{ MeV}) = 2 \times 28.24 \text{ MeV} = 56.48 \text{ MeV}$. \\ \\ The energy released ($Q$-value) in the reaction is the difference between the total binding energy of the products and the total binding energy of the reactants: \\ $Q = (\text{Total BE of products}) - (\text{Total BE of reactants})$ \\ $Q = 56.48 \text{ MeV} - 39.20 \text{ MeV} = 17.28 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 17.28 MeV$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a nuclear fusion reaction, two nuclei, $A$ and $B$ fuse to produce a nucleus $C$, releasing an amount of energy $\Delta \mathrm{E}$ in the process. If the mass defects of the three nuclei are $\Delta M_A, \Delta M_B$ and $\Delta M_C$ respectively, then which of the following relations is true? ( $c$ is the speed of light).
questions.solution:
Energy released in fusion: $\Delta E = BE_C - (BE_A + BE_B)$

Since $BE = \Delta M \cdot c^2$:

$\Delta E = (\Delta M_C)c^2 - [(\Delta M_A)c^2 + (\Delta M_B)c^2]$

Dividing by $c^2$:

$\dfrac{\Delta E}{c^2} = \Delta M_C - \Delta M_A - \Delta M_B$

$\Delta M_A + \Delta M_B = \Delta M_C - \dfrac{\Delta E}{c^2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The nuclear forces
a. are central forces, independent of the spin of the nucleons.
b. have a short-range dominant over a distance of about a few fermi
c. are stronger being hundred times stronger than that of electromagnetic forces.
d. are independent of the nuclear charge.

Which of the above is not true?
questions.solution:
Nuclear forces are known to be non-central forces, meaning they depend on the orientation of the spins of the nucleons. Therefore, the statement that they are central forces is incorrect.

Nuclear forces have a very short range, typically effective only within a few femtometers (fermi), which makes statement b true.

Nuclear forces are the strongest fundamental forces in nature, being approximately 100 times stronger than electromagnetic forces, making statement c true.

Nuclear forces are charge-independent, meaning the force between a proton-proton, neutron-neutron, or proton-neutron pair is essentially the same, making statement d true.

Since statement a claims that nuclear forces are central and independent of spin, it is the only false statement among the given options.

Answer: a

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A nucleus with mass number 190 initially at rest emits an alpha particle. If the $\mathrm{Q}$ value of the reaction is $4.5 \mathrm{~MeV}$, the kinetic energy of the alpha particle is
questions.solution:
Let $M$ be the mass of the parent nucleus, $m_{\alpha}$ be the mass of the alpha particle, and $m_d$ be the mass of the daughter nucleus. The mass number of the parent nucleus is $A = 190$. The alpha particle has a mass number of $4$, so the daughter nucleus has a mass number of $A - 4 = 186$.

From the conservation of linear momentum, since the parent nucleus is initially at rest, the magnitude of the momentum of the alpha particle must be equal to the magnitude of the momentum of the daughter nucleus: $p_{\alpha} = p_d$.

The kinetic energy $K$ is related to momentum $p$ by $K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}$. Thus, the ratio of kinetic energies is $\dfrac{K_{\alpha}}{K_d} = \dfrac{p_{\alpha}^2 / 2m_{\alpha}}{p_d^2 / 2m_d} = \dfrac{m_d}{m_{\alpha}}$.

Using the mass numbers as an approximation for the masses, $m_{\alpha} \approx 4$ and $m_d \approx 186$. Therefore, $\dfrac{K_{\alpha}}{K_d} = \dfrac{186}{4} = 46.5$.

The total kinetic energy released is the Q-value: $K_{\alpha} + K_d = Q = 4.5 \text{ MeV}$.

Substituting $K_d = \dfrac{K_{\alpha}}{46.5}$ into the equation: $K_{\alpha} + \dfrac{K_{\alpha}}{46.5} = 4.5$.

$K_{\alpha} \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{46.5} \right) = 4.5 \Rightarrow K_{\alpha} \left( \dfrac{47.5}{46.5} \right) = 4.5$.

$K_{\alpha} = 4.5 \times \dfrac{46.5}{47.5} \approx 4.405 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 4.4 MeV

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The radius of a nucleus as measured by electron scattering is $4.8 \mathrm{~fm}$. The mass number of nucleus is most likely to be
questions.solution:
The radius of a nucleus $R$ is related to its mass number $A$ by the formula $R = R_{0} A^{1/3}$, where $R_{0} \approx 1.2 \text{ fm}$.

Given $R = 4.8 \text{ fm}$, we have $4.8 = 1.2 \times A^{1/3}$.

Dividing both sides by $1.2$, we get $A^{1/3} = \dfrac{4.8}{1.2} = 4$.

Cubing both sides, $A = 4^{3} = 64$.

Answer: 64

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $\text { If the nuclear radius of }{ }^{27} \mathrm{Al} \text { is } 3.6 \text { fermi, the nuclear radius of }{ }^{125} \mathrm{Fe} \text { is }$
questions.solution:
The nuclear radius $R$ is given by the formula $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant and $A$ is the mass number of the nucleus.

For $^{27}\mathrm{Al}$, the mass number $A_1 = 27$ and the radius $R_1 = 3.6 \text{ fermi}$.

Using the formula, $3.6 = R_0 (27)^{1/3} = R_0 \times 3$, which gives $R_0 = 1.2 \text{ fermi}$.

For $^{125}\mathrm{Fe}$, the mass number $A_2 = 125$. The radius $R_2$ is given by $R_2 = R_0 (125)^{1/3} = 1.2 \times 5 = 6.0 \text{ fermi}$.

Since $1 \text{ fermi} = 10^{-15} \text{ m}$, the radius $R_2 = 6.0 \times 10^{-15} \text{ m}$.

Answer: $6 \times 10^{-15} \mathrm{~m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The binding energy per nucleon for $\mathrm{C}^{12}$ is $7.68 \mathrm{~MeV}$ and that for $\mathrm{C}^{13}$ is $7.47 \mathrm{~MeV}$. The energy required to remove a neutron from $\mathrm{C}^{13}$ is
questions.solution:
The binding energy of a nucleus is given by $BE = A \times (BE/A)$, where $A$ is the mass number and $BE/A$ is the binding energy per nucleon.

For $\mathrm{C}^{12}$, $BE_{12} = 12 \times 7.68 \text{ MeV} = 92.16 \text{ MeV}$.

For $\mathrm{C}^{13}$, $BE_{13} = 13 \times 7.47 \text{ MeV} = 97.11 \text{ MeV}$.

The energy required to remove a neutron from $\mathrm{C}^{13}$ is the difference in binding energies: $\Delta E = BE_{13} - BE_{12} = 97.11 \text{ MeV} - 92.16 \text{ MeV} = 4.95 \text{ MeV}$.

Converting this energy to Joules using $1 \text{ MeV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$:

$\Delta E = 4.95 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J} = 7.92 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$.

Answer: $7.92 \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The closest approach of an alpha particle when it make a head on collision with a gold nucleus is $10 \times 10^{-14} \mathrm{~m}$, then the kinetic energy of the alpha particle is :
questions.solution:
The distance of closest approach $r_0$ for an alpha particle of kinetic energy $K$ colliding head-on with a nucleus of atomic number $Z$ is given by the conservation of energy:

$K = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} \dfrac{(Ze)(2e)}{r_0}$

For a gold nucleus, the atomic number $Z = 79$. The value of the Coulomb constant is $\dfrac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9 \text{ N m}^2 \text{ C}^{-2}$. The charge of an electron is $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.

Substituting the given values $r_0 = 10 \times 10^{-14} \text{ m} = 10^{-13} \text{ m}$:

$K = \dfrac{(9 \times 10^9) \times (79 \times 2) \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{10^{-13}}$

$K = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 158 \times 2.56 \times 10^{-38}}{10^{-13}}$

$K = 9 \times 158 \times 2.56 \times 10^{9 - 38 + 13}$

$K = 3640.32 \times 10^{-16} \text{ J}$

$K = 3.64032 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$

Rounding to the nearest value, we get $K = 3.64 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$.

Answer: $3.64 \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of the radii of the nucleus of two element $\mathrm{X}$ and $\mathrm{Y}$ having the mass numbers 232 and 29 is:
questions.solution:
The radius of a nucleus is given by the formula $R = R_{0} A^{1/3}$, where $R_{0}$ is a constant and $A$ is the mass number of the nucleus.

For the two elements X and Y, the ratio of their radii is given by $\dfrac{R_{X}}{R_{Y}} = \dfrac{R_{0} A_{X}^{1/3}}{R_{0} A_{Y}^{1/3}} = \left( \dfrac{A_{X}}{A_{Y}} \right)^{1/3}$.

Given $A_{X} = 232$ and $A_{Y} = 29$, we substitute these values into the ratio:

$\dfrac{R_{X}}{R_{Y}} = \left( \dfrac{232}{29} \right)^{1/3}$.

Since $232 = 29 \times 8$, we have $\dfrac{232}{29} = 8$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{R_{X}}{R_{Y}} = (8)^{1/3} = 2$.

The ratio is $2 : 1$.

Answer: 2 : 1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Find the binding energy of the tritium nucleus:
[Given: mass of $1 \mathrm{H}^3=3.01605 \mathrm{~u} ; \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{p}}=1.00782 \mathrm{~u} ; \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{n}}=1.00866 \mathrm{~u}$.]
questions.solution:
The tritium nucleus $^{3}_{1}H$ consists of 1 proton and 2 neutrons.

Mass of constituents = $m_p + 2m_n = 1.00782 + 2 \times 1.00866 = 1.00782 + 2.01732 = 3.02514 \text{ u}$.

Mass defect $\Delta m = (m_p + 2m_n) - m_{nucleus} = 3.02514 - 3.01605 = 0.00909 \text{ u}$.

Binding energy = $\Delta m \times 931.5 \text{ MeV/u} = 0.00909 \times 931.5 \approx 8.467 \text{ MeV}$.

Rounding to the nearest given option, the binding energy is approximately 8.5 MeV.

Answer: 8.5 MeV

questions.q: The mass density of a nucleus varies with mass number $A$ as
questions.solution:

$\therefore \text { Mass density, }=\frac{3 m}{4 \pi R_0^3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following statement is true when a gamma decay occurs from the nucleus of an atom?
options: Mass number is reduced by 4 and atomic number is reduced by 2
Mass number is reduced by 4 and atomic number remains the same
Mass number remains the same and atomic number increases by 1
Mass number and atomic number are not changed
questions.solution:
Gamma decay involves the emission of high-energy electromagnetic radiation, known as gamma rays, from an excited nucleus to a lower energy state.

During this process, the nucleus does not lose any protons or neutrons. Consequently, the number of protons (atomic number, $Z$) and the total number of nucleons (mass number, $A$) remain unchanged.

The transition is represented as: _{Z}^{A}X^{*} \rightarrow _{Z}^{A}X + \gamma$.

Therefore, both the mass number and the atomic number remain constant.

Answer: Mass number and atomic number are not changed$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a nuclear reaction 2 deuteron nuclei combine to form a helium nucleus. The energy released in $\mathrm{MeV}$ will be: (Given mass of deuteron $=2.01355 \mathrm{~amu}$. and mass of helium nucleus $=4.0028 \mathrm{~amu}$.
questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction is given by: $2_{1}^{2}H \rightarrow _{2}^{4}He + Q$.

The mass of the reactants is $2 \times 2.01355 \text{ amu} = 4.02710 \text{ amu}$.

The mass of the product is $4.0028 \text{ amu}$.

The mass defect $\Delta m$ is calculated as: $\Delta m = (4.02710 - 4.0028) \text{ amu} = 0.0243 \text{ amu}$.

The energy released $Q$ is given by $Q = \Delta m \times 931.5 \text{ MeV/amu}$.

$Q = 0.0243 \times 931.5 \text{ MeV} \approx 22.62545 \text{ MeV}$.

Rounding to the nearest provided option, the energy released is $22.62 \text{ MeV}$.

Answer: 22.62 MeV

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The mass number of two nuclei $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ are 27 and 125 respectively. The ratio of their radii $R_P: R_Q$ is given by:
questions.solution:
The radius $R$ of a nucleus with mass number $A$ is given by the relation $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant.

For nucleus $\mathrm{P}$, $A_P = 27$. Thus, $R_P = R_0 (27)^{1/3} = R_0 \times 3$.

For nucleus $\mathrm{Q}$, $A_Q = 125$. Thus, $R_Q = R_0 (125)^{1/3} = R_0 \times 5$.

The ratio of their radii is $\dfrac{R_P}{R_Q} = \dfrac{R_0 \times 3}{R_0 \times 5} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Therefore, the ratio $R_P : R_Q$ is $3 : 5$.

Answer: 3 : 5

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The mass density of a nucleus varies with mass number $A$ as
questions.solution:
The radius of a nucleus is given by the relation $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant and $A$ is the mass number.

The volume of the nucleus is $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi (R_0 A^{1/3})^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A$.

The mass of the nucleus is approximately $M = A \times m_p$, where $m_p$ is the mass of a nucleon.

The mass density $\rho$ is given by $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{A m_p}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A} = \dfrac{m_p}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3}$.

Since $m_p$, $R_0$, and $\pi$ are constants, the density $\rho$ is independent of the mass number $A$. Therefore, the density varies as $A^0$.

Answer: $\mathop A\limits^o $

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: During $\alpha$-decay, atomic mass of parent nuclei is
questions.solution:
An $\alpha$-particle is a helium nucleus, denoted as _{2}^{4}\text{He}$. \\ \\ In an $\alpha$-decay process, a parent nucleus _{Z}^{A}\text{X}$ emits an $\alpha$-particle to form a daughter nucleus _{Z-2}^{A-4}\text{Y}$. \\ \\ The atomic mass number $A$ of the parent nucleus is reduced by the mass number of the $\alpha$-particle, which is 4.

Therefore, the atomic mass of the parent nucleus is decreased by 4 units.

Answer: decreased by 4 units$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ba-122 has half-life of $2 \mathrm{~min}$. Experiment has to be done using $B a-122$ and it takes 10 min to set up the experiment. It initially $80 \mathrm{~g}$ at $\mathrm{Ba}-122$ was taken, how much Ba was left when experiment was started?
questions.solution:
The half-life of Ba-122 is given as $T_{1/2} = 2 \text{ min}$.

The time elapsed before the experiment starts is $t = 10 \text{ min}$.

The number of half-lives $n$ that have passed is calculated as $n = \dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}} = \dfrac{10}{2} = 5$.

The amount of substance remaining $N$ after $n$ half-lives is given by the formula $N = N_0 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^n$, where $N_0$ is the initial amount.

Given $N_0 = 80 \text{ g}$, we have $N = 80 \times \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^5$.

$N = 80 \times \dfrac{1}{32} = \dfrac{80}{32} = 2.5 \text{ g}$.

Answer: $2.5 \mathrm{~g}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the speed of light becomes $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of its present value, the energy released in a given atomic explosion would:
options: decrease by $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of its initial value
decrease by $\dfrac{4}{9}$ of its initial value
decrease by $\dfrac{5}{9}$ of its initial value
decrease by $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{9}$ of its initial value
questions.solution:
Initial energy: $E_i = \Delta mc^2$

New speed of light: $c' = \dfrac{2}{3}c$

New energy: $E_f = \Delta m \left(\dfrac{2}{3}c\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{9}\Delta mc^2 = \dfrac{4}{9}E_i$

Decrease $= E_i - E_f = E_i - \dfrac{4}{9}E_i = \dfrac{5}{9}E_i$

The energy decreases by $\dfrac{5}{9}$ of its initial value.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following technique is not used for measuring small time intervals?
questions.solution:
Time measurement techniques are classified based on the physical phenomena involved. Electronic oscillators, such as quartz crystal oscillators, are used for precise timekeeping in electronic devices. Atomic clocks utilize the vibrations of atoms, such as cesium-133, to measure time with extreme precision. The decay of elementary particles is a fundamental process used in particle physics to measure extremely short time intervals. A spring oscillator, while periodic, is subject to significant damping, friction, and environmental factors, making it unsuitable for the precise measurement of small time intervals compared to the other high-precision methods listed.

Answer: Spring oscillator

questions.q: Two radioactive materials $X_{1}$ and $X_{2}$ have decay constant $5 \lambda$ and $\lambda$, respectively. If initially they have the same number of nuclei, then the ratio of the number of nuclei of $X_{1}$ to that $X_{2}$ will be $1 / e$ after a time

questions.q: If $M$ is the atomic mass and $A$ is the mass number, packing fraction is given by
questions.solution:
Packing fraction is equal to the ratio of mass defect to total number of nucleons.
i.e. $\mathrm{PF}=\frac{\text { Mass defect }}{\text { No. of nucleons }}=\frac{M-A}{A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A count rate meter shows a count of 240 per min from a given radioactive source. One hour later the meter shows a count rate of 30 per min. The half-life of the source is
questions.solution:
Let $N$ be the amount of substance left,
$N_{0}$ be the total amount of substance.
The amount of substance left after $N$ half-life is given by $\quad \frac{N}{N_{0}}=\frac{1}{2^{n}}$
Hence, $\quad \frac{30}{240}=\frac{1}{2^{n}}$
(Since, decay rate proportional to amount of substance)

\Rightarrow \quad 2^{n}=8 \Rightarrow n=3

Number of half-life passed $=3$
Time taken for the substance to decay from 240 count rate to 30 count rate $=1 \mathrm{~h}=60 \mathrm{~min}$
\begin{aligned}
\text { Half-life } &=\frac{\text { Total time }}{\text { Number of half - life }} \\
t_{1 / 2} &=\frac{60}{3}=20 \mathrm{~min}
\end{aligned}

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Heavy water is
options: water, in which soap does not lather
compound of heavy oxygen and heavy hydrogen
questions.solution: Heavy water is compound that contains heavy hydrogen or deuterium and oxygen. Heavy water is also called deuterium oxide $\mathrm{D}_{2} \mathrm{O}$.

questions.q: The masses of two radioactive substances are same and their half-lives are 1 year and 2 years, respectively. The ratio of their activities after 6 years will be
questions.solution:
Let initial masses of two radioactive substances be $N_{0}$.
If $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$ be the half-lives of two radioactive substances,
Then, $\quad T_{1}=1$ yr
Hence, remaining mass of the first substances after

\begin{aligned}
t &=6 \mathrm{yrs} \\
N_{1} &=N_{0}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{T}}=N_{0}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{6 / 1} \\
&=\frac{N_{0}}{2^{6}} \\
\Rightarrow \quad N_{1} &=\frac{N_{0}}{64}
\end{aligned}

Similarly, remaining mass of the second substance after $t=6 y r \mathrm{~s}N_{2}=N_{0}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{T_{2}}}=N_{0}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{6 / 2}=\frac{N_{0}}{8}\Rightarrow \quad N_{2}=\frac{N_{0}}{8}\therefore \quad \frac{N_{1}}{N_{2}}=\frac{\frac{N_{0}}{\frac{64}{N_{0}}}}{8}=\frac{1}{8} \Rightarrow \frac{N_{1}}{N_{2}}=\frac{1}{8}$
Since, activity, $A=\lambda N=\frac{0.693}{T} N\Rightarrow \quad A \propto \frac{N}{T}\therefore \quad \frac{A_{1}}{A_{2}}=\frac{N_{1} T_{2}}{N_{2} T_{1}}=\frac{1}{8} \times \frac{2}{1}=\frac{1}{4}\Rightarrow \quad A_{1}: A_{2}=1: 4$

Here, initial nuclei $={ }_{92} \mathrm{U}^{235}$
Final nuclei $={ }_{82} \mathrm{P}^{2013}$
Change in mass number $=235-203=32$
Number of $\alpha$-particle emitted $=\frac{32}{4}=8\therefore$ Number of emitted $\beta$-particles

=8 \times 2-(92-82)=16-10=6

In radioactive decay, the decay rate is proportional to the amount of substance. So, for change of count rate from 240 per min to 30 per min, let $N$ be the number of half-life passed in one hour. Then,
$\frac{240}{2^{N}}=30\Rightarrow \quad 2^{N}=8\Rightarrow \quad N=3$

The number of half-lives in $50 \mathrm{~min}$,

n=\frac{t}{t_{1 / 2}}=\frac{50}{10}=5

In 5 half-lives, number of nuclei left undecayed,

$\therefore$ Number of nuclei decayed $=N_{0}-N=64-2=62$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Force constant of interatomic bond, in a certain element, is $7.1\ Nm^{-1}$. If the atom oscillates in SHM in a certain direction, what is its frequency?
Given: Mole weight of the given element is 108g and Avagadro's number $= 6.023 \times 10^{23}\ g\ mol^{-1}$
questions.solution:
Mass of a single atom is given by $m = \dfrac{M}{N_A}$

Substituting the given values:

$m = \dfrac{108 imes 10^{-3}}{6.023 imes 10^{23}} \approx 1.793 imes 10^{-25}\ kg$

The frequency of oscillation of the atom in simple harmonic motion is given by:

$ u = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

Substituting $k = 7.1\ N\ m^{-1}$ and $m = 1.793 imes 10^{-25}\ kg$:

$ u = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{7.1}{1.793 imes 10^{-25}}}$

$ u = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{39.6 imes 10^{24}}$

$ u = \dfrac{6.29 imes 10^{12}}{2\pi} \approx 1 imes 10^{12}\ s^{-1}$

Answer: $1 imes 10^{12}\ s^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object of mass 10g executes SHM along the $x$-axis with frequency of $\left(\dfrac{10}{\pi}\right)$Hz. At the point $x = 2\ cm$ the object has KE 1.2 J and PE 0.4 J. The amplitude of oscillation is
questions.solution:
Given, Kinetic Energy ($KE$) = $1.2$ J and Potential Energy ($PE$) = $0.4$ J at displacement $x = 2$ cm.

The total energy ($E$) of the object executing SHM is the sum of its kinetic and potential energies:

$E = KE + PE = 1.2 + 0.4 = 1.6$ J

In simple harmonic motion, the potential energy at a displacement $x$ and the total energy are given by:

$PE = \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 x^2$

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 A^2$

Taking the ratio of total energy to potential energy:

$\dfrac{E}{PE} = \dfrac{A^2}{x^2}$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{1.6}{0.4} = \dfrac{A^2}{2^2}$

$4 = \dfrac{A^2}{4}$

$A^2 = 16$

$A = 4$ cm

Answer: $4\ \text{cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the equations given below select the correct equation representing the displacement of a particle undergoing a periodic motion. [$y$ - displacement; a - amplitude $T$ - Period; $\omega$ - angular velocity; $t$-time]
questions.solution:
The general equation for the displacement of a particle undergoing simple harmonic motion is given by $y = a \sin(\omega t + \phi)$, where $\omega$ is the angular frequency and $t$ is the time.

The relationship between angular frequency $\omega$ and the time period $T$ is defined as $\omega = \dfrac{2 \pi}{T}$.

Substituting this expression for $\omega$ into the general displacement equation, we get $y = a \sin\left(\dfrac{2 \pi}{T} t\right)$.

Rearranging the terms inside the sine function, we obtain $y = a \sin\left(\dfrac{2 \pi t}{T}\right)$.

Answer: $y=a \sin \left[\dfrac{(2 \pi \mathrm{t})}{T}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion. The displacement of the particle from the mean position in 2 second is equal to $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ times its amplitude. What is the period of oscillation of the particle ?
questions.solution:
The displacement of a particle in simple harmonic motion is given by $x(t) = A \sin(\omega t + \phi)$. Assuming the particle starts from the mean position at $t = 0$, we have $\phi = 0$, so $x(t) = A \sin(\omega t)$.

Given that at $t = 2$ s, $x(2) = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$, we substitute these values into the equation:

$\dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}} = A \sin(2\omega)$

$\sin(2\omega) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

This implies $2\omega = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ or $2\omega = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$. Taking the simplest case for the first occurrence, $2\omega = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Since $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$, we have $2 \left( \dfrac{2\pi}{T} \right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ or $2 \left( \dfrac{2\pi}{T} \right) = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.

For $2\omega = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $\dfrac{4\pi}{T} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} \Rightarrow T = 16$ s.

For $2\omega = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$, $\dfrac{4\pi}{T} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4} \Rightarrow T = \dfrac{16}{3}$ s.

Comparing with the given options, $T = 16$ s is the correct period.

Answer: $\mathrm{T}=16 \mathrm{~s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Time period of oscillation of a mass suspended from a spring is $T$. If the spring is cut into four equal parts and the same mass is suspended from one of the parts, the fractional change in time period is
questions.solution:
The time period of a mass $m$ suspended from a spring of force constant $k$ is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$.

When a spring of force constant $k$ is cut into $n$ equal parts, the force constant of each part becomes $k' = nk$. Here, $n = 4$, so $k' = 4k$.

The new time period $T'$ for the same mass $m$ suspended from one of the parts is $T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k'}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{4k}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}} = \dfrac{T}{2}$.

The fractional change in the time period is given by $\left| \dfrac{T' - T}{T} \right| = \left| \dfrac{\dfrac{T}{2} - T}{T} \right| = \left| \dfrac{-\dfrac{T}{2}}{T} \right| = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire of negligible mass having uniform area of cross section 'A' and young modulus ' Y ' is used to suspend a point mass ' m '. The point mass executes simple harmonic motion in a vertical plane with a period ' T ', then the length of the wire is :
questions.solution:
The wire acts as a spring with a spring constant $k$ given by the formula $k = \dfrac{YA}{L}$, where $Y$ is the Young modulus, $A$ is the area of cross-section, and $L$ is the length of the wire.

The time period $T$ of a mass $m$ executing simple harmonic motion attached to a spring of constant $k$ is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$.

Squaring both sides of the equation, we get $T^2 = 4\pi^2 \dfrac{m}{k}$.

Substituting the expression for $k$ into the equation for $T^2$, we have $T^2 = 4\pi^2 \dfrac{m}{(YA/L)}$.

Rearranging the equation to solve for $L$, we get $T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2 mL}{YA}$.

Therefore, $L = \dfrac{T^2 YA}{4\pi^2 m}$.

Answer: $L=\dfrac{T^2 Y A}{4 \pi^2 m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two simple harmonic motions are represented by equations $y_1=0.5 \sin \left[200 \pi t+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right]$ and $y_1=0.5 \cos \pi t$. The phase difference of the velocity of particle 1 with respect to the velocity of particle 2 is:
questions.solution:
The first equation is $y_1 = 0.5 \sin \left(200 \pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$. The velocity $v_1$ is given by the derivative $\dfrac{dy_1}{dt} = 0.5 \times 200 \pi \cos \left(200 \pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 100 \pi \sin \left(200 \pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

The second equation is $y_2 = 0.5 \cos(\pi t) = 0.5 \sin \left(\pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. The velocity $v_2$ is given by the derivative $\dfrac{dy_2}{dt} = 0.5 \times \pi \cos \left(\pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0.5 \pi \sin \left(\pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0.5 \pi \sin(\pi t + \pi)$.

The phase of velocity $v_1$ is $\phi_1 = 200 \pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 200 \pi t + \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$.

The phase of velocity $v_2$ is $\phi_2 = \pi t + \pi$.

The phase difference $\Delta \phi = \phi_1 - \phi_2 = (200 \pi t + \dfrac{5\pi}{6}) - (\pi t + \pi) = 199 \pi t - \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

At $t=0$, the phase difference is $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{-\pi}{6}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an experiment to determine the period of a simple pendulum of length 100 cm , it is attached to different spherical bobs have uniform mass distribution. If the relative difference in the periods is found to be $5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~s}$, the difference in radii $\left|r_1-r_2\right|$ is best given by
questions.solution:
Given, $\Delta T=5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~s}$
We know that,
$\begin{array}{cc}
& T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}} \\
\Rightarrow & T \propto \sqrt{l} \\
\therefore & \Delta T=\frac{1}{2} \Delta l \\
\Rightarrow & 5 \times 10^{-4}=\frac{\left|r_1-r_2\right|}{2} \\
\Rightarrow & \left|r_1-r_2\right|=2 \times 5 \times 10^{-4}=10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}
\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body is executing SHM. When its displacements from the mean position are $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $5 \mathrm{~cm}$ it has velocity $10 \mathrm{~cms}^{-1}$ and $8 \mathrm{~cms}^{-1}$ respectively. Its periodic time $\mathrm{t}$ is
questions.solution:
The velocity $v$ of a particle executing simple harmonic motion at a displacement $x$ is given by $v = \omega \sqrt{A^2 - x^2}$, where $A$ is the amplitude and $\omega$ is the angular frequency.

For the first case, $10 = \omega \sqrt{A^2 - 4^2} \Rightarrow 100 = \omega^2 (A^2 - 16)$.

For the second case, $8 = \omega \sqrt{A^2 - 5^2} \Rightarrow 64 = \omega^2 (A^2 - 25)$.

Dividing the two equations: $\dfrac{100}{64} = \dfrac{A^2 - 16}{A^2 - 25} \Rightarrow \dfrac{25}{16} = \dfrac{A^2 - 16}{A^2 - 25}$.

Cross-multiplying: $25(A^2 - 25) = 16(A^2 - 16) \Rightarrow 25A^2 - 625 = 16A^2 - 256$.

$9A^2 = 369 \Rightarrow A^2 = 41$.

Substituting $A^2 = 41$ into the first equation: $100 = \omega^2 (41 - 16) = 25 \omega^2$.

$\omega^2 = 4 \Rightarrow \omega = 2 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

The periodic time $T$ is given by $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{2\pi}{2} = \pi \text{ sec}$.

Answer: $\pi$ sec

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle executes a simple harmonic motion of amplitude $\mathrm{A}$. The distance from the mean position at which its kinetic energy is equal to its potential energy is
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy $K$ and potential energy $U$ of a particle executing simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$ at a distance $x$ from the mean position are given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2} k(A^2 - x^2)$ and $U = \dfrac{1}{2} k x^2$, where $k$ is the force constant.

Given that the kinetic energy is equal to the potential energy, we set $K = U$:

$\dfrac{1}{2} k(A^2 - x^2) = \dfrac{1}{2} k x^2$

Simplifying the equation:

$A^2 - x^2 = x^2$

$A^2 = 2x^2$

$x^2 = \dfrac{A^2}{2}$

$x = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$

Using the value $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$, we calculate:

$x = \dfrac{A}{1.414} \approx 0.707 A$

Rounding to two decimal places, we get $x = 0.71 A$.

Answer: 0.71 A

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The phase difference between displacement and velocity of a particle in simple harmonic motion is
questions.solution:
The displacement of a particle executing SHM is
$x=A \sin \omega t\therefore$ Velocity, $v=\frac{d x}{d t}=A \omega \cos \omega t\therefore v=A \omega \sin \left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\therefore$ Phase difference, $\Delta \phi=\left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\omega t=\frac{\pi}{2} \mathrm{rad}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The phase difference between displacement and velocity of a particle in simple harmonic motion is
questions.solution:
The displacement of a particle in simple harmonic motion is given by $x(t) = A \sin(\omega t + \phi)$.

The velocity of the particle is the time derivative of displacement, $v(t) = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = A \omega \cos(\omega t + \phi)$.

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos(\theta) = \sin(\theta + \pi/2)$, the velocity can be written as $v(t) = A \omega \sin(\omega t + \phi + \pi/2)$.

Comparing the phases of displacement and velocity, the phase of displacement is $\omega t + \phi$ and the phase of velocity is $\omega t + \phi + \pi/2$.

The phase difference is $(\omega t + \phi + \pi/2) - (\omega t + \phi) = \pi/2 \text{ rad}$.

Answer: $\pi / 2 \mathrm{~rad}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: During the phenomenon of resonance
options: the amplitude of oscillation becomes large
the frequency of oscillation becomes large
the time period of oscillation becomes large
questions.solution:
Resonance occurs when the driving frequency of an external periodic force matches the natural frequency of the system.

Under this condition, the energy transfer from the driving force to the oscillator is maximized, leading to a significant increase in the amplitude of oscillation.

The frequency and time period of the oscillation are determined by the system's natural properties and do not necessarily become large; rather, the system oscillates at its natural frequency with a greatly increased amplitude.

Answer: the amplitude of oscillation becomes large

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is performing simple harmonic motion. Equation of its motion is $x=5 \sin \left(4 t-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right), x$ being the displacement from mean position. Velocity (in $\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ ) of the particle at the instant when its displacement is 3 , will be
questions.solution:
The displacement equation is given by $x = 5 \sin \left(4t - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$.

The velocity $v$ of a particle in simple harmonic motion is given by $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 5 \times 4 \cos \left(4t - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 20 \cos \left(4t - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$.

Using the identity $\cos \theta = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 \theta}$, we have $v = 20 \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 \left(4t - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)}$.

Given the displacement $x = 5 \sin \left(4t - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 3$, we find $\sin \left(4t - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Substituting this value into the velocity expression:

$v = 20 \sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^2} = 20 \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{9}{25}} = 20 \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{25}} = 20 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 16$.

Answer: 16

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The function $y=\log \omega t$ can represent
questions.solution:
The function $y = \log(\omega t)$ is defined for $\omega t \gt 0$.

A function $f(t)$ is periodic if there exists a positive constant $T$ such that $f(t + T) = f(t)$ for all $t$.

For the given function, $\log(\omega(t + T)) = \log(\omega t + \omega T) = \log(\omega t) + \log(1 + \dfrac{T}{t})$.

Since $\log(1 + \dfrac{T}{t}) \neq 0$ for any $T \gt 0$ and $t \gt 0$, the condition $f(t + T) = f(t)$ cannot be satisfied for any constant $T$.

Therefore, the function $y = \log(\omega t)$ is a non-periodic function.

Answer: non-periodic function

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Two spring of force constant $k_{1}$ and $k_{2}$ are configured as the figure given below

The angular frequency of this configuration is
questions.solution:
In the given configuration, the block of mass $m$ is connected to two springs with force constants $k_{1}$ and $k_{2}$ on either side. When the block is displaced by a small distance $x$ from its equilibrium position, one spring is compressed by $x$ and the other is stretched by $x$.

The restoring force exerted by the first spring is $F_{1} = -k_{1}x$ and the restoring force exerted by the second spring is $F_{2} = -k_{2}x$. Both forces act in the same direction, opposing the displacement.

The total restoring force $F$ acting on the block is $F = F_{1} + F_{2} = -(k_{1} + k_{2})x$.

This is the standard form of the equation for simple harmonic motion, $F = -kx_{eff}$, where the effective spring constant $k_{eff} = k_{1} + k_{2}$.

The angular frequency $\omega$ of a mass-spring system is given by $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_{eff}}{m}}$.

Substituting the value of $k_{eff}$, we get $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_{1} + k_{2}}{m}}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{k_{1}+k_{2}}{m}}$

Force constant, $k=600 \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$
Maximum speed of oscillation,
$\begin{aligned} v_{\max } &=A \omega \\ &=A \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} \quad\left[\because \omega=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}\right] \\ &=0.2 \sqrt{\frac{600}{10}}=0.2 \sqrt{60} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$
